# Python Package Installation (v1.12.0+)

Install `depictio[local]` with `uv` or `pip`, then run every service as a local process on your machine: no containers.

`depictio local up` starts the same API, worker and viewer as the [Docker Compose](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/index.md) and [Kubernetes](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/kubernetes/index.md) deployments, with MongoDB, Redis and SeaweedFS (the S3 store) run as plain processes on `127.0.0.1`. `depictio ingest` then adds your pipeline results, so you go from a results directory to its dashboard without Docker, a cluster or a shared instance.

Use it to review a template on your own results, or to try Depictio on a laptop. For a team, a demo or production, use Docker Compose or Kubernetes: a local server can later be [moved to Docker Compose](#move-to-docker-compose) with its data.

______________________________________________________________________

## Quick Start

No machine at hand?

[Open in Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/depictio/depictio?devcontainer_path=.devcontainer/try/devcontainer.json&quickstart=1) runs these steps in a GitHub cloud workspace. Its image already holds `depictio[local]`, the services and the examples, so it only starts `depictio local up`, in a terminal of the editor, and opens the viewer. Drag a results folder onto its Explorer, then run `depictio ingest` in its terminal. While the codespace is being created, **View logs** on its loading page, or **Codespaces: View Creation Log** in the command palette, shows what it is doing.

**Hands-on workshop** (v1.21.0+): [Open the workshop codespace](https://codespaces.new/depictio/depictio?devcontainer_path=.devcontainer/workshop/devcontainer.json&quickstart=1). It opens a single-user instance with an nf-core/ampliseq 2.18.0 run already ingested.

**Prerequisites**: Linux, or macOS on Apple silicon (see [Platforms](#platforms)), with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), or pip and Python 3.11 to 3.14.

### Step 1: Install

```
uv tool install "depictio[local]"
```

`uv tool install` puts the `depictio` command on your `PATH`, in an environment of its own. Prefer it to `uvx --from "depictio[local]" depictio local up`, which runs in a temporary environment and leaves no `depictio` command behind for `depictio local status` and `depictio local down`.

If you installed the former `depictio-cli` package with `uv tool install`, add `--force`: it replaces the `depictio` and `depictio-cli` commands that package installed.

```
python3 -m venv ~/.venvs/depictio
source ~/.venvs/depictio/bin/activate
pip install "depictio[local]"
```

The `depictio` command is on your `PATH` while the environment is active.

The `[local]` extra adds the server's Python dependencies, about 1.6 GB installed, from prebuilt wheels on Python 3.11 to 3.14. The package carries the viewer, already built.

The install with uv, then a first look at the `depictio` command:

From a clone of the repository

To run the code of a clone, install it in editable mode:

```
git clone https://github.com/depictio/depictio.git
cd depictio
uv tool install -e ".[local]"
```

A clone has no viewer bundle, so `depictio local up` builds it, with `pnpm install` then `pnpm run build`, when it is missing or older than its sources. That needs [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20 or later with [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/installation) (`corepack enable pnpm`); the output goes to `~/.depictio/local/logs/viewer-build.log`. A build that fails does not stop the start: the server runs with the previous bundle, or without dashboards when there is none, and `up` says so.

### Step 2: Start the server

```
depictio local up
```

The first run downloads MongoDB, Redis and SeaweedFS from conda-forge into `~/.depictio/local/env` (about 170 MB, once), seeds the Iris and Penguins example projects, and waits for them to load so that their dashboards open with data. It then opens the dashboards page in your browser, `http://127.0.0.1:8058/dashboards` unless that port was taken (see [Ports](#ports)). Later runs reuse the binaries and the data, and start in seconds.

Over SSH, or on Linux without a display, no browser opens: `up` prints the tunnel to run from your own machine, `ssh -L <port>:127.0.0.1:<port> <host>`, then the URL to open there.

The next steps above need no `--server`: when no other server is configured (no `~/.depictio/CLI.yaml`, and no `DEPICTIO_CLI_*` variable set), every [CLI](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/index.md) command reaches this server. Otherwise the summary adds `--server local`, which names this server whatever else is configured. See [Which server a command uses](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#choosing-a-server).

### Step 3: Add your results

```
depictio ingest path/to/results
```

[`depictio ingest`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#ingest-command) detects the [template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/templates/index.md) from the pipeline name and version the run recorded, and ends with links to the project and its dashboards. Pass `--template` to choose the template, and template variables with `--var`. nf-core results do not contain the samplesheet: when the template cannot find it under `input/`, pass it explicitly.

```
depictio ingest path/to/results \
  --template nf-core/rnaseq/latest \
  --var SAMPLESHEET_FILE=$PWD/samplesheet.csv
```

If the ingestion fails, the command exits with an error and the server keeps running. To ingest the same results again after a new run, add `--update-config`: it refreshes the project and keeps its dashboards as edited in the viewer (see [Refreshing a project](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#refreshing-a-project)).

Coming from v1.12.0-b1

`depictio local up` no longer ingests data. Given `--template`, `--data-root`, `--project-name` or `--var`, it prints the `depictio local up` and `depictio ingest` commands to run instead, and exits with code 2.

______________________________________________________________________

## Manage the server

`depictio local` manages the server only: data goes in with [`depictio ingest`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#ingest-command).

| Command                 | Effect                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `depictio local up`     | Start the services, print the summary and open the browser. A first run also downloads the binaries and seeds the examples                                                       |
| `depictio local open`   | Open the dashboards page of the running server in a browser, or print the SSH tunnel to use                                                                                      |
| `depictio local status` | Show each process with its port, and whether the API answers. Exits with code 1 unless every process runs and the API answers                                                    |
| `depictio local down`   | Stop every process. The data and the ports are kept for the next `up`                                                                                                            |
| `depictio local wipe`   | Stop the server and delete all its data. The downloaded binaries are kept. `--yes` skips the prompt                                                                              |
| `depictio local export` | Stop the server and copy its data into a directory that Docker Compose runs, see [Move to Docker Compose](#move-to-docker-compose). Formerly `export-compose`, which still works |

Here a first `up`, which downloads the services, then `status`, `open` and `down`:

```
depictio local status
```

```
depictio local down
```

### `up` options

| Option                               | Default                                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--examples`                         | `iris,penguins`                               | Example projects to seed on the first run of a local home: `iris`, `penguins`, `iris,penguins` or `none`                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--port`                             | the previous run's, else `8058` or a free one | Port of the API and the viewer, kept for later runs. A busy `--port` fails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--open` / `--no-open`               | `--open`                                      | Open the dashboards page in a browser                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--screenshots` / `--no-screenshots` | off                                           | Dashboard thumbnails through Playwright. Installs Chromium (about 150 MB) if needed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `--data-root-allow PATH`             |                                               | Also let the web UI read run folders under `PATH`, an existing absolute folder outside `~/.depictio/local` with no comma in its path. Repeatable. Your home folder is always allowed. See [From a run folder](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#from-a-run-folder) (v1.16.0+) |

- Examples are seeded on the first run of a local home only: `up` warns when `--examples` names one the home was created without.
- `up` on a server that is already running reuses it and prints the summary again. `--port`, `--screenshots` and `--data-root-allow` then apply only after `depictio local down`, and a warning says so. For the folders, it also warns when `up` names fewer or none: the running server keeps those it was started with.
- A second `up` on the same home while one is starting fails at once.
- Ctrl-C during startup stops what that run started, and exits with code 130. SIGTERM and SIGHUP, as when the terminal is closed, do the same, with code 128 plus the signal number.

### Upgrade

```
depictio local down
uv tool upgrade depictio            # with pip: pip install --upgrade "depictio[local]"
depictio local up
```

Stop the server first, so that it starts again on the new version. The data under `~/.depictio/local` is kept. `up` downloads the binaries again only when the new version pins other MongoDB, Redis or SeaweedFS series.

______________________________________________________________________

## How it differs from Docker Compose

Only configuration differs, and only through the usual `DEPICTIO_*` variables: every service is pointed at `127.0.0.1`.

|                      | Docker Compose                                | Python package                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MongoDB, Redis, S3   | containers                                    | `mongod` 8.0.x, `redis-server` 8.x and `weed mini` (SeaweedFS) 4.x from conda-forge, fetched by [py-rattler](https://github.com/conda/rattler) |
| API                  | 4 gunicorn workers                            | 1 uvicorn worker                                                                                                                               |
| Celery worker        | 4 processes                                   | 2 slots: `prefork` on Linux, `threads` on macOS                                                                                                |
| Viewer               | its own container, on `http://localhost:5080` | served by the API, on its port: `http://127.0.0.1:8058/dashboards`                                                                             |
| Authentication       | single-user, multi-user or public             | single-user                                                                                                                                    |
| Dashboard thumbnails | on                                            | off unless `--screenshots`                                                                                                                     |

The conda-forge packages follow the major series of the Compose images (the 8.0 series for MongoDB), so their minor versions can be newer than the images'. [`depictio local export`](#move-to-docker-compose) runs the exact MongoDB and SeaweedFS versions of the local server, so the data never moves to an older one.

### Ports

The first `up` picks its ports on `127.0.0.1`: the defaults (API `8058`, MongoDB `27018`, Redis `6379`, S3 `9000`) when they are free, any free port otherwise, so a local server runs next to a Docker stack or another local server. The ports are saved in `ports.json` and reused, so the dashboards URL stays the same. A saved port that another program has taken since moves to a free one, with a warning for the API port; a `--port` that is busy fails instead. The CLI configuration follows the ports in use. SeaweedFS also opens internal ports (master `9333`, volume `9340`, filer `8888`, admin `23646`, and their gRPC ports), picked the same way at each start.

### Files

Everything lives under `~/.depictio/local`, or the folder `DEPICTIO_LOCAL_HOME` names:

| Path                                           | Content                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `env/`                                         | MongoDB, Redis and SeaweedFS binaries                                                                                                                                    |
| `mongo/`, `redis/`, `s3/`                      | Service data, kept between runs                                                                                                                                          |
| `logs/`                                        | One log per process: `api.log`, `worker.log`, `mongo.log`, `redis.log`, `s3.log`, and `viewer-build.log` for a viewer built from a clone                                 |
| `keys/`                                        | Token signing keys                                                                                                                                                       |
| `cli/`                                         | The CLI configuration that `--server local` reads, with its admin token. `up` writes it again if it was deleted, with a new token, and revokes those of earlier rewrites |
| `backups/`                                     | Backups that [`depictio backup create`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/backup/index.md) makes on this server                       |
| `cache/`, `multiqc_prerender/`, `screenshots/` | Caches, and dashboard thumbnails                                                                                                                                         |
| `secrets.json`                                 | Generated S3 and admin passwords                                                                                                                                         |
| `ports.json`                                   | Ports kept for the next `up`                                                                                                                                             |
| `state.json`                                   | Process IDs of the running server, deleted by `down`                                                                                                                     |
| `.depictio-local-home`                         | Marks the folder as a local home: `wipe` deletes nothing in a folder without it, and `up` refuses a folder that holds other files                                        |

The local home, `keys/` and `cli/` are owner-only (`0700`); `secrets.json` and the CLI configuration file are owner-only too (`0600`).

Shared machines

The local server runs in single-user mode: no login, and whoever reaches its port acts as its admin. It listens on `127.0.0.1` only, but on a shared machine, such as an HPC login node, every other user of that machine can reach it, and the data it serves. The owner-only files do not change that. On such a machine, load only data that every user of it may see, or use [Docker Compose](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/index.md) in multi-user mode.

______________________________________________________________________

## Move to Docker Compose

A local server can be handed over to [Docker Compose](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/index.md) with its projects, dashboards and table data, for instance once a review turns into a shared instance.

```
depictio local export
cd depictio-docker && docker compose up -d
```

`export` stops the local server if it is running, so that the copy is consistent, then copies the MongoDB and SeaweedFS data and the token signing keys into the directory, `depictio-docker` by default (`--out`). Everything that can refuse the export (no local data, a directory that is not empty, no compose file to use) is checked before the server is stopped. The two never share files: `depictio local up` restarts the local server on its own data.

The directory is made owner-only (`0700`), since it holds the token signing key. It holds:

| File                           | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docker-compose.yaml`          | The compose file that matches the installed code: the clone's own file when `depictio` runs from a clone, otherwise the file of the release tag `v<version>` (betas included), downloaded from GitHub. A development build outside a clone matches no published file, and the command stops with a message |
| `docker-compose.override.yaml` | The `mongo` and `chrislusf/seaweedfs` images at the versions the local server ran, on the copied data. On Linux they run as your user, who owns the copied files                                                                                                                                           |
| `.env`                         | Single-user mode, the local server's S3 and admin credentials and, for a release, `DEPICTIO_VERSION`. Owner-only                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `data/`                        | The copied MongoDB and SeaweedFS data, and the key files                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Redis is not carried over, since it holds only cache and queues, and thumbnails are rendered again. The token in `~/.depictio/local/cli` stays valid against the Docker stack, since it was signed with the copied keys. The raw pipeline files are not copied, only the tables built from them: to ingest again, point `depictio ingest --server <file>` at the CLI configuration of the Docker stack.

______________________________________________________________________

## Platforms

| Platform                    | Status                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Linux x86_64                | Supported, tested in CI                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Linux arm64                 | Supported, tested in CI                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| macOS arm64 (Apple silicon) | Supported, tested in CI                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| macOS x86_64 (Intel)        | Not supported: `cryptography`, a server dependency, ships macOS wheels for arm64 only. Use [Docker Compose](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/index.md)                                                                                                         |
| Windows                     | Not supported, `up` refuses to start: conda-forge has no `redis-server` for Windows, and the services are managed as POSIX process groups. Use [WSL2](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/wsl/) or [Docker Compose](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/index.md) |

Python 3.11 to 3.14 is supported: the dependencies install from prebuilt wheels on each. CI runs the stack on Python 3.12.

On macOS the Celery worker runs in threads: a forked worker process that opens a Delta table crashes there, because the libraries it loads are not safe to use after `fork()`. Celery time limits and `max-tasks-per-child` do not apply to a threads pool.

MongoDB 5 and later needs AVX on x86_64 and ARMv8.2-A on arm64, which rules out some older machines such as the Raspberry Pi 4. `up` reports it when `mongod` stops on an illegal instruction.

______________________________________________________________________

## Troubleshooting

#### A service exited during startup

`up` stops the services it started and names the log to read, under `~/.depictio/local/logs`.

#### A port is already in use

Every port moves to a free one by itself (see [Ports](#ports)): only an explicit `--port` that is busy stops `up`. So two local servers, each with its own `DEPICTIO_LOCAL_HOME`, or a local server and a Docker stack, run side by side.

#### On an HPC login node or behind a proxy

An HTTP proxy set in the environment does not break startup: the readiness checks on `127.0.0.1` bypass it, SeaweedFS runs without the proxy variables, and the API, the worker and any CLI command that reaches the local server get `127.0.0.1` and `localhost` added to `no_proxy`. The downloads do need the network: MongoDB, Redis and SeaweedFS from conda-forge on the first run, and the compose file of `depictio local export`. When one fails, a one-line error says so: check the network or the proxy settings, then run the command again. Over SSH, open the server through the `ssh -L` tunnel that `up` prints, and mind the [shared machines](#files) warning.

#### `DEPICTIO_*` settings are ignored

`up` does not pass the `DEPICTIO_*` variables of your shell to the server, since they usually target another instance (`DEPICTIO_LOCAL_HOME` is read by `depictio local` itself). There are three exceptions. `DEPICTIO_TELEMETRY_*`: `DEPICTIO_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` (or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`) turns [telemetry](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/telemetry/index.md) off for the local server too. And, since v1.16.0, `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_*`, the [remote data settings](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#remote-data-sources): the hosts and buckets the server may read. And, since v1.19.0, `DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_*`: `DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_ENABLED=true depictio local up` lets the [protein tiles](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/proteins/#structure-resolver) fetch models from AlphaFold DB and ESMFold. The `AWS_*` variables are not passed on, so the services never reach another S3 store with your shell's keys. A bucket on `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_CREDENTIALED_S3_BUCKETS` is then read with the default profile of your `~/.aws` files or the machine's role, never with `AWS_*` variables. Likewise, `DEPICTIO_CLI_TOKEN` and `DEPICTIO_CLI_API_BASE_URL`, which usually hold the credentials of another server, never apply to `--server local`.

#### The example dashboards show no data

The examples load in the background on the first run. If the server was stopped before they finished, they stay incomplete, and `up` then warns that they did not finish loading. `depictio local wipe`, then `depictio local up`, loads them again.

#### Dashboards stay blank

The viewer bundle is missing, which only concerns an install from a clone, where `up` builds it. `up` warns when the build fails: read `~/.depictio/local/logs/viewer-build.log`, fix the cause (often pnpm or Node.js missing), then run `depictio local down` and `depictio local up` again, which builds it. A server that was already running when the sources changed only gets a warning: `depictio local down`, then `depictio local up`, rebuilds it.

#### Start from scratch

`depictio local wipe --yes` deletes every project, dashboard and file of the local server, with its passwords, keys and saved ports. The downloaded binaries are kept. The next `up` seeds the examples again.

# Install and configure the CLI

The `depictio` command ingests pipeline results and manages projects, dashboards and backups on a Depictio server. It needs Python 3.11 or later. No server yet? [`depictio local up`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/local/index.md) starts one on your machine.

## Install

```
pip install "depictio[multiqc]"
```

```
uv tool install "depictio[multiqc]"
```

```
git clone https://github.com/depictio/depictio.git && cd depictio
pip install -e ".[multiqc]"
```

| Extra     | Adds                                                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| none      | The `depictio` command                                                                                                                      |
| `multiqc` | MultiQC report parsing, used by the nf-core templates                                                                                       |
| `watch`   | File events for [`depictio watch`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#watch-command); without it, it polls |
| `builder` | The [Project Builder](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#project-builder)                                  |
| `local`   | The server [`depictio local up`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/local/index.md) runs                          |

Check it with `depictio --version`. `depictio` alone prints a quick start, `depictio --help` the commands.

`depictio-cli`, the former name

Up to v1.11 the CLI was the `depictio-cli` package. Both packages now install both commands, `depictio` and `depictio-cli`, so old scripts and Nextflow hooks keep working. Never `pip uninstall depictio-cli` alone: it removes files `depictio` needs (`pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps depictio` repairs it). With both as `uv tool`s, reinstall with `--force` or `uv tool uninstall depictio-cli` first.

## Configure

The CLI reaches a server through a configuration file, `~/.depictio/CLI.yaml`:

1. In the web UI, open **Account settings** → **CLI agents** → **Add configuration** ([screenshots](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/get_started/#create-a-cli-configuration)).

1. Download or copy the file to `~/.depictio/CLI.yaml`. It holds a token that signs in as you: keep it private.

1. Check it:

   ```
   depictio config check
   ```

The file holds `api_base_url`, `user` with its `token`, `s3_storage`, and optionally `instance_label` (the name shown in monitoring) and `remote_storage_options` (credentials to read `s3://` sources). Other files are named with `--server FILE`; `--server local` reaches the local server. See [Which server a command uses](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#choosing-a-server).

## Run it from a container

```
docker run --rm --network host \
  -v /path/to/results:/path/to/results \
  -v "$HOME/.depictio:$HOME/.depictio:ro" \
  ghcr.io/depictio/depictio-cli:<version> \
  ingest /path/to/results --server "$HOME/.depictio/CLI.yaml"
```

For a CI runner or head node with Docker but no Python. The image carries the MultiQC extra; its entrypoint is `depictio-cli`. Mount each path at the same path inside, since paths are recorded as given. The container runs as UID 1000 with its own home, so name the file with `--server` and make it readable. `-e DEPICTIO_CLI_TOKEN` overrides its token.

## Troubleshooting

Every command first prints a `Server:` line naming the server and the file it read. `depictio config check` tests the server and its S3 storage.

| Symptom              | Check                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Connection error     | The server runs, and `api_base_url` is right                                                   |
| Authentication error | The token is valid; generate a new configuration if needed                                     |
| S3 error             | The storage runs and its credentials are right. The server creates a missing bucket at startup |

Next: [Common tasks](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/tasks/index.md).

# Configuration Guide

Depictio reads its configuration from environment variables. This page covers what to set for a first deployment, then each topic. Every variable, with its default, is in the [Environment Reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/index.md).

| Deployment          | Where the variables go                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Docker Compose      | `.env` next to `docker-compose.yaml`, started from the repository's [`.env.example`](https://github.com/depictio/depictio/blob/main/.env.example) |
| Helm                | `backend.env` in your values file; credentials under `secrets.*`; worker sizing under `celery.env`                                                |
| `depictio local up` | The shell that runs it. See [Python package](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/local/index.md)                         |

## First deployment

With no `.env`, the root `docker-compose.yaml` starts in **single-user mode**: no login, and no secret is checked. That suits one person on one machine. For a server other people reach, set:

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE=false
DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_USER=depictio
DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me     # openssl rand -base64 24
DEPICTIO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.org
DEPICTIO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me     # openssl rand -base64 24
DEPICTIO_VIEWER_PUBLIC_URL=https://depictio.example.org
DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_PUBLIC_URL=https://depictio.example.org
```

| Variable                                                    | Why                                                                                                             | Helm                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE=false`                      | Turns sign-in on, and with it the secret checks                                                                 | Already `false`                                                      |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_USER`, `_ROOT_PASSWORD`                   | Bucket credentials. The server refuses a password under 8 characters or a well-known default such as `minio123` | `secrets.s3RootUser`, `secrets.s3RootPassword`; generated when empty |
| `DEPICTIO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL`, `_ADMIN_PASSWORD`         | The first admin, created once on an empty database. Without them the first start stops                          | `secrets.bootstrapAdminEmail`, `secrets.bootstrapAdminPassword`      |
| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_PUBLIC_URL`, `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_PUBLIC_URL` | The addresses browsers use behind your proxy: magic links and SSO land there                                    | Derived from `global.domain`                                         |

Everything else has a working default. A refused secret is named in the startup error:

```
docker compose logs depictio-backend
```

## Storage

Depictio keeps its data in S3-compatible object storage: the bundled SeaweedFS store (Compose service `s3`, Helm `s3.enabled`), or an external S3 service. The settings are `DEPICTIO_S3_*`; the `DEPICTIO_MINIO_*` names of releases before v1.12.0 still work. An install that ran the bundled MinIO copies its data when it upgrades: see [Upgrading to v1.12.0: MinIO → SeaweedFS](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/upgrade/v1.12.0-seaweedfs/index.md). The server creates the bucket if needed and only needs rights on that bucket: see [Required S3 permissions](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#required-s3-permissions).

### External S3

For AWS, NetApp, Ceph or your own MinIO. With Docker Compose, in `.env`, then start without the bundled store (`docker compose up -d --scale s3=0`):

```
DEPICTIO_S3_PUBLIC_URL=https://s3.example.com
DEPICTIO_S3_EXTERNAL_SERVICE=true
DEPICTIO_S3_BUCKET=your-bucket-name
DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_USER=your-access-key
DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_PASSWORD=your-secret-key
```

With Helm, turn the bundled store off; the chart then sets `DEPICTIO_S3_EXTERNAL_SERVICE` itself:

```
s3:
  enabled: false
  env:
    DEPICTIO_S3_PUBLIC_URL: "https://s3.example.com"
    DEPICTIO_S3_BUCKET: "your-bucket-name"
secrets:
  s3RootUser: "your-access-key"
  s3RootPassword: "your-secret-key"
```

### Browsers that cannot reach S3 (v1.22.0+)

3D structures and file-backed genome tracks are read by the browser, through URLs presigned for the S3 public endpoint. When browsers cannot reach S3 (an IP-only install, a store kept on the cluster network), set `DEPICTIO_S3_BROWSER_ACCESS=proxy` and the API streams those files itself. See [Browser access to indexed files](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#s3-browser-access); Helm picks the mode for you ([`s3.browserAccess`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/kubernetes/#s3-browser-access)).

## Authentication

The sign-in mode is one switch, compared in [Authentication Modes](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/authentication-modes/index.md):

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE=true    # one person, no login (the Compose default)
DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE=true         # anonymous read-only, sign in to create
DEPICTIO_AUTH_DEMO_MODE=true           # with PUBLIC_MODE: never offers sign-in to guests
```

With none set (and `SINGLE_USER_MODE=false` under Compose), everyone signs in. Restricting registration or password sign-in, the public-mode access code and pipeline provisioning are on the same page. Every `DEPICTIO_AUTH_*` variable is in the [reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#authentication).

### Single sign-on (OpenID Connect)

Users can sign in through any OpenID Connect identity provider (Keycloak, Google, Authentik, ...), with their groups mirrored from it. Providers are declared as a JSON list; credentials go in their own variables:

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS='[
  {
    "id": "google",
    "label": "Sign in with Google",
    "discovery_url": "https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
  }
]'
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=1234567890-example.apps.googleusercontent.com
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=change-me
```

The redirect URI to register at the provider is `https://<api-host>/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/<id>/callback`. Full reference, provider recipes and migration from the former `DEPICTIO_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH_*` settings: [Single sign-on (OpenID Connect)](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/index.md).

### Keys

On first start the backend writes an RS256 key pair (`private_key.pem`, `public_key.pem`) and `secrets_key.bin`, which encrypts per-project storage credentials, into `DEPICTIO_AUTH_KEYS_DIR` (`/app/depictio/keys`). The backend and the Celery worker must share that folder: Compose mounts the `depictio_keys` volume on both, the Helm chart a volume of its own. To bring your own pair, put the two files in a folder, mount it read-only on the backend **and** the worker, and point `DEPICTIO_AUTH_KEYS_DIR` at it:

```
openssl genrsa -out private_key.pem 2048
openssl rsa -in private_key.pem -pubout -out public_key.pem
chmod 600 private_key.pem
```

The internal API key, used between services, is generated too. Set `DEPICTIO_AUTH_INTERNAL_API_KEY` (e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`) to choose it.

### CORS

Control which browser origins are allowed to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the FastAPI backend:

```
# Comma-separated list of allowed origins (scheme + host + optional port)
DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://app.example.com,https://dash.example.com
```

| Value                     | Behaviour                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *(empty / unset)*         | No credentialed cross-origin requests are permitted           |
| `https://app.example.com` | Only the listed origins are allowed                           |
| `*`                       | **Rejected when credentials are used**: list explicit origins |

Leave it unset when the browser reaches the API on the viewer's own origin, as with the bundled nginx.

## Background workers

The `depictio-celery-worker` container always runs: the dashboard editor's previews, large renders and thumbnails go through it, over Redis. Size it with `DEPICTIO_CELERY_WORKERS` on the worker (`celery.env` with Helm; default 4 processes, the chart sets 2). Each process holds its own data, so memory sets the limit. When renders offload, and how long the API waits, is set on the backend: see [Celery Task Queue](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#celery-task-queue). Offloaded ingestion runs on a second worker: see [Ingestion worker](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/#ingestion-worker).

## Backup and Restore Configuration

MongoDB backups run from the admin panel or on a schedule; S3 data is copied to a second bucket, a local folder, or both. Day-to-day use is in [Backup & Restore](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/backup/index.md).

```
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_AUTO_BACKUP_ENABLED=true
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_AUTO_BACKUP_TIME_OF_DAY=03:00              # UTC
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_BACKUP_FILE_RETENTION_DAYS=30
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_S3_BACKUP_STRATEGY=s3_to_s3                # s3_to_s3, local or both
```

### Backup to Separate S3 Bucket

Keep the copy of S3 data apart from the primary bucket:

```
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_BACKUP_S3_ENABLED=true
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_BACKUP_S3_BUCKET=depictio-backups
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT_URL=https://s3.amazonaws.com
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY=your-backup-s3-access-key
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_KEY=your-backup-s3-secret-key
DEPICTIO_BACKUP_BACKUP_S3_REGION=us-east-1
```

Scheduled backups, retention tiers and every `DEPICTIO_BACKUP_*` variable: [Backup & Restore](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#backup-restore).

## Example projects

At startup the API seeds five reference projects with their dashboards: Iris, Penguins, Advanced Visualisations, nf-core/ampliseq and nf-core/viralrecon. Every other [pipeline template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/index.md) comes from ingesting a run.

```
DEPICTIO_DISABLE_EXAMPLE_DASHBOARDS=true    # seed none of them
DEPICTIO_SEED_PROJECTS=iris,penguins        # or only these
DEPICTIO_SEED_EXTRA_PROJECTS=genome_tracks_examples   # add an optional one
```

Since v1.22.0 the Genome Tracks Showcase is optional: a fresh database seeds it only when `DEPICTIO_SEED_EXTRA_PROJECTS` names `genome_tracks_examples`. An instance that already has it keeps it.

## Analytics and telemetry

| What                                                                                                                                                  | Default | Set                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Anonymous installation [telemetry](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/telemetry/index.md), once a day                           | On      | `DEPICTIO_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` to stop it                          |
| [Internal analytics](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#internal-analytics): sessions stored in your MongoDB | Off     | `DEPICTIO_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=true`                                                          |
| Google Analytics 4                                                                                                                                    | Off     | `DEPICTIO_GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=true` and `DEPICTIO_GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_TRACKING_ID=G-...` |

All three are set on the backend. The viewer reads them from the API at boot, so with Helm they go in `backend.env` only, as in the chart's `examples/values-google-analytics.yaml`.

## Optional features

Off or bounded by default. Each link goes to the variables.

| Feature                                          | Turn on with                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Live refresh over WebSocket                      | [`DEPICTIO_EVENTS_ENABLED`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#real-time-events)                                                                                                         |
| What changed since a reader's last visit         | [`DEPICTIO_DASHBOARD_VERSIONS_CHANGES_SINCE_ENABLED`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#dashboard-versions)                                                                             |
| Background ingestion and the `/jobs` API         | [`DEPICTIO_JOBS_ENABLED`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#jobs), then [`DEPICTIO_INGESTION_*`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#ingestion) |
| Reading `https://` and `s3://` sources           | [`DEPICTIO_REMOTE_*`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#remote-data-sources)                                                                                                            |
| Exporting and embedding a component              | [`DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_ENABLED`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#component-export)                                                                                                  |
| Remote genome browser tracks                     | [`DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_*`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#genome-browser)                                                                                                                |
| Protein structures from AlphaFold DB and ESMFold | [`DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_ENABLED`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#structure-resolver)                                                                                           |
| Pushing projects to another instance             | [`DEPICTIO_MIGRATION_*`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#project-migration)                                                                                                           |
| Comments by viewers                              | [`DEPICTIO_COMMENTS_VIEWERS_CAN_COMMENT`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#comments)                                                                                                   |
| A feedback link on every dashboard               | [`DEPICTIO_FEEDBACK_*`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#feedback)                                                                                                                     |
| Your logo, colours and fonts                     | [`DEPICTIO_BRANDING_*`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#branding)                                                                                                                     |
| The new-release notice for admins                | [`DEPICTIO_VERSION_CHECK_*`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#release-check)                                                                                                           |

## Version and development

```
DEPICTIO_VERSION=1.22.0       # image tag; unset uses the release the compose file pins, `next` follows main
DEPICTIO_DEV_MODE=true        # API reload, worker restart on code change, no telemetry, tours or landing card
DEPICTIO_WALKTHROUGH_DISABLED=true   # no guided tours or dashboard landing card, for every user
```

`DEPICTIO_DEV_MODE` is not a security switch: since v1.5.2 it no longer touches OAuth state validation. See [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#oauth-callback-security). Keep `DEPICTIO_MONGODB_WIPE` and `DEPICTIO_ENABLE_DEV_ENDPOINTS` off outside development.

## Security checklist

- Keep `.env` and Helm secrets out of version control; supply them from a secret store.
- Turn single-user mode off on anything others can reach, and put a TLS proxy in front.
- Back up the keys folder with the database: without `secrets_key.bin`, stored project credentials cannot be read.
- Keep backups in a bucket apart from the data.

# Environment Variables Reference

Every environment variable Depictio reads, grouped by prefix. The settings models in [`settings_models.py`](https://github.com/depictio/depictio/blob/main/depictio/api/v1/configs/settings_models.py) are the source of truth; the few variables read elsewhere (start scripts, Compose) are listed with their section. For what to set first, see the [Configuration guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/configuration/index.md).

Values are strings in the environment. A list accepts a JSON list, and a comma-separated string where the description says so. With Docker Compose they go in `.env`; with Helm, in `backend.env` (secrets under `secrets.*`).

## FastAPI Backend

**Config Class:** `FastAPIConfig` **Environment Prefix:** `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_`

The API server. Each service section (FastAPI, Viewer, MongoDB, S3) shares the same address fields: `SERVICE_NAME` and `SERVICE_PORT` are the in-network address other containers use, `EXTERNAL_HOST`, `EXTERNAL_PORT` and `EXTERNAL_PROTOCOL` build the address browsers and the CLI use, and `PUBLIC_URL` overrides that address (a reverse proxy or CDN).

| Variable                                  | Default            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_SERVICE_NAME`           | `depictio-backend` | Host name inside the Compose network                                                                                                                                                                |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_SERVICE_PORT`           | `8058`             | Port inside the network                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EXTERNAL_HOST`          | `localhost`        | Host name for external access                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EXTERNAL_PORT`          | `8058`             | Port for external access                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EXTERNAL_PROTOCOL`      | `http`             | `http` or `https`                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_PUBLIC_URL`             | -                  | Public URL of the API, overriding the three above                                                                                                                                                   |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EXTERNAL_SERVICE`       | `false`            | `true` when the API runs outside the Compose network                                                                                                                                                |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_HOST`                   | `0.0.0.0`          | Bind address of Gunicorn, read by the image's start script                                                                                                                                          |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_PORT`                   | `8058`             | Bind port, read by the start script only                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_WORKERS`                | `4`                | Gunicorn worker processes                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`   | *(empty)*          | Allowed CORS origins, comma-separated (e.g. `https://app.example.com,https://example.com`). Empty disables credentialed cross-origin requests. Wildcard `*` is rejected when used with credentials. |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS` | `true`             | Whether the CORS layer attaches credentials (cookies / Authorization header).                                                                                                                       |

### Component export (v1.17.0+)

The API that serves one dashboard component to another website. See [Component export and embedding](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/component-export/index.md).

| Variable                                   | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_ENABLED`           | `false`   | Serve `/depictio/api/v1/export` and show **Export / embed** on the tiles. Off, every export route answers `404`                                                          |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`   | *(empty)* | Sites allowed to frame an exported page, comma-separated. They become its CSP `frame-ancestors`. Empty: the pages open on their own but cannot be framed. `*` is refused |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_CSP_UNSAFE_INLINE` | `false`   | Allow inline scripts in the exported page instead of listing their hashes                                                                                                |

| Variable                                  | Default           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_SERVICE_NAME`            | `depictio-viewer` | Host name inside the Compose network                                                                                                                                                                        |

| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_EXTERNAL_HOST`           | `localhost`       | Host name for external access                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_EXTERNAL_PORT`           | `5080`            | Host-side port mapped to the viewer container                                                                                                                                                               |

| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_EXTERNAL_SERVICE`        | `false`           | `true` when the viewer runs outside the Compose network                                                                                                                                                     |
| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_INSPECTOR_ENABLED`       | `false`           | Docked component inspector, replacing the per-component popovers for advanced-visualisation controls, notes and metadata. Experimental (v1.4.0+)                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_DASHBOARDS_DEFAULT_VIEW` | `table`           | View `/dashboards` opens in for someone who never picked one: `thumbnails` or `table`. A view chosen in the browser, or named by a shared link, wins (v1.11.2+; the default was `thumbnails` until v1.12.0) |
| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_CODE_FIGURES_LOCKED`     | `false`           | Refuse new figure code from non-admin users. Existing code figures still render. See [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#figure-code-lock) (v1.21.0+)             |

## S3 Storage

**Config Class:** `S3DepictioCLIConfig` **Environment Prefix:** `DEPICTIO_S3_` (legacy `DEPICTIO_MINIO_`)

S3-compatible object storage: the bundled SeaweedFS store (Compose service `s3`), or any external S3 endpoint (AWS, NetApp, Ceph, MinIO, …) set with `DEPICTIO_S3_PUBLIC_URL` and `DEPICTIO_S3_EXTERNAL_SERVICE=true`.

`DEPICTIO_MINIO_*` became `DEPICTIO_S3_*` in v1.12.0

The bundled store is SeaweedFS instead of MinIO since **v1.12.0**, and these settings were renamed with it. The former `DEPICTIO_MINIO_<FIELD>` names still work: each is read when its `DEPICTIO_S3_<FIELD>` counterpart is unset, the new name wins when both are set, and the server logs a deprecation warning naming the old variables it found. An install that used the bundled MinIO has to copy its data to the new store: see [Upgrading to v1.12.0: MinIO → SeaweedFS](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/upgrade/v1.12.0-seaweedfs/index.md).

| Variable                                | Default           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_SERVICE_NAME`              | `s3`              | Host name of the store inside the Compose network (`minio` before v1.12.0, still an alias of the `s3` service)                                                                                                                                                               |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_SERVICE_PORT`              | `9000`            | -                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_EXTERNAL_HOST`             | `localhost`       | -                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_EXTERNAL_PORT`             | `9000`            | -                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_EXTERNAL_PROTOCOL`         | `http`            | -                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_PUBLIC_URL`                | -                 | Full endpoint URL of an external S3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_EXTERNAL_SERVICE`          | `false`           | `true` when the store is outside the Docker Compose network                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_USER`                 | `minio`           | S3 access key                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_PASSWORD`             | *(empty)*         | S3 secret key. Outside single-user mode the server refuses to start unless it has at least 8 characters and is not a well-known default (`minio123`, `changeme`, ...)                                                                                                        |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_BUCKET`                    | `depictio-bucket` | -                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_VERIFY_TLS`                | `true`            | Verify TLS certificates when connecting to S3. Set to `false` only for local dev with self-signed certificates.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `DEPICTIO_S3_BROWSER_ACCESS` (v1.22.0+) | `presigned`       | How browsers read [indexed files](#s3-browser-access) (3D structures, GenomeSpy VCF/BAM/bigWig tracks): `presigned` or `proxy`. The Helm chart sets it, see [`s3.browserAccess`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/kubernetes/#s3-browser-access) |

### Browser access to indexed files (v1.22.0+)

The 3D structure viewer and GenomeSpy's file-backed tracks read their files from the browser, by HTTP range request.

- **`presigned`** (default): the API hands out URLs signed for the S3 public endpoint (`DEPICTIO_S3_PUBLIC_URL`, or the `EXTERNAL_*` host and port), and the browser reads S3 directly. S3 must be reachable from the reader's browser, with CORS allowing `Range`.
- **`proxy`**: the API hands out its own URLs, `GET|HEAD /depictio/api/v1/files/indexed/{dc_id}/object/{sample}/{name}`, and streams each object by byte range. Each URL is signed for one object and one user and lives 15 minutes; the reader's access is checked again on every request. No CORS or CSP entry for S3 is needed.

Use `proxy` when browsers cannot reach S3: an IP-only install where S3 stays on the Compose network, a Serve app, a store with no public route. The symptom in `presigned` mode is a structure or track that fails with *Failed to fetch* while tables and figures load.

### Required S3 permissions

At startup the server checks that the configured bucket is usable. Since **v1.5.2** those checks are scoped to that single bucket: `HeadBucket`, then a put/delete round trip on a test object.

A credential that can only reach `DEPICTIO_S3_BUCKET` is therefore enough, which is useful on managed S3 where keys are issued per bucket rather than per account.

Since **v1.6.0** the server creates the bucket before running those checks, so **you do not have to provision it first**: pointing a fresh deployment at empty object storage is enough. A bucket that already exists is left alone: creation short-circuits and no `CreateBucket` call is made, so a credential issued against an existing bucket needs no extra permission.

Account-wide `ListBuckets` is no longer required

Before v1.5.2 the check called `ListBuckets`, an account-level operation. Bucket-scoped credentials got `AccessDenied` and the server refused to start, even though the bucket itself was perfectly usable.

Before v1.6.0, a first boot against empty storage failed

The checks ran before the line that creates the bucket, so a deployment with nothing provisioned ahead of it died during startup with *"Bucket 'depictio-bucket' does not exist"*. Genuinely broken storage still refuses to start, since the checks now simply follow creation.

## Remote Data Sources (v1.16.0+)

**Config Class:** `RemoteConfig` **Environment Prefix:** `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_`

Policy for reading user-supplied locations: the gateway that fetches `https://` URLs (the `url` and `manifest` scan modes, manifest downloads, the endpoint gating of per-project storage credentials), and which `s3://` buckets the server may read without the project's storage settings. The section is read from the environment on every read, so the API and the Celery worker apply the same policy, and a malformed value fails at the first read instead of silently falling back to a default. The run-folder browser then offers no S3 location, and the server log says why. See [Remote data and manifests](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#reading-s3-buckets) and [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#remote-data-sources).

| Variable                                  | Default               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_ALLOW_HTTP`              | `false`               | Accept plain `http://` URLs in addition to `https://` and `s3://`. Off by default: the gateway and the models reject `http://` locations. Turn on for local or airgapped deployments that serve data without TLS                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_ALLOWLIST`           | *(empty)*             | Comma-separated host names the gateway may fetch from. **Exclusive while set**: any host not listed is rejected, and a listed host skips the private/loopback address rejection, which is how internal deployments opt an intranet host in. Empty accepts every public host |
| `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_DENYLIST`            | *(empty)*             | Comma-separated host names the gateway always rejects. Checked before the allowlist, so a host present in both lists is denied                                                                                                                                              |
| `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_PUBLIC_S3_BUCKETS`       | *(empty)*             | Comma-separated S3 locations read without credentials, each `bucket` or `bucket/prefix`, on Amazon S3. Unsigned access is opt-in: any other `s3://` location needs the project's storage settings, read unsigned too when they hold no key, or an entry in the next list    |
| `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_CREDENTIALED_S3_BUCKETS` | *(empty)*             | Comma-separated S3 locations, same syntax, that the API and the worker read with their own ambient credentials (the AWS default chain: environment, IAM role, web identity). Every user of the instance can read what is listed here. Not used by the CLI                   |
| `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES`      | `524288000` (500 MiB) | Size cap in bytes for a single remote download: a data file, a manifest the CLI reads, a MultiQC report. Downloads stream and abort, removing the partial file, once the cap is exceeded. The server reads a manifest up to 50 MiB, or this cap when it is lower            |
| `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_S`               | `30.0`                | Timeout in seconds applied to each connect, read and write operation of a remote fetch, not a total download time. Also the connect and read timeouts of the S3 client that reads a user-supplied `s3://` location                                                          |
| `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_MAX_REDIRECTS`           | `3`                   | Maximum redirect hops followed for a remote URL. Every `Location` is re-validated against this policy before it is followed                                                                                                                                                 |

A listed host bypasses the private-address check

Setting `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_ALLOWLIST` both restricts fetches to the listed hosts and exempts those hosts from the private-range rejection. List only hosts you control.

The backend and the Celery worker must agree on these variables:

| Deployment     | Where to set them                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Kubernetes     | `backend.env` in the Helm values, rendered for both the backend and the Celery worker                                                                                                                            |
| Docker Compose | `.env`, passed to both the backend and the worker                                                                                                                                                                |
| Python package | The shell that runs `depictio local up`, which passes `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_*` on to the server, but not `AWS_*`: see [`depictio local`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/local/index.md) |

### Local data folders (v1.16.0+)

**Config Class:** `LocalDataConfig` **Environment Prefix:** `DEPICTIO_LOCAL_DATA_`

| Variable                    | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_LOCAL_DATA_ROOTS` | *(empty)* | Comma-separated absolute folders (or `~/...`) the web UI may read run folders from. Empty turns local folders off. Honoured only with `DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE`; hidden folders and the folders Depictio keeps for itself are never read |

`depictio local up` sets it to your home folder plus each [`--data-root-allow`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/local/#up-options) folder; there is no need to set it by hand. See [From a run folder](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#from-a-run-folder).
