# Configuration reference

Every setting of [OpenID Connect single sign-on](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/index.md): the variables, the keys of a provider entry, which claims feed the account, and the callback to register at the IdP.

______________________________________________________________________

## Environment variables

| Variable                                | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS`          | *(empty)* | JSON list of provider objects, see [provider keys](#provider-keys)                                                                                         |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_<ID>_CLIENT_ID`     | -         | Client id of provider `<ID>`. Overrides `client_id` in the list                                                                                            |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_<ID>_CLIENT_SECRET` | -         | Client secret of provider `<ID>`. Overrides `client_secret` in the list                                                                                    |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_REGISTRATION_DISABLED`   | `false`   | SSO becomes login-only: see [Closed registration](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/groups-and-access/#registration-closed) |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_PASSWORD_LOGIN_DISABLED` | `false`   | SSO becomes the only way in: see [SSO-only mode](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/groups-and-access/#sso-only)             |
| `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_PUBLIC_URL`            | -         | Public URL of the viewer, where the ticket hand-off and error redirects land                                                                               |

The deprecated `DEPICTIO_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH_*` variables are described in [From Google OAuth to OIDC](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/migration/#from-google-oauth-to-oidc). The full variable list is in the [Environment Reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#authentication).

______________________________________________________________________

## Provider keys

Each object of `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS` accepts these keys. Unknown keys are rejected.

| Key                          | Default                                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                         | *(required)*                                                 | Stable identifier, used in URLs and in the credential variable names. Lower case, `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`                                                                                |
| `label`                      | `Sign in with <id>`                                          | Text of the sign-in button                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `enabled`                    | `true`                                                       | Set `false` to hide a provider without deleting it                                                                                                                                          |
| `issuer`                     | -                                                            | Expected issuer, for example `https://idp.example.org/realms/example`. Discovery defaults to `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, and the document's `issuer` must equal this value |
| `discovery_url`              | -                                                            | Explicit discovery document URL, overriding the default derived from `issuer`                                                                                                               |
| `client_id`                  | -                                                            | Client id. Prefer `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_<ID>_CLIENT_ID`                                                                                                                                       |
| `client_secret`              | -                                                            | Client secret. Prefer `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_<ID>_CLIENT_SECRET`                                                                                                                               |
| `scopes`                     | `["openid", "email", "profile"]`                             | A list or a space-separated string. `openid` is always added                                                                                                                                |
| `redirect_uri`               | `<API external URL>/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/<id>/callback` | Callback registered at the IdP. Never read from the request                                                                                                                                 |
| `claims`                     | see [Claim mapping](#claim-mapping)                          | Which claims feed the account                                                                                                                                                               |
| `sso_provider`               | the `id`                                                     | Value stored on the user as `sso_provider`                                                                                                                                                  |
| `assume_email_verified`      | `false`                                                      | Trust the email even without `email_verified: true`. See [Email and accounts](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/#email-and-accounts)                         |
| `token_endpoint_auth_method` | `client_secret_basic`                                        | How the client authenticates at the token endpoint: `client_secret_basic`, `client_secret_post`, or `none` for a public client protected by PKCE alone                                      |
| `authorize_params`           | `{}`                                                         | Extra parameters added to the authorization request, for example `{"prompt": "select_account", "hd": "example.org"}`                                                                        |
| `fetch_userinfo`             | `true`                                                       | Also call the userinfo endpoint and merge its claims **under** the `id_token` claims, only when its `sub` matches                                                                           |

At least one of `issuer` or `discovery_url` is required, plus a client id and, unless `token_endpoint_auth_method` is `none`, a client secret.

______________________________________________________________________

## Claim mapping

`claims` maps Depictio's fields to the **names of claims** the IdP sends:

| Key            | Default   | Feeds                                                                                                      |
| -------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`        | `email`   | The account email (the matching key)                                                                       |
| `groups`       | *(unset)* | SSO-managed [groups](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/groups/index.md) |
| `display_name` | *(unset)* | The display name, for example `name`                                                                       |
| `login`        | *(unset)* | The login, for example `preferred_username`                                                                |
| `title`        | *(unset)* | The title shown in Account settings                                                                        |
| `picture`      | `picture` | The profile picture (an `https://` URL), unless the user uploaded one                                      |

- A claim value can be a string or a list of strings: IdPs disagree on whether a single group is `"lab"` or `["lab"]`, and Depictio accepts both.
- Names are matched exactly first, then ignoring case.
- A **dotted name** is read as a path into nested objects when no top-level claim carries the whole name: `realm_access.roles` reads `{"realm_access": {"roles": [...]}}`.
- A mapping left unset skips that part of the sync.

______________________________________________________________________

## Redirect URI

The default callback is `<API external URL>/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/<id>/callback`, built from the API's external URL setting. Register exactly that value at the IdP: a mismatch is refused by the IdP before the user ever reaches Depictio. Behind a proxy, or on a public host other than the one Depictio knows, set `redirect_uri` explicitly. Most providers only allow `https` redirect URIs outside `localhost`, so the API must be served over TLS.

______________________________________________________________________

## On Kubernetes

With the Helm chart, the provider list goes under `oidc.providers` (rendered into `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS`) and the credentials under `secrets.oidcClients.<id>` (rendered into the chart's Secret as `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_<ID>_CLIENT_ID` and `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_<ID>_CLIENT_SECRET`):

```
oidc:
  providers:
    - id: keycloak
      label: Sign in with your institution
      issuer: https://idp.example.org/realms/example
      claims:
        groups: groups
secrets:
  oidcClients:
    keycloak:
      clientId: depictio
      clientSecret: change-me
```

Keep `secrets.oidcClients` in your environment's secrets values rather than in the repository. The backend ConfigMap also exports `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_PUBLIC_URL`, which the hand-off back to the viewer needs.

# Groups and access

What an OpenID Connect sign-in changes on the account, and how to restrict who gets in. The claim names are set in the [claim mapping](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/configuration/#claim-mapping).

______________________________________________________________________

## Group and profile sync

Four optional claim mappings are read at every OIDC sign-in. An unset mapping skips its step, so nothing changes until a deployment sets them.

| Claim mapping         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `claims.groups`       | Mirrors the listed groups as **SSO-managed** [groups](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/groups/index.md): created when first seen, membership re-synced both ways at every sign-in |
| `claims.title`        | The user's title, shown in Account settings                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `claims.display_name` | The user's display name                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `claims.login`        | The user's login                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

The provider's `id` (or `sso_provider`) is stamped on the user as `sso_provider`, and a profile picture is taken from `claims.picture` when the provider sends one.

______________________________________________________________________

## Group claim semantics

- The claim's values are taken verbatim as group names (whitespace stripped, empty values dropped); no parsing is attempted.
- Each listed group is created if missing, marked SSO-managed, and the user is added.
- The user is then **removed from every SSO-managed group that the claim does not list**, including as a group admin or P.I.
- **An absent claim counts as an empty list.** With `claims.groups` configured, a login whose token carries no such claim removes the user from all SSO-managed groups: the IdP is the source of truth for SSO-managed membership. Check that your IdP puts the claim in the ID token, or in userinfo (which Depictio merges in).
- **Groups created by hand (manual groups) are never touched** by the sync.
- A failed sync is logged and never blocks the sign-in; the next sign-in syncs again.
- A [P.I. named in advance](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/groups/#pi) is claimed at the sign-in that first sends their group.

**Group and profile sync.** Names and values are illustrative.

______________________________________________________________________

## Registration and SSO-only mode

### Closed registration

With `DEPICTIO_AUTH_REGISTRATION_DISABLED=true`, SSO is **login-only**: a known email signs in, an unknown one is refused (`registration_disabled`) instead of being provisioned an account. Administrators create the accounts. See [Registration](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/authentication-modes/#registration).

### SSO-only mode

`DEPICTIO_AUTH_PASSWORD_LOGIN_DISABLED=true` closes email and password sign-in, so single sign-on is the only way in. It takes effect **only when at least one OIDC provider is enabled and fully configured**, so a typo in the provider list gives you the password form back instead of a locked instance. See [Password sign-in](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/authentication-modes/#password-login).

# From Google OAuth to OIDC

Existing accounts are matched by email, so nobody loses their projects, dashboards or group memberships when you switch.

Google is now a plain OIDC provider: the dedicated Google sign-in code is gone. The old variables **keep working for one release** and are mapped onto a provider with the id `google`, the label *Sign in with Google* and the Google discovery URL. The API logs a deprecation warning at startup while they are set, and an explicit `google` entry in `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS` wins over them.

| Old variable                               | New setting                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH_ENABLED`       | declare the provider (`enabled`)          |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`     | `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`     |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | `DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_GOOGLE_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`  | `redirect_uri` (or drop it, see below)    |

The redirect URI registered in Google can stay as it was: the old value is the viewer URL `https://<host>/auth/google/callback`, and that viewer path now forwards the browser, with its query string, to the API callback `/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/google/callback`. To move to the new default, add `https://<api-host>/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/google/callback` to the authorized redirect URIs in the Google Cloud Console, remove the `redirect_uri` override, and delete the old URI once nothing uses it.

Move to the [Google recipe](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/providers/#recipe-google) before the legacy variables are removed. Google accounts keep working unchanged: they are matched by email.

# Provider recipes

Ready-to-adapt settings for common identity providers. The keys are described in the [configuration reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/configuration/#provider-keys).

All values are placeholders: replace `idp.example.org`, the realm and client credentials with your own. In every recipe the redirect URI to register is `https://depictio.example.org/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/<id>/callback`, with the `<id>` of that recipe.

______________________________________________________________________

## Keycloak

1. In the realm, create a client: **Client type** OpenID Connect, **Client ID** `depictio`, **Client authentication** on, **Standard flow** on (direct access grants and implicit flow off).
1. **Valid redirect URIs**: `https://depictio.example.org/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/keycloak/callback`.
1. In the client's **Advanced** settings, set **Proof Key for Code Exchange Code Challenge Method** to `S256`.
1. Copy the secret from the **Credentials** tab.
1. For groups, add a **Group Membership** mapper to the client's dedicated scope with **Token Claim Name** `groups`, **Full group path** off (to get `lab` rather than `/lab`), and **Add to ID token** on. To use realm roles instead, read the built-in dotted claim `realm_access.roles`.

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS='[
  {
    "id": "keycloak",
    "label": "Sign in with your institution",
    "issuer": "https://idp.example.org/realms/example",
    "claims": {
      "groups": "groups",
      "display_name": "name",
      "login": "preferred_username"
    }
  }
]'
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID=depictio
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET=change-me
```

For realm roles, use `"groups": "realm_access.roles"`. Keycloak also lists its built-in roles (such as `offline_access`) in that claim, and they would become groups.

______________________________________________________________________

## Google

1. In the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), under **APIs & Services** > **Credentials**, create an **OAuth client ID** of type **Web application**.
1. **Authorized redirect URIs**: `https://depictio.example.org/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/google/callback`.
1. Configure the consent screen. Choose **Internal** to restrict sign-in to your Google Workspace organization.

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS='[
  {
    "id": "google",
    "label": "Sign in with Google",
    "discovery_url": "https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration",
    "claims": { "display_name": "name" },
    "authorize_params": { "hd": "example.org", "prompt": "select_account" }
  }
]'
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=1234567890-example.apps.googleusercontent.com
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=change-me
```

- `hd` in `authorize_params` only **hints** the Workspace domain to the account chooser; it is not enforced on its own. To restrict sign-in for real, use an **Internal** consent screen, or close registration so that only pre-provisioned accounts can sign in.
- Google sends **no groups claim**, so there is no group sync. Leave `claims.groups` unset.
- Google sends `email_verified`, so `assume_email_verified` is not needed.

______________________________________________________________________

## Authentik and other providers

Any compliant provider works the same way. In **Authentik**, create an **OAuth2/OpenID Provider** with client type *Confidential*, the redirect URI `https://depictio.example.org/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/authentik/callback` (strict matching), and the scopes `openid email profile`. Attach it to an application; the issuer is `https://idp.example.org/application/o/<application-slug>/`. For groups, add a scope mapping that returns a `groups` claim.

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS='[
  {
    "id": "authentik",
    "label": "Sign in with Authentik",
    "issuer": "https://idp.example.org/application/o/depictio/",
    "claims": { "groups": "groups", "display_name": "name", "login": "preferred_username" }
  }
]'
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_AUTHENTIK_CLIENT_ID=change-me
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_AUTHENTIK_CLIENT_SECRET=change-me
```

For another provider: open its **discovery document** (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`), use its `issuer` value verbatim, and add to `scopes` any extra scope it needs to release groups.

# Troubleshooting and security

What to check when an OpenID Connect sign-in fails, and what the flow protects against.

______________________________________________________________________

## Troubleshooting

A failed sign-in always ends at `/auth?error=<code>` with a short code, to keep details out of the browser. **The reason is in the API logs** (`docker logs depictio-backend`, or `kubectl logs` on the backend pod): search for `OIDC`.

| Code                    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                | Where to look                                                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sso_failed`            | The login could not be completed: unknown or reused `state`, token exchange refused, invalid `id_token`, no usable email claim, or an unexpected error | The warning `OIDC login with '<id>' failed: …` names the reason                                |
| `sso_cancelled`         | The user denied access or cancelled at the IdP (`access_denied`)                                                                                       | Nothing to fix; the IdP may also deny by policy                                                |
| `sso_unavailable`       | The provider is unknown or disabled, or its discovery document could not be fetched                                                                    | `OIDC provider '<id>' discovery failed: …`, or an unknown provider id in the URL               |
| `registration_disabled` | The email has no account and `DEPICTIO_AUTH_REGISTRATION_DISABLED` is on                                                                               | Create the account first, or reopen registration                                               |
| `email_not_verified`    | The IdP did not assert `email_verified: true`                                                                                                          | `provider '<id>' did not verify …`: fix the IdP, or set `assume_email_verified` if appropriate |

Common causes:

- **Issuer mismatch.** The `issuer` you configured must equal the `issuer` field of the discovery document, and the `iss` of the tokens, character for character (scheme, host, path, realm). Open `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` and copy the value.
- **Redirect URI mismatch.** The IdP rejects the authorization request, before Depictio is involved, when the callback differs from the registered one. Compare it with `https://<api-host>/depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/<id>/callback`, mind the scheme (`https` behind a TLS-terminating proxy) and set `redirect_uri` if Depictio builds a different host than the public one.
- **Clock skew.** `exp` and `iat` are checked with 60 seconds of leeway. A larger drift between the API host and the IdP makes the `id_token` look expired or not yet valid: synchronize clocks (NTP).
- **No button.** The provider is disabled, or lacks an issuer or client id or secret: the startup log has `OIDC provider '<id>' is enabled but lacks …`. `GET /depictio/api/v1/auth/oidc/providers` lists what is shown.
- **Groups disappear.** The groups claim is missing from the token; see [Group claim semantics](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/groups-and-access/#group-claim-semantics).
- **`sso_failed` after a long pause at the IdP.** The `state` lives 10 minutes; start again.

______________________________________________________________________

## Security

- A callback is accepted only if it answers a login this instance started, and only once: the `state` is consumed atomically, so a replay finds nothing.
- Authorization-code interception is covered by PKCE (`S256`), and ID-token replay by the `nonce`. Tokens are verified against the IdP's JWKS, which is re-fetched when the IdP rotates keys.
- The redirect URI comes from the configuration, never from the request, and a `next` path stays on this site.
- The browser is handed a single-use ticket in the URL fragment, redeemed by the viewer.

See [OpenID Connect sign-in](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#oidc-sign-in) on the Security page.

# Upgrading to v1.12.0: MinIO → SeaweedFS

From v1.12.0 the S3 store bundled with Depictio is [SeaweedFS](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs) (`weed mini`, Apache-2.0) instead of MinIO, whose community edition no longer receives releases. SeaweedFS cannot read MinIO's files, so **the bundled store starts empty** on a new volume: dashboards miss their tables and images until you copy the bucket over. MongoDB is untouched and object keys are the same on both sides, so that copy is the whole migration.

| Your install                                                                                                                                | What to do                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Docker Compose with the bundled store                                                                                                       | [Copy the bucket after the upgrade](#docker-compose) |
| Helm chart with the bundled store                                                                                                           | [Export the bucket **before** `helm upgrade`](#helm) |
| External S3 (`DEPICTIO_S3_EXTERNAL_SERVICE=true`, `docker-compose.no-minio.yaml`, Helm `s3.enabled: false`)                                 | Nothing                                              |
| Fresh install, or the [Python package](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/local/index.md) (always used SeaweedFS) | Nothing                                              |

## Renamed settings

Settings are named after S3 rather than MinIO. **The old names keep working**: an old name is read when its new counterpart is unset, the new name wins when both are set, and the server logs a deprecation warning listing the old names it found.

| Before v1.12.0                                                                                                                                                                        | From v1.12.0                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_MINIO_*`: `ROOT_USER`, `ROOT_PASSWORD`, `BUCKET`, `PUBLIC_URL`, `EXTERNAL_SERVICE`, `VERIFY_TLS`, `EXTERNAL_HOST` / `_PORT` / `_PROTOCOL`, `SERVICE_NAME` / `_SERVICE_PORT` | `DEPICTIO_S3_*`, same suffixes                                                                      |
| Compose service `minio`                                                                                                                                                               | `s3`, with `minio` as a network alias: `http://minio:9000` in CLI configurations still resolves     |
| Compose `MINIO_PORT` / `MINIO_CONSOLE_PORT`                                                                                                                                           | `S3_PORT` / `S3_CONSOLE_PORT`                                                                       |
| Helm `minio.*`, `persistence.minio`, `secrets.minioRootUser` / `minioRootPassword`, `global.urlPattern.templates.minio`                                                               | `s3.*`, `persistence.s3`, `secrets.s3RootUser` / `s3RootPassword`, `global.urlPattern.templates.s3` |

- **Helm** still merges the legacy keys and renders the same manifests, with a deprecation warning in the install and upgrade notes. Its ConfigMaps export both prefixes, so a backend image older than v1.12.0 keeps working. The legacy copies will be dropped in a later release.
- **Exception, the development stack**: `docker-compose.dev.yaml` requires `DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_USER` and `DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_PASSWORD` under their new names in `docker-compose/.env`.

All storage settings: [Environment Reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#s3-storage).

Names that stay `minio` on purpose

They are part of live state, and renaming them would break an upgrade:

- Helm: the `<release>-minio` Deployment and Service and their `app: minio` selector (a Deployment selector cannot change); the `<release>-minio-pvc` PVC (a new name would mean an empty volume); the `<release>-minio-ingress` and `-minio-httproute` routes and the `<release>-minio.<domain>` host, which DNS, TLS certificates and presigned URLs point at; the Secret keys `MINIO_ROOT_USER` / `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD`, which keep the generated password stable across upgrades.
- Compose: the backup-only `minio-backup` service and the files `docker-compose.backup-minio.yaml`, `docker-compose.no-minio.yaml` and `docker-compose.minio-legacy.yaml`.

## Docker Compose

The old MinIO is started again as a side-car on its untouched `minio_data` volume, and `scripts/migrate_minio_to_seaweedfs.py` copies the bucket through the S3 API. Run these steps from a clone of the [repository at `v1.12.0`](https://github.com/depictio/depictio/tree/v1.12.0), which holds both files; `uv run` provides the script's only dependency, `boto3`.

1. **Upgrade.** `--remove-orphans` stops the old `minio` container, which the v1.12.0 file no longer declares; its volume stays.

   ```
   docker compose pull
   docker compose up -d --remove-orphans
   ```

1. **Start the old MinIO** on `127.0.0.1:9100`:

   ```
   docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml \
     -f docker-compose/docker-compose.minio-legacy.yaml up -d minio-legacy
   ```

   For the development stack, whose data is a bind mount, run `MINIO_LEGACY_DATA=./data/minio_data docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yaml …` instead.

1. **Publish the new store on `127.0.0.1:9000`.** The development stack already does. The root `docker-compose.yaml` does not: add a temporary override.

   s3-port.yaml

   ```
   services:
     s3:
       ports: ["127.0.0.1:9000:9000"]
   ```

   ```
   docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f s3-port.yaml up -d s3
   ```

1. **Copy.** Credentials and bucket are read from `.env` (`docker-compose/.env` for the development stack). Dry run first, then copy and compare both listings:

   ```
   set -a; source .env; set +a
   uv run scripts/migrate_minio_to_seaweedfs.py --target-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9000 --dry-run
   uv run scripts/migrate_minio_to_seaweedfs.py --target-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9000 --verify
   ```

   An interrupted copy resumes with `--skip-existing`.

1. **Check a dashboard**, then clean up: drop the override (`docker compose up -d`), remove the side-car and, once satisfied, the old volume.

   ```
   docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml \
     -f docker-compose/docker-compose.minio-legacy.yaml rm -sf minio-legacy
   docker volume rm "$(docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)_minio_data"
   ```

   For the development stack: `rm -rf ./data/minio_data`.

**Rolling back:** go back to the previous release's compose files; `minio_data` is untouched until step 5.

## Helm

The chart keeps the `<release>-minio` names, so the upgrade reuses the same PVC. That PVC is `ReadWriteOnce`: the old MinIO pod and the new SeaweedFS pod cannot mount it at the same time, so the copy goes through a local directory, and the export must happen **before** the upgrade.

```
SECRET=<release>-depictio-secrets
KEY=$(kubectl get secret $SECRET -o jsonpath='{.data.MINIO_ROOT_USER}' | base64 -d)
PASS=$(kubectl get secret $SECRET -o jsonpath='{.data.MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}' | base64 -d)

# 1. Before upgrading, while MinIO still runs: export the bucket
kubectl port-forward svc/<release>-minio 9100:9000 &
uv run scripts/migrate_minio_to_seaweedfs.py \
  --source-access-key "$KEY" --source-secret-key "$PASS" --export-dir ./s3-export
kill %1

# 2. Upgrade: SeaweedFS starts on the same PVC and ignores MinIO's files
helm upgrade <release> ./helm-charts/depictio -f values.yaml

# 3. Import into the new store
kubectl port-forward svc/<release>-minio 9000:9000 &
uv run scripts/migrate_minio_to_seaweedfs.py --target-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9000 \
  --target-access-key "$KEY" --target-secret-key "$PASS" --import-dir ./s3-export --verify
kill %1

# 4. Once checked, reclaim the space of MinIO's old files on the PVC
kubectl exec deploy/<release>-minio -- sh -c 'rm -rf /data/.minio.sys /data/depictio-bucket'
```

Keep `./s3-export` until the new store is checked: it is a full copy taken before the upgrade. With a second bucket on an external S3, you can export there (`--target-endpoint https://…`) instead of to a local directory.

Copy script options

| Option                                                                                     | Default                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--source-endpoint`                                                                        | `http://127.0.0.1:9100`                                                                          |
| `--target-endpoint`                                                                        | the S3 URL resolved from the Depictio settings, else `http://127.0.0.1:9000`                     |
| `--source-access-key`, `--source-secret-key`, `--target-access-key`, `--target-secret-key` | `DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_USER` / `DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_PASSWORD`, else the `DEPICTIO_MINIO_ROOT_*` names    |
| `--bucket` (`--target-bucket` for another name on the target)                              | `DEPICTIO_S3_BUCKET`, else `depictio-bucket`                                                     |
| `--prefix`                                                                                 | copy only the keys under this prefix                                                             |
| `--workers`                                                                                | 8 parallel copies                                                                                |
| `--dry-run` / `--verify` / `--skip-existing`                                               | list only / compare listings after the copy / skip keys already on the target with the same size |
| `--export-dir` / `--import-dir`                                                            | download the bucket into a directory / upload a directory into it, instead of copying directly   |

Each endpoint and key can also come from a `MIGRATE_SOURCE_*` / `MIGRATE_TARGET_*` variable (`MIGRATE_SOURCE_ENDPOINT`, …).

## What else changes

- The S3 API stays on port 9000; the health check is `GET :9000/healthz` instead of `/minio/health/live`. WebDAV is off.
- The SeaweedFS admin UI is off in the root compose file and in Helm (`s3.adminUI.enabled`); the development stack serves it on `127.0.0.1:9001`, the former MinIO console port, behind the root keys.
- Root credentials are applied again from the environment at every start, so changing `DEPICTIO_S3_ROOT_*` and restarting rotates them, as with MinIO.
- For very large object counts, pass `-volume.index=leveldb` through Helm `s3.extraArgs` to keep the volume index out of memory.

# Authentication Modes

Depictio supports four authentication modes, each designed for a different deployment scenario. Only one mode is active at a time.

## Quick comparison

- **[Auth](#auth-mode)** · default

  ______________________________________________________________________

  For teams. Everyone signs in to an account of their own, with a role on each project.

  Nothing to set with Helm. With Compose, `DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE=false`.

- **[Single-user](#single-user-mode)**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  For your own instance. No sign-in page: every visitor is signed in as the admin.

  `DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE=true`

- **[Public](#public-mode)**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  For a showcase. Every visitor gets a guest account of their own; SSO can turn it into a real one.

  `DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE=true`

- **[Demo](#demo-mode)**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Public mode as a read-only demo: the same guests, never asked to sign in.

  `DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE=true` and `DEPICTIO_AUTH_DEMO_MODE=true`

Side by side

|                                                                                                                | [Auth](#auth-mode)               | [Single-user](#single-user-mode) | [Public](#public-mode)             | [Demo](#demo-mode)              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **A visitor gets**                                                                                             | The sign-in page                 | The admin's session              | A guest account, 24 h              | A guest account, 24 h           |
| **Register**                                                                                                   | unless [disabled](#registration) |                                  |                                    |                                 |
| **[SSO](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/index.md)**                           |                                  | Not used                         | a guest [signs in](#guest-sign-in) | At `/auth/login` only           |
| **Create projects**                                                                                            |                                  |                                  | Admins only                        | Admins only                     |
| **Duplicate a dashboard**                                                                                      |                                  |                                  | the copy expires with the guest    | the copy expires with the guest |
| **[Guided tours](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/web_ui/#guided-tours)**          | Builder chapters                 | Builder chapters                 | Guest chapter                      | Guest chapter                   |
| **[Landing card](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard-guide/#landing-hint)** |                                  |                                  |                                    | What's new line only            |

## Auth mode default

For teams and organizations: every visitor signs in, to an account of their own, and sees what their roles allow.

**Turn it on:** it is the mode whenever the other three are off. That is the Helm chart's default. The root `docker-compose.yaml` starts in single-user mode instead, so with Compose set `DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE=false` in `.env`. [Single sign-on](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/index.md) is optional, here with Google:

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_PROVIDERS='[{"id": "google", "label": "Sign in with Google", "discovery_url": "https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"}]'
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
DEPICTIO_AUTH_OIDC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-secret
```

```
oidc:
  providers:
    - id: google
      label: "Sign in with Google"
      discovery_url: "https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
secrets:
  oidcClients:
    google: {clientId: "<client-id>", clientSecret: "<client-secret>"}
```

SSO behind multiple workers

Since **v1.5.2** the OAuth CSRF state is shared through MongoDB, so sign-in works with any number of workers or replicas. On earlier versions the state was per-process and the callback only succeeded when it happened to reach the process that issued it. See [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#oauth-callback-security).

**Behavior:**

- Users register or are created by admins, unless [registration is disabled](#registration)
- A first SSO sign-in creates the account, under the same rule
- JWT-based authentication (RS256)
- Admin and regular users; owner, editor and viewer on each project and dashboard

## Single-user mode

For an instance only you use: there is no sign-in page, and every visitor is signed in as the admin.

**Turn it on:** with the root `docker-compose.yaml` it is already on. Otherwise:

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE=true
```

```
backend:
  env:
    DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE: "true"
```

**Behavior:**

- The session is the bootstrap admin's (`DEPICTIO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL`): whoever reaches the URL can do anything, so keep the instance on your machine or a private network
- Projects, dashboards and every admin page are available at once
- The sidebar shows *Single user mode*
- Provisioning and magic links are refused (403)
- Set together with public mode, single-user mode wins

## Public mode

For a public showcase: there is no sign-in page, and every visitor gets a guest account of their own.

**Turn it on:**

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE=true
# Optional: how long a guest account lives (default 24 hours, plus minutes)
DEPICTIO_AUTH_TEMPORARY_USER_EXPIRY_HOURS=24
DEPICTIO_AUTH_TEMPORARY_USER_EXPIRY_MINUTES=0
```

```
backend:
  env:
    DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE: "true"
    DEPICTIO_AUTH_TEMPORARY_USER_EXPIRY_HOURS: "24"
```

`DEPICTIO_AUTH_UNAUTHENTICATED_MODE=true` is still read as an alias. To ask visitors for a shared code first, add an [access code](#public-access-code).

**Behavior:**

- On the first page load, the viewer creates a guest account, `temp_user_<id>@depictio.temp`, and signs the visitor in with it: no modal, no shared anonymous user. The account and what it made are removed when it expires
- A guest reads the public dashboards and can duplicate one into a copy of their own, which expires with the account
- Creating a project, importing a dashboard or registering is refused (403) for anyone but an admin; admins and project editors can import (v1.21.0+)
- With an OpenID Connect provider enabled, a guest can [sign in](#guest-sign-in) to a persistent account
- A welcome card and a three-step [tour](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/web_ui/#guided-tours) of the dashboards list (v1.22.0+); on a dashboard, the [landing card](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard-guide/#landing-hint) points to its Guide (v1.17.4+)
- The sidebar shows a *Public Mode* badge
- Admins can create CLI tokens in **Profile** > **CLI agents** to refresh dashboards and ingest data without switching public mode off (v1.21.0+)

### Signing in as a guest (v1.17.3+)

When Google or another identity provider is configured, a guest finds **Sign in** where they would need it: the avatar menu, the sidebar's mode line (*Public mode · Sign in*), the profile page, the tour's welcome card and, when [viewers may comment](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/comments-annotations/#viewers-can-comment), the comments buttons, which open a *Sign in to comment* prompt. `/auth/login` shows the sign-in form with **Continue as guest**, and a sign-in returns to the page it started from. A public instance with password sign-in only behaves as before.

A public showcase where signed-in readers comment combines `DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE`, an identity provider and `DEPICTIO_COMMENTS_VIEWERS_CAN_COMMENT`. Keep [registration](#registration) open, or a first-time reader's account is never created.

## Demo mode

Public mode run as a read-only demo: the same guest accounts, without a prompt to sign in.

**Turn it on:** set both. Demo mode alone does not open the instance: without public mode, visitors meet the sign-in page.

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE=true
DEPICTIO_AUTH_DEMO_MODE=true
```

```
backend:
  env:
    DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE: "true"
    DEPICTIO_AUTH_DEMO_MODE: "true"
```

**Behavior:**

- Everything in public mode: guest accounts, the access code, the same guest tour
- Guests are never offered **Sign in**, even with an identity provider; an admin signs in at `/auth/login`
- No landing card introducing a dashboard, the tour does that job; it still appears with a What's new line when a dashboard changed since the last visit
- Monitoring is off even for an admin, and profile pictures cannot be changed
- The sidebar shows a *Demo Mode* badge

## Pipeline provisioning and magic links (v1.1.3+)

A pipeline often finishes before its owner has an account. Provisioning closes that gap: `depictio ingest <results dir> --user alice@example.org` creates-or-gets the account, runs as them, and prints a passwordless link to the dashboard it just imported.

Set the shared secret on the instance:

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_PROVISIONING_API_KEY=<a long random string>
```

**The provisioning endpoints are disabled while this is unset**, so an instance that never sets it cannot have accounts created this way. The CLI must present the same value, through `--provisioning-key` or the identically-named variable.

| Variable                                  | Default                                                                                                     | Description                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_PROVISIONING_API_KEY`      | unset                                                                                                       | Shared secret for `POST /depictio/api/v1/auth/provision_user`. Unset disables provisioning entirely. |
| `DEPICTIO_AUTH_MAGIC_LINK_EXPIRY_MINUTES` | see [reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#authentication) | How long a magic link stays redeemable.                                                              |

Treat the key like a password

Anyone holding it can create accounts on the instance. Keep it separate from `DEPICTIO_AUTH_INTERNAL_API_KEY` (alias `DEPICTIO_AUTH_INTERNAL_API_KEY_ENV`), whose scope is deliberately different. Pass it through a secret store rather than a shell history, and rotate it if a CI log ever captures it.

A magic link is single-use and expires; redeeming it exchanges the ticket for a normal session. Sending it to the user is the pipeline's job; Depictio only emits it on stdout.

## Restricting access

Three switches, all opt-in, all independent of the four modes above.

### Self-service registration

Set it on an instance where accounts are provisioned by an admin rather than claimed by whoever finds the URL:

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_REGISTRATION_DISABLED=true
```

**Behavior:**

- `POST /auth/register` returns 403, and the Register view and the link to it are hidden
- [OpenID Connect sign-in](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/index.md) becomes a login-only door: a known email signs in, an unknown one is refused instead of being provisioned an account
- Existing accounts, roles and permissions are untouched
- An administrator can still create accounts with [Add user](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/web_ui/#add-a-user) (v1.19.0+)

### Password sign-in (v1.8.2+)

Closes email and password sign-in so [single sign-on](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/index.md) is the only way in, for an instance whose accounts all come from one identity provider:

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_PASSWORD_LOGIN_DISABLED=true
```

**Behavior:**

- `POST /auth/login` refuses before reading any credential, so a valid password is not a way around the setting, and the sign-in card hides the form rather than showing one that always fails
- Ignored unless at least one OpenID Connect provider is enabled and configured, so forgetting the variables gives you the password form back instead of a locked instance
- Since v1.19.0 it also closes `POST /auth/register` (403), and the refusal says to use single sign-on
- `DEPICTIO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is no longer required: SSO matches the admin by email, so pointing `DEPICTIO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL` at your own address at the identity provider is what makes you the admin, with no seeded local account

### Public-mode access code (v1.8.2+)

Public mode hands a temporary session to anyone who loads the page. A code makes the instance link-shareable without being world-open:

```
DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE=true
DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CODE=your-shared-code
```

**Behavior:**

- A visitor enters the code before a temporary user is minted, and still gets their own throwaway account: it is a shared secret, not a login
- Checked in `/auth/public/create_temporary_user` after the rate limiter, so it is no more brute-forceable than any other credential there
- Ignored outside public and demo mode

On Kubernetes, the first two go under `backend.env` in your values file, and the access code under `secrets.publicAccessCode`, which keeps it in the Secret.

## Choosing a Mode

- **Just you**, on a laptop or a workstation: single-user mode, the default of the Docker Compose quick start.
- **A team** with accounts and roles: auth mode, the Helm chart's default.
- **A public gallery** of dashboards anyone can open: public mode.
- **A product demo** or a guided tutorial: demo mode.
