- [Configuration Guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/configuration/index.md): full environment variable reference
- [Environment Reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/index.md): all 160+ variables

# Picking a component from the catalog (v1.9.0+)

**Add component** opens a chooser with two routes:

- **New component** is the manual stepper: pick a type, connect it to data, configure it yourself. See [Dashboard Creation](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard_creation/index.md).
- **Pick from catalog** skips all of it and offers visualizations already built for the tool outputs Depictio found in this project.

The chooser, with a note that catalog suggestions come from the project's ingested data collections.

______________________________________________________________________

## Where the offers come from

Nothing is inferred from the data itself. Every entry in the [Tools Catalog](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/catalog/index.md) declares **how to recognise the file** and **which columns it must carry**, and Depictio compares your ingested data collections against those declarations. A project whose outputs match no entry simply has nothing to offer.

**Filename**

The collection's file matches the name the entry expects, such as `*.variants.tsv`.

**Path glob**

The collection's path matches the entry's glob, such as `**/ivar/*.tsv`. This is how a real pipeline run is recognised.

**Recipe**

The collection came from a [recipe](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/recipes/index.md) the entry declares. Derived collections carry no raw pipeline path, so neither of the other two can fire.

Any one of the three is enough to surface the tool. The entry's column schema then decides which of its renders are offered, so a render binding a column your file does not carry is never proposed.

MultiQC is a special case

Every `multiqc/*` output keys the same `multiqc.parquet`, so offers are narrowed to the sections the ingested report actually holds, and the originating tool is named on each one. The General Statistics offer adds the report's General Statistics table; before v1.16.0 it added the first plot of another module.

______________________________________________________________________

## The browser

Offers are grouped by tool on the left, one row per recognised output, with a coloured dot for each component type it can become. Selecting a row previews it on the right.

The preview is the real component, rendered in an iframe at the exact grid box it will occupy, so what you see is what lands on the dashboard.

iVar's variant calls, previewing as a lollipop plot.

**Add** saves it straight away. **Edit** drops it into the Design step first. Browser Back and Forward walk the picker's surfaces rather than leaving the flow.

______________________________________________________________________

## Narrowing the list

Search matches tool, output, description, file and collection at once, so `coverage` finds mosdepth's own outputs and the MultiQC coverage section together.

One search box across every field an offer carries.

**Filters** adds two facets with counts, **Component** and **Data collection**, computed against the current search rather than the whole catalog. A violet badge on the button says how many are active.

Two facets, each counted against what the search already narrowed.

______________________________________________________________________

## One output, several renders

Most recognised outputs support more than one visualization: iVar's variant calls can be drawn as a lollipop plot, an oncoplot, a Manhattan plot or a histogram. The tab strip switches between them, each render carrying its own configuration and its own grid box.

The same iVar output, switched to its Manhattan render.

Settings tuned inside the preview travel with the offer, on both the Add and the Edit path.

______________________________________________________________________

## Provenance

A component added from the catalog says so:

- a copyable `use: <tool>/<render-id>` snippet, the same identifier you would write in a project YAML;
- a `catalog_source` stamp carried through later edits and YAML import;
- a violet catalog action on the tile, opening a metadata inspector with identity, resolved configuration, data source, catalog origin and raw JSON.

______________________________________________________________________

## See also

- [Tools Catalog](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/catalog/index.md) to browse every tool and render outside a project
- [Dashboard Creation](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard_creation/index.md) for the manual stepper
- [Contributing a Tool](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/developer/contributing-a-tool/index.md) to add a tool to the catalog

# The dashboard Guide (v1.14.0+)

Every dashboard has a **Guide**: a short page on how to move around it, filter it and read its components. It is opened from the **Guide** entry at the bottom of the sidebar's tab list. It is not a walkthrough to click through once, but a page to come back to, and it is built from the dashboard it sits on: its tabs, its sections, its filters, its components.

______________________________________________________________________

## What it covers

Each part is a card with a short text, a live demo and a **Show me** button that rings the thing it is about inside the demo. A row of links at the top jumps to each part.

Parts come in this order, and a part shows only when the dashboard has what it covers.

| Part                              | What it shows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **About this Guide** (v1.22.0+)   | What the Guide is for: one part per thing you can do, live examples that change nothing, **Show me** and the way back                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Tabs**                          | The sidebar's own tab list, with its groups and the tab you are on. Pointing at a tab shows what it holds; clicking opens it                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Sections**                      | The tab's own sections (else pinned ones, or a sibling tab's), drawn by the dashboard itself: headers, folding, the numbers a folded section of cards still shows, **Collapse all**                                                                                                                    |
| **Filters**                       | A real card and filter from the dashboard. Picking a value changes the number without touching the dashboard's own filters                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Components**                    | Pick a kind: one of the dashboard's own components of it, from this tab or a sibling, with its full action row, so every icon can be tried. A kind the dashboard lacks shows a stand-in. *In the editor* adds the grip, the resize corner and the ⋮ menu, whose items only describe what they would do |
| **Analysis**                      | Select, save as a group and compare, overlaid or split, on the dashboard's own figure, table and card. See [Analysis](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/interactive-selection-filtering/#analysis-panel)                                                                        |
| **Genome**                        | The genome browser's menus and gestures, where the dashboard has one                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Label your samples** (v1.22.0+) | Only with a metadata table: a live demo of label columns on the dashboard's own table (nothing is saved) and a button that opens the [Metadata panel](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/metadata-panel/index.md)                                                                |
| **Comments** (v1.17.4+)           | Threads and annotations on one of the dashboard's own figures, through the real comment controls. It works without an account and writes nothing. See [Comments and Annotations](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/comments-annotations/index.md)                               |
| **Versions** (v1.17.4+)           | A component's real history, read-only for any reader (no **Restore**). A dashboard with no saved version gets a sample list. See [Component history](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/#component-history)                                                           |
| **What's new** (v1.22.0+)         | The changes since your last visit, in the real [What's new](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/whats-new/index.md) panel; with no change, how the header will announce one                                                                                                       |
| **Settings**                      | The reader's own page width and text size (*Settings → Your view*), and light or dark (the sidebar's sun / moon). **Show me what they do** plays them on the demo, then puts them back                                                                                                                 |

Everything the demos do stays in the Guide: no filter, group or setting of the dashboard changes.

______________________________________________________________________

## Landing card (v1.17.4+)

A reader who does not own the dashboard (a public-mode guest or a signed-in colleague) gets a small card under the *Powered by Depictio* credit on its main tab: what Depictio is, what this dashboard is, and a button to the Guide. Before v1.22.0 only public-mode guests saw it. It is remembered per dashboard, in this browser, and goes away with its close button or when the Guide is opened.

Since v1.22.0, when something changed since the reader's last visit, the card comes back, owner included, with a [What's new](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/whats-new/index.md) line naming the new runs; its button opens the What's new panel.

Demo mode keeps its tour of the dashboards list and gets no introduction. A dashboard with `show_guide: false` gets no card, and the card stays away while a [guided tour](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/web_ui/#guided-tours) runs and wherever tours are turned off (`DEPICTIO_WALKTHROUGH_DISABLED`, dev mode, `?no-walkthrough=1`).

______________________________________________________________________

## The address

The Guide opens as `?guide=1` on the tab it was opened from, so it can be bookmarked or shared. The tab stays loaded underneath: **Back to …** (at the top right and at the foot of the page), **Esc**, the browser's Back, or the tab or the **Guide** entry clicked again in the sidebar returns to it at once.

______________________________________________________________________

## For authors

The Guide is on by default for every dashboard. Two settings change it, set on the main tab for the whole dashboard, from **Settings → Guide** in the editor or in YAML:

| Key           | Default | Effect                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `show_guide`  | `true`  | `false` removes the Guide entry from the sidebar; a `?guide=1` link then opens the tab |
| `guide_intro` | `""`    | A markdown note shown at the top of the Guide, such as where to start reading          |

```
title: TREC Advanced Mobile Lab 2024
guide_intro: Start with **Key figures** on the Overview, then follow the tabs in order.
```

See also [Landing tabs](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#landing-tabs) for the authoring side of a dashboard's first page, and [Spotlight search](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/spotlight-search/index.md) for finding one component.

# Dashboard Creation

## Video example

A new dashboard on the nf-core/ampliseq project: **New dashboard**, then **Edit**, a card with the median Shannon diversity, a box plot of Shannon diversity per habitat, and **Save**.

[![](../../../images/guides/dashboard_creation/create-dashboard.webp)](../../../images/guides/dashboard_creation/create-dashboard.mp4)

## Add a component to the dashboard

### Step 1: Component Selection

1. Open a dashboard in edit mode, then **Add** > **Component** > **New component**.
1. Pick a component type: **Figure**, **Card**, **Interactive**, **Table**, **MultiQC**, **Image**, **Map**, **Text** or **Advanced viz**. Clicking a card takes you straight to the next step.

Or skip the stepper entirely (v1.9.0+)

**Add** > **Component** opens a chooser first. Alongside **New component**, which is the flow described here, **Pick from catalog** offers pre-configured visualizations that Depictio recognised in the project's ingested data. See [Picking a component from the catalog](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/catalog-picker/index.md).

### Step 2: Data Selection

1. Choose the **data collection** from the dropdown.

1. Check **Data Collection Information**: type, row and column counts, Delta table version, and the column preview underneath.

1. Click **Next Step**.

   The first compatible data collection is pre-selected, so you only touch the dropdown when you need another one. Here it is `alpha_diversity_multi_canonical`, one row per sample with its diversity indices. **Text** components skip this step entirely, since they read no data collection.

   The **Selected Component** badge at the top of the step names the type you picked in step 1. Before v1.6.0 the MultiQC badge rendered white on white and read as an empty row.

### Step 3: Customize Your Component

1. **Customise your component**:

   - For **Figure** components, you can select the type of figure (e.g., scatter plot, histogram) and customize its appearance.
   - For **Interactive** components, you can set up interactive elements like sliders or dropdowns to allow users to filter or manipulate the data dynamically.
   - For **Card** components, you can display key metrics of your data.

All options are dependent on the type of column in your data collection. For example, if you select a `numeric` column, you can choose to between a **Slider** or a **RangeSlider** for interactive components, and metrics like **Mean**, **Median**, or **Standard Deviation** for card components. If you select a `string` column, you can choose to display the **Select/Multiselect** or a **SegmentedControl** for interactive components, and metrics like **Count** or **Unique Count** for card components.

| Data Type | Interactive Options                   | Card Metrics                                    |
| --------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Numeric   | Slider, RangeSlider                   | Mean, Median, Standard Deviation, Variance, ... |
| String    | Select, Multiselect, SegmentedControl | Count, Unique Count, Most Frequent (mode)       |

1. **Set additional parameters**:

1. For **Figure** components, you can tweak visualization settings such as colors, axis labels, and bin sizes. Settings are categorised in the following way:

   - **Core parameters**: Define key parameters such as **X-axis** and **Y-axis** and **Color**, and assign the relevant data columns from your dataset.
   - **Styling & Layout**: Adjust the layout of the figure, including titles and axis labels, colors, hover data, and more.
   - **Figure type specific options**: Access additional options specific to the figure type, such as **scatter plot** or **histogram** settings.
   - **Advanced**: For advanced users, additional settings can be configured here like facetting, animation and more.

1. For **Interactive** components, you can set adjust sliders to have a given number of marks, use a linear or logarithmic scale.

   Two panels sit at the end of that list, both folded and both optional (v1.6.0+):

   - **Placement** — which [section](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#sections) the component joins. It appears only once the dashboard has sections; you can also move a placed component later, from its own menu on the dashboard.
   - **Performance** — for figures, **Max points**, the point count above which a scatter-family figure downsamples. Leave it blank for the global default; viewers can still load every point on demand.

   Since **v1.14.0** every builder lays its form out in collapsible sections, each headed by an icon, a title and a one-line subtitle. The sections holding what the component cannot work without open every time; the others reopen as you left them, per builder type, in this browser. The preview draws in the dashboard's brand (a child tab's in its main tab's).

1. **Finalize Customization**:

1. Review the component preview and ensure all settings are accurate.

1. Once complete, click **Next Step** to proceed to the final stage.

### Previewing with active filters (v1.5.2+)

When the dashboard already has filters applied, the component builder previews the **filtered** data rather than the whole data collection. Before v1.5.2 the builder always showed the unfiltered dataset, and returning to the dashboard reset the grid.

Take the nf-core/ampliseq Alpha Diversity tab with its Shannon diversity filter raised to 6.58, which drops the three Groundwater samples. The cards summarise the 9 samples left, not all 12:

*No filter: a median Shannon of 7.70 over 12 samples. From 6.58 up: 8.63 over 9.*

Open the builder from there and the design step carries that filter, with a banner naming how many filters are active:

The table holds only the 9 samples left, not the collection's 12.

**Apply to preview** is on by default. Switch it off to preview the full dataset, which matters when a narrow filter would otherwise leave you designing against an empty table:

The toggle only affects the preview

Whichever way you leave it, the saved component always follows the dashboard's live filters. The toggle is a design-time convenience, not a property of the component.

Save, and the new component arrives already filtered, with no flash of unfiltered data on the way, and the filters you had set are still applied:

The banner appears only when at least one filter is active, and is suppressed for **Text** and **MultiQC** components, which have no notion of row filtering.

### Figure Code Mode (v0.6.0+)

The **Figure** component includes a **Code Mode** for advanced users who want to write custom Python/Plotly code to generate visualizations. This provides maximum flexibility for complex or custom figures.

#### Accessing Code Mode

1. In the Figure design interface, click the **"Code"** tab
1. Switch from **UI Mode** to **Code Mode** at any time
1. Switching from UI to Code Mode automatically generates code from your current UI settings

#### Available Variables

In Code Mode, the following variables are pre-loaded:

| Variable | Description                                     |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `df`     | Your data as a Polars DataFrame                 |
| `px`     | Plotly Express for quick visualizations         |
| `pd`     | Pandas for data manipulation                    |
| `pl`     | Polars for high-performance data operations     |
| `go`     | Plotly Graph Objects for detailed customization |

#### Code Structure

Your code must follow this structure:

```
# Optional: any number of preprocessing statements
threshold = 0.5
keep = ["alpha", "beta"]
df_modified = (
    df.filter(pl.col("value") > threshold)
      .filter(pl.col("category").is_in(keep))
)

# Required: create the figure using px or go
fig = px.scatter(df_modified, x="col_x", y="col_y", color="category")

# Optional: post-figure customization
fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
```

Everything before the `fig =` statement counts as preprocessing, whatever the variables are called, and a statement may span several lines: parentheses and brackets are both tracked, so `agg([` continues across a line break just as `agg(` does.

Changed in v1.8.3

Preprocessing used to be recognised by variable *name*: a line had to mention `df_modified` or start with `df_`, and every other line was silently discarded. The figure then ran without it and failed on the first name it could no longer resolve, pointing at the `fig =` line rather than at the dropped one.

Code Constraints

- The final `fig` variable must be a Plotly Figure object
- The figure must use something the preprocessing produced, or `df` itself
- Only the pre-loaded libraries are available for security

#### Code Mode Features

- **Live Preview**: Click "Execute Code" to preview your figure instantly
- **Syntax Highlighting**: Python syntax highlighting with the Ace editor
- **Theme Support**: Editor theme follows the dashboard light/dark mode
- **Resizable Editor**: Drag the editor border to adjust panel size
- **Error Messages**: Clear error feedback for syntax and execution issues

#### Component design Examples:

##### Figure design - scatter plot - UI mode

`faith_pd` against sequencing `depth`, coloured by `habitat`, from `alpha_rarefaction_summary`. The preview redraws on every change.

##### Figure design - scatter plot - code mode

Switching to Code Mode carries the UI settings over as a `px.scatter` call, which you can then take past what the form exposes: here, marginal violins and a `fig.update_layout()` override.

##### Interactive design - RangeSlider example

##### Card design - metrics selection

## MultiQC Integration

A MultiQC component draws one plot of a MultiQC report: the report's own controls stay, and the dashboard filters apply on top. Reports are added in the browser (**Add data**, or **Manage data** on a MultiQC collection) or with `depictio ingest`. See [MultiQC](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/multiqc/index.md) for the whole feature.

### Adding MultiQC Components

1. Pick **MultiQC** in Step 1. The data collection dropdown then narrows to the MultiQC collections of your project, so Step 2 is usually already filled in.
1. In Step 3, choose a **Module**, then a **Plot** inside it. Both lists are read from the report itself. For an nf-core/ampliseq run that means `General Stats Table`, `cutadapt` and `fastqc`. The preview renders on the right as soon as you pick.
1. Repeat for every plot you want: each one becomes its own component, and they can sit in different sections or tabs.

MultiQC data collections show no data preview in Step 2 because they aren't tabular, so `Rows` and `Columns` read `N/A`.

The General Statistics table keeps its **Mean / R1 / R2 / All** read selector and its **Table / Violin** toggle. To filter MultiQC plots from a metadata table, link them with the `sample_mapping` resolver ([Link to sample metadata](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/multiqc/#link-to-sample-metadata)). To compare the reports of several runs, see [MultiQC: compare runs](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/multiqc/#compare-runs).

# Using a dashboard

A dashboard opens in view mode, where you filter, read and comment. Its owner switches to edit mode to change it. Labels below are those of the default Paper look, with **Search**, **Comments**, **Analysis** and **Edit** in the dock; the Classic look has the same buttons in its header. See [Paper and Classic](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/web_ui/#looks). For what each part does in depth, see [Layout, tabs and sharing](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/index.md).

## As a viewer

### Move around

- **Tabs** sit in the sidebar, folded to an icon rail while the filter panel is open.
- **Search** (**⌘K** / **Ctrl+K**) finds a component on any tab. See [Spotlight search](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/spotlight-search/index.md).
- The **Guide**, when the author turned it on, walks you through the dashboard. See [The dashboard Guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard-guide/index.md).

### Filter

- The **filter panel** holds the dashboard's filters in foldable sections. Collapse it to a rail that still counts the active filters, or resize it by its edge; both are remembered across tabs.
- The summary above the controls lists each active filter, with a clear button per row. **Reset** clears every filter on this tab.
- A section with a pin is shared by every tab and keeps its values when you switch. See [Sections on every tab](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#persistent-sections).
- Selecting points on a scatter plot, rows in a table or an area on a map filters the other components too. **Reset selection** on the tile clears it. See [Selection filtering](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/interactive-selection-filtering/index.md).

### Use the map panel

A map authored as a dashboard-wide panel follows you across tabs. Its header control docks, floats or hides it. Lasso, box or click on it to filter every tab, and open the rows behind it from its header.

### Read a tile

Hover a tile for its actions:

- **About this component**: what it shows and how to read it, as its author wrote it. A tile with a title has it beside the title.
- **Data source and settings**: its type, data source and configuration, with the code to copy.
- **Toggle fullscreen**, **Download CSV** on a table, **Inspect**, and **Export / embed** to put the tile on another website (see [Export and embedding](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/component-export/index.md)).

### Wait for a large dashboard

Tiles load as they scroll into view, and a ring with a count such as `6/8` beside the title tracks those on screen. Large collections arrive reduced, and say so:

- A figure shows a badge such as `9,900 / 12,011,000 pts`. **Load all** fetches every point.
- A table pages its rows. Past about a million rows, sorting is off.
- An advanced visualization computed from a sample carries an orange **estimated** badge.

See [Performance & Scaling](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/performance/index.md) for the thresholds.

### Discuss and compare

| Button       | What it does                                                                 | More                                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Comments** | Threads on a tile or a tab, and annotations drawn on charts, tables and maps | [Comments and annotations](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/comments-annotations/index.md)             |
| **Analysis** | Save selections as groups, then colour or split every figure by them         | [Selection groups](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/interactive-selection-filtering/#selection-groups) |
| **Metadata** | The sample table beside the dashboard, with your own label columns           | [Metadata panel](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/metadata-panel/index.md)                             |

From a project's **Runs** tab, **Compare** opens a dashboard with one run's changes marked. See [Runs and run comparison](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/runs/index.md).

### Catch up on what changed

The **What's new** key in the header counts the changes since your last visit: new data, edited components, new comments. Its panel shows them on the figures with **Off**, **Overlay** or **Split**, and **Before | Now** draws one tile as it was and as it is. The **Notifications** bell lists every dashboard and project that changed. See [What's new](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/whats-new/index.md).

### Keep your filters

A dashboard reopens on the filters you left, in any browser you sign in to: panel filters, chart and map selections, table rows. **Settings → Filters → Remember my filters** turns this off for one dashboard. Anonymous visitors keep their filters in this browser only. **Reset** also clears what is remembered.

### Share a filtered view

The address bar carries the view as `#filters=…`. Copy it from there, from the link icon beside **N filters active**, or with the copy button of **Share this view** in **Settings → Filters**. Opening such a link applies its filters on top of yours.

Which filters win when a dashboard opens

Three sources merge, each overriding the one before: the remembered filters, the selections carried across tabs, then the link. A `?version=` preview neither restores nor remembers anything.

### Change your view and settings

**Settings** opens **Dashboard settings**, a dialog with a rail of sections. Changes save as you make them.

| Section                                               | Shown                                                                                                        | What it holds                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **About this dashboard**                              | Always                                                                                                       | Project, template, owner and visibility, the **Run parameters**, **View ingestion report** and the IDs under **Identifiers**                                                   |
| **Your view**                                         | Always                                                                                                       | **Font size** (85% to 130%) and **Page width** (Full, Wide, Comfortable, Compact), for you, in this browser                                                                    |
| **Filters**                                           | View mode                                                                                                    | **Remember my filters** and the filter link                                                                                                                                    |
| **Tab defaults**, **Tiles**, **Filtering**, **Guide** | Edit mode                                                                                                    | Saved with the dashboard. See [Settings for everyone](#settings-for-everyone)                                                                                                  |
| **Branding**                                          | Edit mode                                                                                                    | Logo, colours and figure palette. See [Brand the dashboard](#appearance)                                                                                                       |
| **History**                                           | Edit mode                                                                                                    | Every saved version, to preview, restore or bookmark. See [History](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/#history)                              |
| **Data version**                                      | Edit mode                                                                                                    | The dashboard drawn from earlier data, for you only, until you reload. See [Data versions](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/#data-versions) |
| **Feedback**                                          | With a [feedback link](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#feedback) | Report a problem or suggest an improvement                                                                                                                                     |

## As an editor

### Edit and save

- **Edit** opens the editor on a dashboard you own. On someone else's, its tooltip suggests duplicating it to get your own copy.
- **Add → Component** opens the builder and **Add → Section** adds a section. See [Dashboard creation](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard_creation/index.md).
- Changes save on their own about half a second after you stop. **Save** writes at once and refreshes the dashboard's thumbnail.
- Each save is a version: automatic saves fold into one per 5 minutes of editing, and **Save** always records its own. See [Versions and history](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/index.md).
- **Exit Edit** returns to view mode.

### Arrange tiles

Move a tile by **Drag to move**, and resize it by its edges and corners. Its menu holds:

| Item                                           | What it does                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Edit**                                       | Reopens the builder on this tile                                                                                                                                                |
| **History**                                    | The tile across saved versions, to compare or restore it alone. See [Component history](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/#component-history) |
| **Duplicate**, **Move to section**, **Delete** | What they say                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Copy to tab…**                               | Adds a copy to another tab. See [Copy to tab](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#copy-to-tab)                                                 |
| **Highlight on…**                              | Shows a figure on another tab without copying it. See [Highlight components](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/components/#highlight-components)         |
| **Font size**                                  | A figure's own font scale, 0.7× to 2×                                                                                                                                           |
| **Reset to auto height**                       | On a tile resized by hand that could fit its content                                                                                                                            |

### Describe a tile

A component's `description` fills the subtitle under its title and **About this component**. The first paragraph is the lead; a paragraph that opens with `How to read:`, `Annotations:`, `Note:`, `Warning:` or `Source:` becomes a block, a callout or the footer.

```
description: |
  Which lineages make up the community? Each dot is one phylum.

  How to read: a large dot is a dominant phylum.

  Note: with more than 3,000 ASVs, the tree keeps the 3,000 most abundant.
```

### Settings for everyone

In edit mode, these sections of **Settings** are saved with the dashboard for every reader:

| Section          | What it holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Tab defaults** | What this tab opens with: page width, filter panel open or collapsed, **Show the tab's name**. A reader's own choice wins. See [Tab defaults](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#tab-defaults) |
| **Tiles**        | **Fit tiles to their content**, and **Advanced viz controls** as *Popover*, *Under title* or *Side rail*. See [Tile height](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/yaml-sync/#tile-height)                     |
| **Filtering**    | **Funnel filtering by default**                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Guide**        | **Show the Guide** and its **Introduction**. See [The dashboard Guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard-guide/index.md)                                                                    |

### Brand the dashboard

**Settings → Branding → Customise** gives this dashboard its own logo, colours, fonts and figure palette inside the instance's brand. Fields left empty follow the instance, and a child tab follows its main tab (**Inherit main tab**). A **Preview** renders real components in light and dark.

An uploaded logo stays on this instance and is left out of YAML exports; use `logo_url` for one that has to travel. See [Branding](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/branding/index.md).

# Real-time Events

Real-time events let a dashboard **refresh itself over a WebSocket** the moment the data behind it changes, with no manual reload and no polling. When new data is ingested into a data collection, subscribed dashboards refetch and re-render automatically: new rows appear, figures recompute, and updated items briefly highlight.

This makes Depictio suitable for **live feeds**: an instrument streaming acquisitions, a pipeline emitting results batch by batch, or any process that keeps appending to a data collection.

The *Adaptive Feedback Microscopy* dashboard part-way through a run. The status pill sits at the right of the header; the acquisition window scrubber is pinned in the footer.

Built with the ALMF at EMBL

This dashboard was designed together with the Advanced Light Microscopy Facility at EMBL, on top of [**SVLT** (Serving Vision to Living Things)](https://git.embl.org/grp-almf/svlt): on-demand computer vision that segments each acquired image into RoiSets and classifies every object while the experiment is still running. SVLT posts each batch of phenotypes to Depictio, which is what the dashboard above is reacting to.

______________________________________________________________________

## Video example

🎬 **Real-time events in action:** a virtual-microscopy simulator streams acquisitions into a live dashboard

In this recording, a virtual-microscopy acquisition simulator stands in for the instrument. Each acquisition is segmented and pushed to Depictio through `/deltatables/upsert`, which broadcasts an event on the WebSocket. The dashboard on the left is open the whole time and is never reloaded: it refetches on every broadcast, so its figures and cards keep up with the acquisitions streaming in the terminal on the right.

______________________________________________________________________

## How it works

The refresh is driven entirely by data ingestion. There is no separate "push" API to call:

Any producer that re-ingests or upserts a data collection triggers this. The CLI does it on every `depictio ingest`, and an external instrument or pipeline can do the same by POSTing to the `/deltatables/upsert` endpoint.

______________________________________________________________________

## Enable it

Real-time refresh activates only when **all** of the following hold.

### 1. Turn the system on (server)

Set the master switch and make sure a Redis instance is reachable (events are fanned out to viewers via Redis pub/sub):

```
DEPICTIO_EVENTS_ENABLED=true
```

The most relevant variables:

| Variable                      | Default | Purpose                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_EVENTS_ENABLED`     | `false` | Master switch; nothing happens until this is `true` |
| `DEPICTIO_EVENTS_REDIS_HOST`  | `redis` | Redis host used for pub/sub                         |
| `DEPICTIO_EVENTS_DEBOUNCE_MS` | `1000`  | Coalesce bursts of rapid updates (ms)               |

See the [Environment Variables Reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#real-time-events) for the full `DEPICTIO_EVENTS_*` list (Redis port/password/db, WebSocket heartbeat and timeout, change streams).

### 2. Opt the project in

Real-time is **opt-in per project**. Add a top-level `realtime` block to the project's `project.yaml`:

```
realtime:
  enabled: true
  debounce_ms: 500   # optional; overrides the server default for this project
```

Projects without this block never open a WebSocket, and their dashboards show no live indicator.

### 3. Open the dashboard

Open any dashboard in an opted-in project. A **real-time indicator** appears in the header and turns green once the viewer has subscribed. From then on the dashboard updates on its own whenever the underlying data collection is re-ingested.

The indicator sits at the far right of the header, past *Edit* and *Settings*.

It reads *Connecting…* while the socket opens, **Live** once subscribed, and *Offline* if the connection drops. An orange dot on the icon marks an update you have not taken yet.

______________________________________________________________________

## Following the stream

Click the indicator to open the **Live updates** menu.

Refresh mode and pause sit above the event log. Each row is one broadcast: local arrival time, row delta, data collection tag, operation and aggregation version.

- **Auto-refresh on update**: on, the dashboard silently refetches on every event. Off, an event only raises a notification and the orange dot, and you refresh when you are ready. Useful when you are reading a figure and don't want it moving under you.
- **Receiving events / Paused**: pausing stops updates from being applied but keeps the socket open, so nothing is missed from the log.
- **Event log**: the last 50 events, newest first. It lives in the browser's local storage, so it survives a reload; **Reset** empties it.

Hover a log row for the whole event.

The hover card carries the project and data collection, the row count before and after, the Delta and aggregation versions, a sample of the ids that arrived, and the raw payload.

### Re-highlighting a batch

Rows glow briefly as they land, then fade. The highlight button on a log row brings that batch back: every component bound to the collection re-lights exactly the rows that event added, and keeps them lit until you choose another batch or select **Clear highlight**.

The pinned batch of 293 cells, ringed in yellow across every figure bound to the collection. The source row stays marked in the log, and *Clear highlight* appears next to *Reset*.

The button only appears on events that carry a list of added ids. The first commit of a collection has nothing to diff against, so there is no batch to pin.

______________________________________________________________________

## Scoping to an acquisition window

A dashboard that tracks a stream usually places its timeline component in the footer, where it spans the full width below both the filter panel and the components and stays visible as the page scrolls (v1.2.2+).

Every mark on the track is one acquisition timestamp. The buttons on the right change tick spacing and label format only.

Drag either handle to narrow the window and every component re-renders against the selection. The `Year … Min` buttons do not change the selection itself.

______________________________________________________________________

## Driving updates

Once enabled, any of these will move a live dashboard:

- **Re-ingest with the CLI**: `depictio ingest --project-config-path <project.yaml> --update-config` refreshes the project in place: it re-scans and upserts the data collection, which broadcasts the refresh, and keeps the dashboards as edited in the viewer. See [Refreshing a project](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#refreshing-a-project).
- **An external producer**: an instrument or pipeline that POSTs new data to the `/deltatables/upsert` API endpoint (with a valid token) triggers the same path. This is the intended integration point for a live experimental feed, and how SVLT feeds the dashboard above.
- **A pipeline that ingests itself** (v1.10.0+): a Nextflow `workflow.onComplete` handler runs the CLI on the output directory when the run finishes. With `--depictio_attach true`, each new run of the pipeline moves the dashboard with no one at a keyboard. See [Nextflow trigger](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/workflows/nextflow/trigger/#running-it-again).

### Try it locally

The bundled `adapt_feedb_ms` demo project ships with the `realtime` block already set and a small synthetic driver that needs no extra dependencies, just the CLI and a token:

```
cd depictio/projects/test/adapt_feedb_ms
./stream_test.sh reset       # seed a couple of rows and ingest
./stream_test.sh stream 3    # append one row every 3s until Ctrl+C
```

Open the project's dashboard and watch each tick land live: new gallery items, recomputed cards, and a moving timeline, with no manual refresh.

______________________________________________________________________

## Requirements & notes

- **Redis** is required for pub/sub when events are enabled.
- **MongoDB change streams** (`DEPICTIO_EVENTS_MONGODB_CHANGE_STREAMS_ENABLED`, on by default) require MongoDB to run as a **replica set**.
- **Reverse proxy**: the WebSocket route `/depictio/api/v1/events/ws` needs the HTTP upgrade proxied. If you front Depictio with nginx, forward the `Upgrade` and `Connection` headers on that path, and allow `connect-src 'self' ws: wss:` in your Content-Security-Policy.
- **Authentication**: the WebSocket carries its JWT as a `token` query parameter (browsers can't set `Authorization` headers on WS connections) and is permission-checked against the dashboard's project at viewer level before any events are delivered.

# Spotlight search (v1.14.0+)

A dashboard with a dozen tabs of thirty components each used to mean opening tabs until the right plot showed up. **⌘K** on a Mac, **Ctrl+K** elsewhere, or the magnifier in the header, opens a search across every component of every tab of the dashboard. Picking a result takes you to that component.

______________________________________________________________________

## What it searches

The search reads what the dashboard already says about itself:

- tab names, descriptions and the sidebar group they sit under;
- component titles, subtitles, captions and descriptions;
- type and chart-kind labels (*filter*, *card*, *phylogenetic*, *sankey*), and a MultiQC panel's module and plot;
- the columns a component binds;
- the prose of text tiles, without its markdown;
- section names.

Every word typed must be found; case and accents are ignored. A word is found where a field starts with it, then where one of its words does, then anywhere inside it, though a word of one or two letters only counts at the start of a word. A hit in a title ranks above the same hit in a text body. There is no typo tolerance: a misspelt word finds nothing rather than a list of near misses.

In the editor, the tab you are on is searched with its unsaved changes. The other tabs are fetched the first time the search opens, and only those you can open.

______________________________________________________________________

## Results

Results are grouped by tab: the tab you are on first, marked **This tab**, then the others in sidebar order. Tabs are results too, and an empty field lists them, as a tab switcher. Each row shows a type icon (MultiQC panels wear the MultiQC logo), the title with the match highlighted, a dimmed *tab · section · snippet* line and, on the right, what it is (*Card*, *Filter*, *Sunburst*, *Tab*). **↑** and **↓** move, **Enter** opens, **Esc** or **⌘K** / **Ctrl+K** again closes, and a middle-click or ⌘/Ctrl-click opens a result in a new browser tab. A tab shows at most eight matches, then *N more in this tab — add a word to narrow it down*. Reopening the search keeps the last query, selected.

______________________________________________________________________

## Where it lands

1. Whatever hides the component opens first: the [Guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard-guide/index.md), a folded section, a filter group, the collapsed filter panel, a [section shown on every tab](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#persistent-sections), or the filter drawer on a phone.
1. The page scrolls to the component and rings it for a moment. If a tile above it grows meanwhile, the page scrolls once more to correct.

A result on another tab opens that tab with `?component=` in the address, which the tab acts on and then removes. A component this tab also shows, such as one in a section pinned from another tab, is landed on in place. Picking a tab opens it; picking the tab you are on scrolls back to its top. In the editor, pending changes are saved before leaving the tab; if the save fails, you stay on the tab and a notification says so.

Search works in view mode, in edit mode and on public dashboards. The shortcut is ignored while you type in a field or in the code editor.

Known limit

A filter folded under a filter bar's **More filters**, or a map panel the reader has hidden, is not uncovered. You get a *That component is not on screen* notice instead.

# Unauthenticated Mode

Renamed to Public Mode

This page describes the legacy "Unauthenticated Mode" which has been renamed to **Public Mode**. The env var `DEPICTIO_AUTH_UNAUTHENTICATED_MODE` still works as a backward-compatible alias. See [Authentication Modes](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/authentication-modes/index.md) for the full overview of all four modes.

## Overview

### What is Unauthenticated Mode?

Each visitor lands on the **Dashboards** page with a temporary guest account, created without a form. The sidebar reads **Public mode**. A guest sees the public dashboards and can use their filters and figures. The account expires after `DEPICTIO_AUTH_TEMPORARY_USER_EXPIRY_HOURS`.

Earlier versions first landed a visitor as a shared anonymous user, with a modal to switch to a temporary account. That step is gone: every visitor gets a temporary account at once.

Example unauthenticated mode URL is available on documentation landing page: <https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/>.

## Screenshots

**Account settings** shows the guest's temporary account: a `temp_user_…@depictio.temp` email and the **User** role.

`/auth/login` opens the sign-in form with **Continue as guest**, to sign in with an account or keep the guest session.

## Configuration

### Environment Variables

Enable unauthenticated mode by setting these environment variables:

```
# Enable public mode (DEPICTIO_AUTH_UNAUTHENTICATED_MODE=true still works)
DEPICTIO_AUTH_PUBLIC_MODE=true

# Configure anonymous user settings
DEPICTIO_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_USER_EMAIL=anonymous@depict.io
DEPICTIO_AUTH_TEMPORARY_USER_EXPIRY_HOURS=24
```

### Helm Deployment

For Kubernetes deployments, use the provided values files:

```
# Deploy with unauthenticated mode
helm upgrade --install your-release ./helm-charts/depictio \
  -f ./helm-charts/depictio/values.yaml \
  -f ./helm-charts/depictio/values-unauth.yaml \
  -n your-namespace
```

## Limitations

- **Session-Based**: Data and dashboards expire after configured time
- **No Persistence**: User data is not permanently stored
- **No User Management**: No user accounts, groups, or permissions
- **Temporary Storage**: All content is ephemeral

## Use Cases

### Scientific Outreach and Demonstrations

- Public sharing of dashboards
- Public demos and presentations

### Educational Use

- Training sessions
- Workshops and tutorials
- Proof-of-concept deployments

## Security Considerations

- **Public Access**: Anyone can access the deployment
- **Data Sensitivity**: Only use with non-sensitive, public data (e.g., public & published datasets ; data powering the visualizations could be extracted from the dashboard by scrapping the page)
- **Resource Limits**: Configure appropriate resource constraints
- **Network Security**: Use proper network isolation and ingress controls

# Web UI

## Paper and Classic (v1.17.0+)

Depictio comes in two looks, with the same pages, panels and settings:

- **Paper**, the default since v1.17.0: every page on paper panels, a top bar with the page or dashboard title, and a sidebar. On a dashboard, the tab sidebar folds to an icon rail, by itself while the filter panel is open, and a floating **dock** holds Search, Analysis, Comments and Edit / Save / Exit as icon keys. Drag it by its grip, or use the arrow keys, to the bottom, left, right or top of the page; the browser keeps the place.
- **Classic**, the layout of earlier versions: a header bar of buttons and a tab sidebar.

A page takes the first of:

1. `?chrome=glass` (Paper) or `?chrome=base` (Classic) in its URL, kept for the rest of the browser session, for support and testing;
1. your own pick, in [**Account settings → Preferences → Look**](#account-settings), kept in this browser;
1. the default an administrator sets in [**Administration → Branding → Default look**](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/branding/#default-look);
1. Paper.

Screenshots in these docs show one look or the other; where a control sits in the header in Classic, Paper has it in the top bar or the dock.

## Register and login

### Registering an Account (Sign Up)

1. On the **Sign in** page, click **Create an account**.
1. Enter your **Email**, a **Password**, and the same password again in **Confirm password**.
1. Click **Create account**. **Already have an account? Sign in** goes back to the sign-in form.

### Logging In (Sign In)

1. Open the **Sign in** page.
1. Enter your **Email** and **Password**. The eye icon shows the password as you type.
1. Click **Sign in**. You land on the **Dashboards** page (`/dashboards`).

### Single sign-on login

An instance with [OpenID Connect single sign-on](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/index.md) shows one button per identity provider (for example *Sign in with Google* or the label the administrator set). It sends you to the provider and back. If the account does not exist, it is created automatically, unless registration is closed.

When the server refuses the sign-in, for example because registration is closed or the provider did not verify your email, the page shows **Sign-in failed** and the reason.

## Landing page / Dashboards section (/dashboards)

The listing opens on the **Table** view (v1.12.0+), one row per dashboard. In the **Thumbnails** view each dashboard is shown as a card. Cards display the dashboard's screenshot thumbnail once one has been captured, and fall back to the dashboard's logo (when set) before the generic placeholder.

The table view has a **Last viewed** column (v1.11.0+), sorted newest first, with dashboards you never opened last. It is kept per browser.

The **Table display** menu (v1.17.0+) sets the row height, **Comfortable** or **Compact**, and which columns show, with **Show all** and **Reset**. The Projects listing has the same menu. On a narrow screen the actions column stays pinned to the right edge while the table scrolls (v1.17.3+).

Dashboards are grouped into sections, each dashboard in one only, in this order: **nf-core dashboards**, **Demo dashboards**, **Public**, **Accessed** and **Owned**. Since v1.17.2 the nf-core section holds every dashboard of an nf-core workflow, the imported templates included: the seeded ones first, then the others by title.

#### Thumbnails or table (v1.11.2+)

The view switcher in the toolbar picks between **Thumbnails**, the card grid, and **Table**, with sortable columns and bulk selection. The Tiles view of earlier versions is gone, and a browser that had it opens on Thumbnails.

In Thumbnails, the **Card display** menu beside the switcher sets:

- **Cards per row**: 5 by default since v1.12.0, or 2 to 6, or Auto. Auto never makes more columns than a section has cards, so a section with a single dashboard draws it across the whole width.
- **Badges**: which of Project, Template, Owner, Visibility, Last modified and Tabs a card shows. Hovering a badge gives its long form.

**Reset to defaults** restores both, so five cards per row. They are layout preferences, kept in the browser and left out of shared links. A browser that opened the listing before v1.12.0 stored Auto, the former default, and keeps it until you pick another value or reset. Resting the pointer on a thumbnail opens a larger, sharper preview.

Someone who never picked a view gets the one the deployment sets with [`DEPICTIO_VIEWER_DASHBOARDS_DEFAULT_VIEW`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#react-viewer-frontend): **Table** since v1.12.0, Thumbnails before. Set it to `thumbnails` to open the grid again. A view picked in the browser, or named by a shared link such as `/dashboards?view=thumbnails`, wins over it.

### Sidebar Navigation

The left sidebar provides easy access to various sections of the application. This includes:

- **Dashboards**: View and manage your dashboards.
- **Projects**: Manage your projects and data collections.
- **Administration** (sysadmin users only): Access administrative features (only available to users with admin privileges).
- **About**: Information about the application and its repository.

The button at the top of the sidebar folds it to icons. The top bar holds the theme toggle and your avatar, which opens [Account settings](#account-settings) (v1.17.0+). The compass in the header of the Dashboards and Projects pages starts the [tour](#guided-tours) of the page (*Take the tour of this page*; *Take the tour* for a guest).

#### Guided tours (v1.22.0+)

Tours are short cards beside the page: nothing is dimmed, the control they describe is ringed, and the arrow keys and **Esc** move through them. A first visit to the Dashboards or Projects list opens a welcome card; for a builder it offers three journeys: *Explore a dashboard*, *Bring in a pipeline's results* and *Build a dashboard*. Each page then has one short chapter (Dashboards, Projects, the editor, the component builder), offered once on first arrival and never started on its own; a guest gets a three-step Dashboards chapter. A dashboard has no chapter: its [landing card](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard-guide/#landing-hint) and [Guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard-guide/index.md) do that job. Seen chapters are remembered in this browser. When the deployment turns tours off ([`DEPICTIO_WALKTHROUGH_DISABLED`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#global-settings)), the compass stays, disabled, with *Guided tours are turned off on this deployment*.

#### Server information (v1.17.0+)

The server status at the foot of the sidebar, **Online** with the server version, opens the server information: version, API, mode, and links to the documentation, GitHub, the releases and the issue tracker. On a dashboard it sits at the foot of the tab rail, and in Classic it is the version badge.

For administrators, its last line says whether a newer Depictio release is out. When one is, a dot marks the status and a card in the popover names the release; **OK** hides it until the next one. See [Release check](#release-check).

### Creating a New Dashboard

1. On the **landing page**, click the orange **"+ New Dashboard"** button located in the top right corner.
1. A pop-up window will appear with a field labeled **"Dashboard Title"**.
1. **Enter a name** for your new dashboard.
1. Your dashboard will be created with the title you provided and added to the section.
1. Click the blue **"Create Dashboard"** button to create the dashboard.
1. The new dashboard will appear in the section with informations including name, owner and status (public/private).

### Functionalities

#### Viewing a Dashboard

1. Once a dashboard is created, it will appear under the section.
1. Click the **"View"** button next to the dashboard name to open and explore its content.

#### Deleting a Dashboard

1. To delete a dashboard, locate the dashboard in the section.
1. Click the red **"Delete"** button next to the dashboard name.
1. A confirmation pop-up will appear, asking **"Are you sure you want to delete this dashboard?"**.
1. Click **"Delete"** to permanently remove the dashboard, or **"Cancel"** to keep it.

#### Editing dashboard name

1. To edit the name of a dashboard, locate the dashboard in the section.
1. Click the **"Edit name"** button next to the dashboard name.
1. A pop-up window will appear with a field labeled **"New name"**.
1. **Enter a new name** for your dashboard.
1. Click the blue **"Save"** button to save the new name.

#### Duplicating a dashboard

1. To duplicate a dashboard, locate the dashboard in the section.
1. Click the **"Duplicate"** button next to the dashboard name.
1. The dashboard will be duplicated and added to the section with the suffix **"(copy)"**.

Note

The **Visibility** column of the **Dashboards** page says whether a dashboard is **Public** or **Private**. A dashboard takes the visibility of its project: a public one opens for every user, a private one only for the users the project is shared with. Public means read-only for everyone else. Editing a dashboard needs the editor role on its project and deleting it the owner role. Admins can do both, and so can the owner of the dashboard itself, such as a copy they made.

#### Share a filtered listing (v1.10.1+)

The filters of `/dashboards` and `/projects` are kept in the URL. Set them, then press the link button in the toolbar to copy a link to that view:

| Link                                                   | Shows                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `/dashboards?template=nf-core/rnaseq`                  | Dashboards built from nf-core/rnaseq, any version |
| `/projects?template=nf-core/rnaseq,nf-core/viralrecon` | Projects built from either pipeline               |

Whoever opens it sees a **Shared view** banner, with **Show everything** to clear the filters. The link grants no access: it only narrows what they could already open.

## Projects section (/projects)

Complete Projects Documentation

The Projects Guide covers:

### Quick Overview

- The left sidebar includes a **"Projects"** section where users can manage their projects
- Click on **"Projects"** to navigate and view them
- Projects organize your data and provide structure for dashboards
- You can access workflows and data collections recursively within each project
- Each entity allows you to view configuration details and preview data

### Creating a project from a run folder or a manifest (v1.16.0+)

**+ New Project** starts a project from a source. There is no Basic or Advanced choice since v1.21.0: the project is created from its data, and the pipeline is detected or picked as an optional correction. A folder can be read as **Flat tables**, **Custom workflows** (Project Builder) or **Pipeline template**. See [Create a project](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/guide/#create-a-project). The run folder and manifest sources build a project from data the server reads, with no CLI involved, in three steps: **Source**, **Preview** (a dry run, nothing is created) and **Create**.

- **From a run folder**: point at the results folder of one pipeline run, in a bucket or, on a `depictio local` server, on this computer. Depictio recognises the pipeline, picks the template and shows what each data collection finds there; the data is ingested in the background. See [From a run folder](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#from-a-run-folder).
- **From Manifest**: paste the URL of a [data manifest](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#the-data-manifest-contract) and pick a template that reads one. See [From a manifest](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#creating-a-project-from-a-manifest).

## Account settings (/profile) (v1.17.0+)

Your avatar in the top bar opens **Account settings**, one page of sections that open and close:

- **Account**: your email, role and dates. Click the avatar to upload a profile picture; the server stores it as a 256-pixel WebP and includes it in [backups](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/backup/index.md). Signing in with Google sets your Google picture until you upload one. Since v1.18.0 it shows your [group](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/groups/#my-groups) badges (crown for P.I., shield for group admin), which open `/groups`, and the name and title your identity provider gives.
- **Password**: change the password you sign in with.
- **CLI agents**: the long-lived tokens of the `depictio` command line, see [Create a CLI configuration](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/get_started/#create-a-cli-configuration). The former `/cli-agents` page leads here.
- **Preferences**, kept in this browser: **Theme**, light or dark; [**Look**](#looks), Paper, Classic or the instance default; **Font size** of figures, tables and cards.
- **Getting started** (v1.22.0+): the [guided tours](#guided-tours). **Take the tour** starts the tour of the dashboards list, **Offer every tour again** resets the tours you have seen, and the switch *Offer a tour on pages I open for the first time* stops or resumes the offers. All three are disabled when the deployment turns tours off.
- **Server**: the [server information](#server-information).

**Sign out** is at the foot of the page.

## About section (/about)

The **About** section provides information about the GitHub repository and the documentation.

## Admin section (/admin)

The **Admin** section is only accessible to users with admin privileges. Since v1.17.0 its pages are listed down the side, in four groups:

| Group        | Pages                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **People**   | **Users**: every account, its role (standard or system admin), deletion and, since v1.19.0, [Add user](#add-a-user). **Groups** (v1.18.0+): see [Groups](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/groups/#managing-a-group) |
| **Content**  | **Projects** and **Dashboards**: every one of them, whoever owns it. Admins can delete any                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Activity** | **Tasks**, **Ingestion**, **Watchers**, **Logs** and **Health**, see [Monitoring](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/monitoring/index.md)                                                                             |
| **Instance** | [**Branding**](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/branding/index.md), [**Backups**](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/backup/index.md), **Maintenance** and **Settings**           |

### Adding a user (v1.19.0+)

**Administration → Users → Add user** creates an account with an email, a display name and an initial password, generated by default (with refresh and copy). Two switches: **ask for a new password at first sign-in**, on by default, and **system admin**. A person asked to change it is taken to the Password section of Account settings until they do, and the Users list shows the pending change.

It works even when [registration](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/authentication-modes/#registration) or [password sign-in](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/authentication-modes/#password-login) is closed: on an SSO-only instance the account is matched by email at the first SSO sign-in, which is how a person is added to a [group](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/groups/index.md) before they ever sign in. It is not offered in single-user or public mode.

### Release check (v1.17.0+)

**Administration → Settings → Version check** tells administrators when a newer Depictio release is published. The server asks the GitHub Releases API of `depictio/depictio` every 6 hours, with a plain request that sends nothing about the instance, and the [server information](#server-information) shows the result to administrators only. **Check now** asks at once.

The check is on by default and the switch turns it off for the instance. Setting [`DEPICTIO_VERSION_CHECK_ENABLED`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#release-check) to `true` or `false` decides instead and locks the switch, for instances that must make no outbound call.

Since v1.18.0 the check also runs as soon as the running version is not the one that last checked, so the page never shows a latest release older than the current one after an upgrade.

## Page reference

Depictio's main pages and their URLs:

### Projects list (/projects)

### Project detail (/projects/{id})

A single project's data. Since v1.17.0 the page starts with a sentence on what the project holds and its workflows, as cards to pick one from, then a switch between two views:

- **Data collections** — the project's workflows, a sortable, filterable table of its data collections, its cross-DC links, and the details of the selected collection. For a [composed](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/composed-dashboards/index.md) project, a **Files the catalog did not recognise** card lists the tables left out, with the command that adds each (v1.16.0+).
- **Ingestion** — the [ingestion report](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#ingestion-report-health), offered for **every** project since v1.6.0. For one created from a [pipeline template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/index.md) it compares expected against ingested data collections; for any other it reads the collections the project declares today, and a **Live project** badge says so. Since v1.15.0 a **History** view lists the project's [ingestion runs](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#ingestion-history), and, where the server allows it, [**Run ingestion**](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#run-ingestion) starts one from the browser.

Selecting a data collection shows its details, including its **Delta version**, and for a table a data preview and its **Version history**: see [Dataset history](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/#dataset-history).

You can reach this page directly by clicking the **project badge** shown on any dashboard card or in the dashboards table, or the **project name** in an open dashboard's Settings (v1.6.0+).

Data that is not on the server's own disk is handled in two places (v1.16.0+); the mechanisms are described on [Remote data and manifests](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/index.md).

- **Remote URL** in **Create Data Collection**: the **Table (CSV / TSV / Parquet)** tab offers **Upload a file** or **Remote URL**. With the latter, paste an `https://` or `s3://` address as the **File URL** (`http://` only when the server allows it); the name and format are filled in from its last segment. The server fetches the file, so it never travels through the browser, and a private bucket is read with the project's storage settings. MultiQC reports are uploaded only.
- **Project settings** in the header, next to **Permissions**, opens three sections; nothing is saved on close, each acts on its own button:
  - **Storage**, for project owners and administrators: the endpoint, bucket, region and keys of a private bucket the project reads, with **Test connection**. See [Project storage settings](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#project-storage-settings).
  - **Data refresh**: re-read the collections that come from a manifest, a URL or a bucket, and rebuild their tables. See [Refreshing the data](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#refreshing-the-data).
  - **Export**: package the project and its dashboards as a template bundle (zip). See [Export a project as a template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/templates/#export-a-project-as-a-template).

**Data refresh** and **Export** are for owners, editors and administrators; on a public instance, administrators only. The dialog opens on the section used last.
