# YAML Configuration Reference

Full Configuration Template Warning

**Do not copy-paste this entire configuration blindly.** This reference shows all available options with their defaults and descriptions. Only specify values that differ from defaults or are required for your specific use case.

This is a complete reference of all configuration options available in Depictio YAML files, as of v1.21.0. For getting started and examples, see the [YAML Examples Guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/yaml-examples/index.md). For a folder no template recognises, `depictio project-builder <dir>` (v1.21.0+) defines the collections in the browser and writes an ad-hoc template next to the data, which `depictio ingest <dir> --template <bundle>` runs.

```
# =============================================================================
# DEPICTIO PROJECT CONFIGURATION REFERENCE
# =============================================================================

# Required: Project identification
name:
  "My Project Name" # Required: Human-readable project name
  # Must be non-empty string
  # Example: "Multi-omics Cancer Study"

description: null # Optional: plain text shown with the project (HTML is removed)

# Optional, ignored since v1.21.0: kept so older files still validate
project_type:
  "basic" # Options are "basic" or "advanced" (default: "basic")
  # No longer decides what a project can do

# Optional: Project visibility settings
is_public:
  false # Optional: Project visibility (default: false)
  # true: Visible to all users (read-only)
  # false: Restricted to project members

# Optional: CLI integration path
yaml_config_path:
  null # Optional: Path to this YAML file (default: null)
  # Set by the CLI to the file's absolute path; never set by hand

# Optional: External project management integration
data_management_platform_project_url:
  null # Optional: URL to external project system (default: null)
  # Must start with http:// or https://
  # Example: "https://labid.embl.org/projects/123"

layout:
  null # Optional: "runs", "pipeline" or "tables" (default: null = detected)
  # Overrides the layout the viewer detects; no backend effect

realtime: # Optional: real-time updates (default: null)
  enabled: true # Default: true
  debounce_ms: 1000 # Default: 1000
  watch_data_collections: null # DC tags to watch (default: null = all)

# Accepted, but `depictio ingest` only scans the collections of `workflows`:
# declare data collections under a workflow (see below).
data_collections: [] # Optional (default: [])

# Set by Depictio, never written by hand: permissions (the CLI user becomes
# owner), registration_time, last_modified, hash, triggered_by (what ran the
# last ingestion, default "manual"), template_origin, provenance,
# published_lock, pending_owner_email.

# =============================================================================
# LINKS (Cross-DC Interactive Filtering)
# =============================================================================

links:  # Optional: Define relationships for cross-DC filtering
  - source_dc_tag: "sample_metadata"   # Required (or source_dc_id): DC holding the filter
    source_column: "sample_id"         # Required: Column to filter on
    target_dc_tag: "multiqc_fastqc"    # Required (or target_dc_id): DC to update when filtered
    target_type: "multiqc"             # Required: "table", "multiqc", "image" or "genomic_tracks"
    # source_dc_id / target_dc_id take a DC id (the `id` pinned on a DC),
    # never a tag: a tag written there matches nothing
    link_config:                       # Optional (default: resolver "direct")
      resolver: "sample_mapping"       # Default "direct"
      target_field: "sample_name"      # Optional: Field to match in target DC
      # mappings: {S1: [S1_R1, S1_R2]} # Optional: explicit variants (sample_mapping)
      # pattern: "{sample}.bam"        # Optional: must contain {sample} (pattern)
      # columns: {chrom: chromosome, pos: position}  # Required by "region"
      # case_sensitive: true           # Default: true
      # Resolvers:
      #   "direct" - Same value in both DCs
      #   "sample_mapping" - Canonical ID → MultiQC sample variants
      #   "pattern" - Template substitution (e.g., "{sample}.bam")
      #   "regex" - Target values matched by a regex
      #   "wildcard" - Glob matching (e.g., "S1*")
      #   "region" - Genomic region renamed onto the target's chrom/pos columns
    description: null                  # Optional
    enabled: true                      # Default: true; disabled links are ignored

# =============================================================================
# JOINS (tables combined at ingestion)
# =============================================================================

joins: # Optional: run by `depictio ingest` on the client, stored as a new Table DC
  - name: "expression_with_metadata" # Required: letters, digits, _ and - (1-100 chars)
    left_dc: "gene_expression"       # Required: DC tag, or "workflow.tag" across workflows
    right_dc: "sample_metadata"      # Required: must differ from left_dc
    on_columns: ["sample_id"]        # Required: at least one, no duplicates
    how: "inner"                     # Default "inner"; "left", "right", "outer"
    workflow_name: null              # Optional: workflow unscoped tags are looked up in
    persist: true                    # Default: true (write the result as a Delta table)
    description: null                # Optional
    granularity:                     # Optional: aggregate the finer table first
      aggregate_to: "sample_id"      # Required: aggregation key column
      numeric_default: "mean"        # Default "mean"; also sum, min, max, first, last, count, median
      categorical_default: "first"   # Default "first"
      column_overrides:              # Optional
        - column: "reads"
          function: "sum"

# =============================================================================
# WORKFLOWS (for projects with workflows)
# =============================================================================

workflows:
  - # Required: Workflow identification
    name:
      "rnaseq_pipeline" # Required: Unique workflow identifier
      # Example: "rnaseq_pipeline", "variant_calling"

    # Required: Execution engine information
    engine:
      name:
        "nextflow" # Required: Engine name
        # Examples: "nextflow", "snakemake", "python", "galaxy", "cwl", "shell", "r"
      version:
        "24.10.3" # Optional: Engine version for reproducibility
        # Example: "24.10.3", "7.32.0"

    # Optional: Workflow metadata
    version:
      "3.18.0" # Optional: Workflow version
      # Example: "1.0.0", "v2.3.1"
    description: "nf-core RNA-seq pipeline for expression quantification" # Optional: Workflow description
    repository_url:
      "https://github.com/nf-core/rnaseq" # Optional: Source code repository
      # Example: "https://github.com/user/workflow"
    workflow_tag:
      "nextflow/rnaseq_pipeline" # Optional: workflow identifier (CLI --workflow-name)
      # Default from a YAML file: the workflow `name`

    # Optional: Workflow registry information
    catalog:
      name:
        "nf-core" # Required in a catalog: "nf-core", "smk-wf-catalog" or "workflowhub"
      url:
        "https://nf-co.re/rnaseq" # Required in a catalog: http(s):// or git:// URL

    # Optional: run settings and provenance
    config:
      version: null # Optional
      workflow_parameters: null # Optional: free mapping of pipeline parameters
      # Filled by ingestion when the run tells: engine_name, pipeline_version,
      # nextflow_version, tools_executed

    # Required: Data location configuration
    data_location:
      structure:
        "sequencing-runs" # Required: Directory organization pattern
        # Options:
        #   "flat" - All files in single directory level
        #   "sequencing-runs" - Hierarchical run-based structure

      locations: # Required: Root directories to search
        - "{DATA_ROOT}/rnaseq_studies/cohort_2024" # Supports environment variable expansion: {VAR_NAME}
        - "/backup/rnaseq_data" # Examples: "/absolute/path/to/data", "{DATA_ROOT}/project1"
        # The CLI checks that each local location exists (a directory, or a
        # local manifest file). A location may also be an s3:// or https://
        # URL, for remote scan modes (http:// only with DEPICTIO_REMOTE_ALLOW_HTTP)

      runs_regex:
        "batch_[A-C]" # Required for "sequencing-runs" structure
        # Optional for "flat" structure
        # Regex pattern to identify individual runs
        # Example: "run_\\d+", "sample_.*", "batch[A-Z]"

      # attached_locations: written by `depictio ingest --attach-run`, not by hand

    # runs, registration_time: written by ingestion, not by hand

    # Required: Data collections for this workflow
    data_collections:
      - # Required: Unique identifier for this data collection
        data_collection_tag:
          "gene_expression" # Required: Unique within project
          # Used for referencing in links and dashboards
          # Example: "gene_counts", "quality_metrics"

        # Optional: Human-readable description
        description:
          "Per-sample gene expression quantification" # Optional: Description of the data collection
          # Used in UI tooltips and documentation

        optional: false # Default: false. In a template, the DC is dropped when
        # its source is absent instead of failing the run

        # Required: Data collection configuration
        config:
          # Required: Type of data collection
          type:
            "table" # Required: Data collection type
            # Options:
            # Case-insensitive, stored lowercase. Options:
            #   "table" - Tabular data (CSV, TSV, Excel, Parquet, Feather)
            #   "MultiQC" - MultiQC quality control reports
            #   "Image" - A table with a column of image paths; see "IMAGE" below
            #   "geojson" - GeoJSON boundary files for choropleth maps
            #   "phylogeny" - Newick / Nexus trees for the phylogenetic viz
            #   "indexed_file" - Indexed genomic files (VCF, BAM, bigWig,
            #     bigBed, GFF3, FASTA, bgzip + tabix), range-read by the
            #     browser; see the "INDEXED FILE" block below
            #   "genomic_tracks" - Manifest of genome-browser tracks, one row
            #     per track file; see the "GENOMIC TRACKS" block below
            #   "jbrowse2" - legacy, superseded by "genomic_tracks"

          source:
            "native" # Optional (default "native"): where the data comes from
            # "native" - scanned files (needs scan)
            # "transformed" - computed by a recipe (needs transform, no scan)
            # "joined", "aggregated" - derived, no scan

          transform: # Required when source is "transformed"; see Recipes
            # recipe: "nf-core/ampliseq/taxonomy_rel_abundance.py"  # Required: a .py recipe
            # source_overrides:                 # Optional: repoint a recipe source
            #   rel_table: {path: "custom/rel-table.tsv"}  # path or glob_pattern, exactly one
            # params: {marker_panel: "{MARKER_PANEL}"}      # Optional: passed to transform()
            # scope: null   # Optional (v1.21.0+): "run" (once per run), "aggregate"
            #               # (over every run) or "pipeline"; null = the recipe's default
            # materialized, run_params: written by Depictio, not by hand

          # Optional: a free label, not checked
          metatype:
            "aggregate" # Optional (default: null)
            # Conventions:
            #   "metadata" - Single annotation/metadata file per project
            #   "aggregate" - Multiple files combined into unified dataset
            # A join with a "Metadata" side gets no depictio_run_id column

          # Required for native DCs except MultiQC: File discovery configuration
          scan:
            # Required: File scanning strategy
            mode:
              "recursive" # Required: Scanning strategy
              # Options:
              #   "single" - Single file per project/run
              #   "recursive" - Pattern-based file discovery
              #   "url" - One remote file at an s3:// or https:// URL
              #   "s3_prefix" - Every object under an s3:// prefix matching a glob
              #   "manifest" - The files a Data Manifest lists for this collection
              # mode and scan_parameters must agree: a parameter block that
              # belongs to another mode is rejected with a message naming both.
              # The three remote modes are detailed under "Remote scan modes" below.

            # Required: Mode-specific scan parameters
            scan_parameters:
              # For mode: "recursive" - specify search pattern
              regex_config: # Required for recursive mode: Pattern matching configuration
                pattern:
                  "salmon/{sample_id}/quant.sf" # Required: Regex pattern for file discovery
                  # Example: "stats/.*_stats\\.tsv"
                wildcards: # Optional: what each {name} placeholder of the pattern stands for
                  - name: "sample_id" # The placeholder, and since v1.16.0 a column of the table holding what it matched
                    wildcard_regex: "[^/]+" # Regex the placeholder is replaced by
              max_depth: null # Optional: directory levels searched below each run (0 = run directory only)
              ignore: null # Optional: glob patterns skipped, e.g. ["work", "*.tmp"]

              # For mode: "single" - specify exact file (alternative to regex_config)
              # filename: "metadata/sample_info.csv"  # Required for single mode: File path
              # Can be absolute or relative path
              # scope: null   # Optional (v1.21.0+): "project" reads one file for every
              #               # run; null (default) or "run" binds each run its own file
              # run_files is written by the CLI on --attach-run, not by hand

              # For mode: "url" - one remote file, fetched by the server
              # url: "https://data.example.org/run42/metadata.tsv"  # Required: absolute s3:// or https:// URL

              # For mode: "s3_prefix" - list a bucket prefix (the remote counterpart of recursive)
              # prefix: "s3://my-bucket/run42/"          # Required: s3:// prefix, bucket included
              # pattern: "*.samples.csv"                 # Optional: glob on the key relative to the prefix, or on the file name (default "*")
              # pattern_syntax: "glob"                   # Optional: "glob" (default) or "regex"
              # id_regex: "^([^/]+?)\\.samples\\.csv$"   # Optional: one capture group, searched in the key relative to the prefix; the capture becomes depictio_manifest_id
              # max_files: 10000                         # Optional: ceiling on matching objects (default 10000, max 100000)

              # For mode: "manifest" - consume the entries of a Data Manifest
              # manifest_url: "https://data.example.org/run42/manifest.json"  # Required: https:// manifest URL (a local path in CLI context)
              # manifest_type: "samples"                 # Required: manifest `type` this collection consumes (its tag, by convention)
              # id_field: "id"                           # Optional: manifest column holding the entity id
              # url_field: "url"                         # Optional: manifest column holding the file URL
              # type_field: "type"                       # Optional: manifest column holding the type
              # run_field: "run"                         # Optional: manifest column holding the run grouping

          # Required: Type-specific configuration
          dc_specific_properties:
            # Required: File format specification
            format:
              "tsv" # Required: File format
              # Values: "csv", "tsv", "xlsx", "xls", "parquet", "feather"
              # Case-insensitive, normalized to lowercase

            # Optional (default: {}): keyword arguments passed as they are to
            # polars: scan_csv (csv, tsv), scan_parquet, scan_ipc (feather) or
            # read_excel (xls, xlsx). A key the reader does not take fails at ingestion.
            polars_kwargs:
              # Common options (scan_csv)
              separator:
                "\t" # Optional: Column separator character
                # Unset: tab for a .tsv/.tab file (or format tsv), else ","
                # Example: ",", "\t", "|", ";"
              has_header:
                true # Optional (default: true): First row contains column names
              skip_rows:
                0 # Optional: Number of rows to skip at file beginning (default: 0)
                # Useful for files with metadata headers

              # Advanced options
              schema_overrides: # Optional: Explicit column type mapping
                Name: "String" # Forces specific data types
                Length: "Int64" # Example types: "String", "Int64", "Float64", "Boolean"
                EffectiveLength: "Float64"
                TPM: "Float64"
                NumReads: "Float64"
              new_columns:
                null # Optional: Rename the columns, e.g. when has_header: false
                # Example: ["sample", "gene", "expression"]
              null_values:
                ["", "NA"] # Optional: Values to treat as null/missing (default: none)
              n_rows:
                null # Optional: Limit number of rows to read
                # Useful for testing configurations
              encoding:
                "utf8" # Optional: "utf8" (default) or "utf8-lossy"

              # Excel-specific options (read_excel, for .xlsx, .xls files)
              # sheet_name: "Results"   # Optional: sheet to read (default: the first)
              # sheet_id: 1             # Optional: 1-based sheet index, instead of sheet_name

            # Optional (default: all columns): Column filtering for performance
            keep_columns: # Optional: Column filtering
              - "Name" # If specified, only these columns are retained
              - "TPM" # Improves performance for large datasets
              - "NumReads" # Example: ["sample_id", "expression", "p_value"]

            # Optional: Column documentation
            columns_description: # Optional: Column documentation
              Name: "Gene/transcript identifier" # Human-readable column descriptions
              TPM: "Transcripts per million" # Used in dashboard tooltips and documentation
              NumReads: "Estimated read count" # Example format: column_name: "Description"

            # Optional, for Map components: both or neither
            # lat_column: "latitude"   # Column holding the latitude
            # lon_column: "longitude"  # Column holding the longitude; must differ
            # crs: "EPSG:4326"         # Default: "EPSG:4326"

          # Legacy: config.join {on_columns, how, with_dc} is still accepted but
          # no longer joins anything (its on_columns only order the Delta table).
          # Declare joins at project level, under "joins" above.

      # --- MultiQC DATA COLLECTION (v0.5.0+) ---
      - data_collection_tag:
          "multiqc_data" # Required: Unique identifier for MultiQC data

        description:
          "MultiQC quality control report data" # Optional: Description

        config:
          # Required: Type specification for MultiQC
          type:
            "MultiQC" # Required: Identifies this as a MultiQC data collection
            # NOTE: MultiQC type has special handling:
            #   - scan is optional. Without it, ingestion looks for
            #     <location>/*/multiqc_data/multiqc.parquet (also under */multiqc/
            #     and */*/); the templates declare a recursive scan instead
            #   - metatype and dc_specific_properties are optional: samples,
            #     modules and plots are filled at ingestion
            #   - Requires MultiQC 1.29+ to generate parquet format

          # scan:                       # Optional, as the templates do
          #   mode: "recursive"
          #   scan_parameters:
          #     regex_config:
          #       pattern: "multiqc/multiqc_data/multiqc.parquet"

        # NOTE: For MultiQC, use project-level "links" instead of joins
        # Links enable interactive filtering with sample_mapping resolver
        # Example link configuration (at project level):
        #   links:
        #     - source_dc_tag: "sample_metadata"
        #       source_column: "sample_id"
        #       target_dc_tag: "multiqc_data"
        #       target_type: "multiqc"
        #       link_config:
        #         resolver: "sample_mapping"

      # --- IMAGE DATA COLLECTION ---
      - data_collection_tag: "cell_images" # Required

        config:
          type: "image" # A table whose image_column holds image paths
          metatype: "Metadata"
          scan:
            mode: single
            scan_parameters:
              filename: "path/to/images.csv" # The table, not the images

          dc_specific_properties:
            format: "csv" # Required: csv, tsv, parquet, feather, xls, xlsx or mixed
            image_column: "image_path" # Required: column of image paths
            s3_base_folder:
              "s3://my-bucket/project/images/" # Optional: paths in image_column
              # are relative to it; must start with s3://
            local_images_path:
              null # Optional: local folder `depictio ingest` uploads to
              # s3_base_folder (which the CLI then requires)
            thumbnail_size: 150 # Optional: pixels, 50 to 1000 (default 150)
            supported_formats: [".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".webp", ".svg", ".bmp", ".tiff"] # Default
            # polars_kwargs, keep_columns, columns_description: as for a Table DC

      # --- GeoJSON DATA COLLECTION ---
      - data_collection_tag:
          "europe_geojson" # Required: Unique identifier for GeoJSON data

        description:
          "GeoJSON boundaries for European regions" # Optional: Description

        config:
          # Required: Type specification for GeoJSON
          type:
            "geojson" # Required: Identifies this as a GeoJSON data collection
            # NOTE: GeoJSON type stores FeatureCollection files in S3
            #   - Used as boundary source for choropleth_map components
            #   - Referenced by geojson_dc_tag in dashboard YAML
            #   - Requires a single .geojson file

          metatype:
            "GeoJSON" # Optional: free label

          # Required: File discovery configuration
          scan:
            mode: single
            scan_parameters:
              filename: "path/to/boundaries.geojson"

          # Required: GeoJSON-specific configuration
          dc_specific_properties:
            feature_id_key:
              "properties.NAME" # Optional (default "id"): GeoJSON property path to match locations_column
              # Maps to Plotly's featureidkey parameter
              # Common values: "id", "properties.NAME", "properties.ISO_A3"

      # --- PHYLOGENY DATA COLLECTION ---
      - data_collection_tag:
          "bacterial_tree" # Required: Unique identifier for the tree

        description: "Bacterial phylogeny, Newick file" # Optional

        config:
          type:
            "phylogeny" # Required: Identifies this as a tree data collection
            # NOTE: file-backed, nothing is parsed or converted
            #   - Ingestion copies the file as is to S3; served as raw Newick via
            #     /advanced_viz/phylogeny/{dc_id}/newick
            #   - Referenced by tree_dc_id in an advanced_viz component
            #     of kind "phylogenetic"

          metatype: "Aggregate" # Optional: free label

          scan:
            mode: single
            scan_parameters:
              filename: "path/to/tree.nwk"

          dc_specific_properties:
            format: "newick" # Optional: "newick" (default) or "nexus"

            ladderize:
              true # Optional: ladderise the tree by default (default true)
              # Viewers can toggle this in the viz controls

            # Tip annotations live in a SEPARATE Table DC, keyed by taxon
            # name, the same pattern Microreact uses. All three keys are
            # optional; without them the tree renders unannotated.
            metadata_dc_tag:
              "bacterial_metadata" # Optional: tag of the metadata Table DC
            metadata_taxon_column:
              "taxon" # Optional: column joining to tip labels (default "taxon")
            tip_label_strategy:
              "taxon" # Optional: "taxon" (leaf name IS the taxon id, default)
              #                   or "first_token" (take the first
              #                   underscore-separated token of the leaf name)

      # --- GENOMIC TRACKS DATA COLLECTION ---
      - data_collection_tag:
          "tracks" # Required: Unique identifier for the track manifest

        description: "Genome-browser tracks, one row per file" # Optional

        config:
          type:
            "genomic_tracks" # Required: Identifies this as a track manifest
            # NOTE: the manifest is ingested like a Table DC (a Delta table)
            #   - Each row names one track file in uri_column
            #   - Rendered by the "jbrowse" component; filterable and
            #     linkable like any table (target_type: "genomic_tracks")

          metatype: "Metadata" # Optional: free label

          scan:
            mode: single
            scan_parameters:
              filename: "path/to/tracks.tsv" # The manifest, not the track files

          dc_specific_properties:
            format: "tsv" # Required: manifest format (csv, tsv, parquet, feather, xls, xlsx)
            polars_kwargs:
              separator: "\t" # As for a Table DC

            # Manifest columns
            uri_column: "uri" # Column holding the track location (default "uri")
            track_id_column: "track_id" # Unique track id (default: the row's uri)
            sample_column: "sample" # Entity the track belongs to; used for cross-filtering
            format_column: "format" # Track format column (default "format")
            default_format: "bigwig" # Used when no column and no file extension tells
            # Track formats: bigwig, bedgraph, bed, bigbed, narrowpeak,
            # broadpeak, vcf, bam, cram, gff3, gtf, fasta
            index_column: "index_uri" # Index location (default "index_uri"; inferred otherwise)
            order_column: "order" # Tracks open in ascending order of this column
            name_column: "name" # Track label
            color_column: "color" # Track colour
            category_column: "category" # Folders in the track selector

            # Reference genome: a preset name or a custom assembly
            assembly:
              "hg38" # Default "hg38". Presets: hg38, hg19, hs1, mm10, mm39,
              # sacCer3, dm6, ce11, danRer11, TAIR10, wuhCor1.
              # A custom assembly is a mapping with `name` and either
              # `fasta_uri` + `fai_uri` (+ `gzi_uri` when bgzipped) or `twobit_uri`;
              # optional: display_name, aliases, chrom_sizes_uri, refname_aliases_uri

            # Where the track files are. A track uri is one of:
            #   - a relative path: uploaded to Depictio's S3 at ingestion
            #   - s3://bucket/key or https://host/path: read in place
            tracks_base_path:
              null # Optional: local folder relative uris resolve against
              # (default: the manifest's folder)
            remote_base_uri:
              null # Optional: s3:// or https:// prefix relative uris are read
              # in place under, instead of being uploaded
            direct_access:
              false # Optional: let the browser fetch https:// tracks itself
              # (the host must send CORS and Range headers)

            # Display
            display_defaults: {} # Optional: per-format JBrowse track config, keyed by track format
            presets: {} # Optional: named JBrowse config fragments a component can pick

            keep_columns: null # Optional: as for a Table DC
            columns_description: null # Optional: as for a Table DC

      # --- INDEXED FILE DATA COLLECTION ---
      - data_collection_tag: "variant_files" # Required

        config:
          type: "indexed_file" # Files read whole or by range from S3; no table
          metatype: "Aggregate" # Optional: free label
          scan:
            mode: recursive
            scan_parameters:
              regex_config:
                pattern: "variants/.*\\.vcf\\.gz"

          dc_specific_properties:
            format:
              "vcf" # Required: vcf, bam, bigwig, bigbed, gff3, fasta, tabix,
              # pdb, mmcif or pae (aliases: bw, bb, gff, cif, ent)
            index_suffix:
              null # Optional: index sidecar suffix, starting with "."
              # (default: the format's, e.g. .tbi; "" for no index)
            sample_regex:
              null # Optional: regex on the file path naming the sample
              # (named group "sample"; default: the file name without suffixes)
            sample_col: "sample" # Default "sample": the sample column name elsewhere in the project
            assembly: null # Optional: genome assembly, e.g. "hg38"
            max_file_size_mb: 512 # Default 512 (1 to 51200): larger files are skipped
```

A `genomic_tracks` collection is shown by the [genome browser](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/index.md); the [guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/guide/#example-genomic-tracks-dcs) has a worked example.

## Remote scan modes (v1.16.0+)

Three scan modes fetch data from where it already is instead of walking a local directory. Whoever ingests, the CLI or the server, reads the files there; the server goes through a gateway that validates every URL and decides which buckets it may read (see [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#remote-data-sources)). The files are materialised to Delta Lake exactly like scanned local files. [Remote data and manifests](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/index.md) explains when to use which.

`mode` and `scan_parameters` are cross-checked: declaring `mode: url` with a `filename` block, for instance, is rejected with a message naming the mode the parameters belong to and the parameters the declared mode expects. The [scan bounds](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/yaml-examples/#scan-bounds) `max_depth` and `ignore` belong to `recursive`: a remote mode that declares them is rejected the same way.

### `url`: one remote file

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`     | yes      |         | Absolute `s3://` or `https://` URL of the file. `http://` is accepted only with `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_ALLOW_HTTP=true`, set on the server and, for a CLI ingestion, in the CLI's environment too. Validation here is syntactic; reachability and address checks happen at fetch time. |

```
scan:
  mode: url
  scan_parameters:
    url: "https://data.example.org/run42/metadata.tsv"
```

### `s3_prefix`: every object under a prefix

The remote counterpart of `recursive`: list the objects under an `s3://` prefix and keep the keys matching a glob. It is S3-only by construction, since plain HTTPS exposes no listing operation.

| Parameter        | Required | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------- | -------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prefix`         | yes      |          | `s3://` prefix, bucket included, e.g. `s3://my-bucket/run42/`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `pattern`        | no       | `"*"`    | Glob matched against the key *relative to* the prefix and against the file name, so `*.csv` rather than the full path. Its `*` also crosses `/`, so `*.csv` reaches the keys of sub-prefixes too                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `pattern_syntax` | no       | `"glob"` | How `pattern` is read: `glob` (fnmatch) or `regex`. A regex is matched from the start of the file name, and of the relative key when it contains a `/`, as in a `recursive` scan. A [run folder on S3](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#a-run-folder-on-s3) turns each `recursive` collection into an `s3_prefix` scan that keeps the template's regex, with `regex` here |
| `id_regex`       | no       | `null`   | Regex with exactly one capture group, searched in the key relative to the prefix, then in the file name. The capture is stored as the file's entity id and read back as the `depictio_manifest_id` column, which gives a prefix scan the same cross-DC join key as a manifest. An object it does not match is kept without an id, and the scan warns how many there are                                              |
| `max_files`      | no       | `10000`  | Ceiling on the number of matching objects (at most `100000`), a backstop against pointing a collection at a bucket root. The listing also stops after 10 × `max_files` keys. Either limit is reported as a warning                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

```
scan:
  mode: s3_prefix
  scan_parameters:
    prefix: "s3://my-bucket/run42/"
    pattern: "*.samples.csv"
    id_regex: "^([^/]+?)\\.samples\\.csv$"
```

### `manifest`: the entries of a Data Manifest

The collection consumes every manifest entry whose `type` equals `manifest_type`. The manifest contract (`id`, `type`, `url`, optional `run`) is described on [Remote data and manifests](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#the-data-manifest-contract).

| Parameter       | Required | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | -------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest_url`  | yes      |          | `https://` URL of the manifest (JSON or CSV). In CLI context a local path is accepted too. An `s3://` URL passes validation but is not read yet |
| `manifest_type` | yes      |          | Which manifest `type` this collection consumes. By convention, the collection's own tag                                                         |
| `id_field`      | no       | `"id"`   | Manifest column holding the entity id                                                                                                           |
| `url_field`     | no       | `"url"`  | Manifest column holding the file URL                                                                                                            |
| `type_field`    | no       | `"type"` | Manifest column holding the type                                                                                                                |
| `run_field`     | no       | `"run"`  | Manifest column holding the run grouping. Files of a manifest without that column get `remote` as their run                                     |

The `*_field` overrides remap a manifest with non-canonical column names onto the contract without rewriting it. In a template, every `manifest` collection reads the same manifest, so they must all name the same columns: **From Manifest** refuses a template whose collections disagree.

```
scan:
  mode: manifest
  scan_parameters:
    manifest_url: "{MANIFEST_URL}"
    manifest_type: "samples"
```

# Remote data and manifests (v1.16.0+)

Data can stay where it is: an `s3://` run folder, one file at a URL, every object under a bucket prefix, or a list of files called a **data manifest**. Depictio reads it there and writes Delta tables to its own storage, so dashboards, links and joins work as with local files.

## Which way to use

| You have                                    | Web UI                                                                                                                            | CLI                                                                                                                 | Scan mode             |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| A pipeline run folder in a bucket           | [**Read in place**, Folder or bucket](#from-a-run-folder)                                                                         | [`depictio ingest s3://bucket/run42`](#a-run-folder-on-s3)                                                          | `s3_prefix`, `url`    |
| A pipeline run folder on this computer      | [**Read in place**](#from-a-run-folder), on a `depictio local` server                                                             | [`depictio ingest /data/run42`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#ingest-command) | `recursive`, `single` |
| One file on the web or in a bucket          | **Read in place**, One file URL ([guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/guide/#create-a-project)) | [`--bind tag=https://host/data.csv`](#bind-a-data-collection-to-a-location)                                         | `url`                 |
| Many files under one prefix                 |                                                                                                                                   | [`--bind tag=s3://bucket/run42/*.csv`](#bind-a-data-collection-to-a-location)                                       | `s3_prefix`           |
| Files of several types, in scattered places |                                                                                                                                   | [`--manifest <url or path>`](#creating-a-project-from-a-manifest)                                                   | `manifest`            |

Plain HTTPS cannot be listed: use `url` for one known file, or a manifest for several. The scan parameters are in the [YAML reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/reference/#remote-scan-modes).

## A run folder on S3

`depictio ingest` takes an `s3://` prefix as `DATA_DIR`. One listing of the prefix stands in for the folder, and the template is detected from the run's records as for a local folder. A folder no bundled template reads needs `--template`: it is not [composed from the catalog](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/composed-dashboards/index.md).

```
depictio ingest s3://my-bucket/ampliseq/run42
depictio ingest s3://my-bucket/ampliseq/run42 --template nf-core/ampliseq/latest --dry-run
```

The template is not modified. Each collection is pointed at the prefix:

| Template declares                | Read under `s3://` as                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `recursive` scan                 | `s3_prefix` scan with the template's regex (`pattern_syntax: regex`); `max_depth` and `ignore` are dropped |
| `single` scan                    | `url` scan of the file under the prefix                                                                    |
| Recipe (`source: transformed`)   | Its sources are read through the listing                                                                   |
| `url`, `s3_prefix` or `manifest` | Unchanged                                                                                                  |
| `indexed_file`                   | Not supported yet: a required one stops the run, an optional one is skipped. `--bind` it to a local folder |

Limits and edge cases

- A `sequencing-runs` workflow keeps its runs: each first-level folder matching `runs_regex` is a run. Elsewhere, files carry `remote` as `depictio_run_id`.
- MultiQC reports are downloaded to a temporary copy within `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES`; one that does not fit is skipped.
- A `single` collection pointing at a local file (`--var METADATA_FILE=/data/meta.tsv`) becomes a `url` scan, which refuses it: `--bind metadata=/data/meta.tsv` instead.
- The data root listing stops at 100,000 objects, and each `s3_prefix` scan at its `max_files` (10,000).
- An `s3_prefix` scan that matches nothing stops the run, where an empty local scan would not.

Which buckets can be read, and with which keys: [Reading S3 buckets](#reading-s3-buckets).

### Preview before ingesting

With a template and a `DATA_DIR`, local or `s3://`, `--dry-run` prints what each data collection finds there and creates nothing. Above the table come the template, the runs detected, the dashboards to import and the variables derived from the folder; under it the missing sources and a summary line.

| Status    | Meaning                                       |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `ok`      | It will ingest                                |
| `empty`   | Its scan matched nothing                      |
| `missing` | A source it needs is not there                |
| `pruned`  | Dropped, because an optional source is absent |

Zeros on every row mean the folder is one level too high or too low. A `url` or `manifest` collection cannot be counted from the listing and shows `ok` with 0 files. Without a template, `--dry-run` lists the [files each collection would match](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#ingest-command) instead.

## Bind a data collection to a location

`--bind TAG=LOCATION` points one collection at its data. It is repeatable, and the scan mode follows the location:

| Location                                           | Mode                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/scratch/run42` (a folder)                        | `recursive`, with the template's pattern                    |
| `/scratch/run42/*.csv` (a local glob)              | `recursive`, the glob as pattern                            |
| `./samplesheet.csv`                                | `single`                                                    |
| `https://host/data.csv`, or `s3://bucket/key.csv`  | `url`                                                       |
| `s3://bucket/run42/*.csv`, or `s3://bucket/run42/` | `s3_prefix`; without the trailing `/`, one object, so `url` |

```
depictio ingest --template my-lab/rnaseq-qc/1 \
  --bind samples=s3://my-bucket/run42/*.samples.csv \
  --bind metadata=https://data.example.org/run42/metadata.tsv
```

- With `--template`, the bindings stand in for `DATA_DIR`. A variable still needed after binding fails the run, by name.
- An unknown tag is an error listing the tags that exist.
- The local folder bindings of one workflow must share a folder, otherwise *Conflicting local roots for workflow …*.
- With `--project-config-path`, the file is left untouched: the bindings apply to this run only.
- `--bind` never guesses a manifest from a file name: use `--manifest`.

### Cross-filtering without a manifest

In an `s3_prefix` glob with a single `*`, what the `*` matches becomes each file's id (`sample_A.samples.csv` gives `sample_A`), read back as the `depictio_manifest_id` column. Two collections bound this way share a key, and a [link](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/data-model/#joining-and-linking) with the `direct` resolver cross-filters them. A bare `*`, several wildcards, `?` or `[` give no id.

## The data manifest contract

A manifest lists remote files, one entry per file. Its `type` is a **data collection tag**, which is all it takes to map it onto a project.

| Field  | Required | Meaning                                                                 |
| ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`   | yes      | Entity or sample id. Becomes `depictio_manifest_id`                     |
| `type` | yes      | The tag of the collection the file belongs to                           |
| `url`  | yes      | `s3://` or `https://`; `http://` only with `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_ALLOW_HTTP` |
| `run`  | no       | Becomes `depictio_run_id`, `remote` when absent                         |

```
id,type,url,run
S1,counts,https://data.example.org/run42/S1.counts.parquet,run42
S1,stats,https://data.example.org/run42/S1.stats.tsv,run42
S2,counts,https://data.example.org/run42/S2.counts.parquet,run42
```

```
{
  "version": "1",
  "entries": [
    {"id": "S1", "type": "counts", "url": "https://data.example.org/run42/S1.counts.parquet", "run": "run42"},
    {"id": "S1", "type": "stats",  "url": "https://data.example.org/run42/S1.stats.tsv",      "run": "run42"}
  ]
}
```

A bare list of entries works too.

The schema is closed: other CSV columns go into an `extra` field. A file listed twice is refused. Entries of the same `type` are aggregated into one collection. Other column names are mapped with `id_field`, `url_field`, `type_field` and `run_field` (see the [reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/reference/#manifest-the-entries-of-a-data-manifest)).

An nf-core samplesheet becomes a manifest in one command, each file column a `type` ([all options](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#manifest-from-table)). A YAML or JSON samplesheet, a list of records, is read exactly as the same CSV (v1.22.0+):

```
depictio manifest from-table samplesheet.csv --id-col sample --base-url s3://my-bucket/run42 -o manifest.json
```

## Creating a project in the web UI

### From a run folder

**New project**, **Add data**, then **Read in place** with **Folder or bucket** (see [Create a project](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/guide/#create-a-project)). Depictio recognises the pipeline from the run's records, picks the template and previews each collection before anything is created.

| Run folder           | Read when                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `s3://bucket/prefix` | The server may read the bucket ([rules](#reading-s3-buckets)), or you give its keys ([Private bucket](#private-bucket-at-creation))                                                                                                                                   |
| `/path/to/run`       | Only on a [`depictio local`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/local/index.md) server, below your home folder or a folder added with [`--data-root-allow`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/local/#up-options) |

The variables and collection locations must stay inside the run folder; the CLI has no such limit.

**Checks** compares the run with the template, one line each: **Pipeline**, **Version**, **Engine**, **Tasks**, **Folder**, **Input files**, **Samples**, **Collections**. The verdict is **Exact match**, **Closest available version** or **Different version**. Each collection then shows where it **Looks in** and what it found: **Found**, **Not found**, **Optional, not found**. The eye beside a file previews its first rows. When nothing matched, **Nothing to ingest in this folder** blocks the next step.

**Create Project** imports the template's dashboards and ingests the collections in the background. **Project created** follows them one by one, with **Open dashboard**; closing it does not stop the workers. The run is recorded under the project's [ingestion history](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#ingestion-history) and in [**Log & Task → Ingestion**](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/monitoring/#ingestion), command `from_run`.

Ingestion order, missing sources, time limits

A collection whose source is missing is not sent to a worker: **Failed** when required, **Skipped** when optional. One built from another collection's table waits for it, up to 30 minutes, and each collection has 30 minutes to ingest. The server's Celery worker runs them: the [ingestion worker](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/#ingestion-worker) is not needed.

#### The folder browser

**Browse** opens **Choose a folder to read in place**, with a **This computer** group (under `depictio local`) and an **S3** group (the locations the server may list, and a private bucket once its keys are given). A folder holding `pipeline_info/`, or MultiQC output under `multiqc/`, carries a **Run folder** badge and explains **Why this is a run folder**. **Pipeline runs in subfolders** searches below a folder for runs, and **Filter by name** narrows a long folder.

#### Private bucket

For an `s3://` folder, **This bucket needs credentials** opens the **Private bucket** fields: **Endpoint** (empty for Amazon S3), **Region** (optional, the connection test fills it in), **Access key** and **Secret**. It opens by itself when the bucket refuses the read. The keys are used for that bucket only, for every read of the creation, and become the project's [storage settings](#project-storage-settings): **Project created** confirms *Storage settings saved for this project*. On a public instance, only administrators can give them.

#### From a script

```
# $DEPICTIO_TOKEN: user.token.access_token from your CLI configuration
curl -X POST "$API/depictio/api/v1/projects/from_run" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPICTIO_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"data_root": "s3://my-bucket/ampliseq/run42", "dry_run": true}'
```

| Field                                      | Default                | Content                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `data_root`                                | required               | The run folder                                                                                         |
| `template_id`                              | detected               | Such as `nf-core/ampliseq/2.16.0`                                                                      |
| `project_name`, `description`, `is_public` | derived, none, `false` |                                                                                                        |
| `variables`                                | `{}`                   | As `--var` on the CLI                                                                                  |
| `dry_run`                                  | `false`                | Preview only                                                                                           |
| `storage`                                  |                        | `endpoint_url`, `region`, `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key` of a private bucket; both keys required |

The report lists each collection as the preview does, then `project_id`, the imported dashboards, `storage_saved` and a `run_id` to poll at `GET /projects/refresh_manifest/{run_id}`. A refusal carries `detail` and a `code` such as `template_not_detected` or one of the [S3 codes](#s3-errors); a taken name answers 409. The folder browser uses `GET /projects/templates`, `/local_dirs`, `/s3_dirs`, `/folder_inspect`, `/find_runs`, `POST /projects/run_file_preview` and `/storage_test`.

### From a manifest

The web UI no longer has a manifest tab (v1.21.0): use the CLI or the API.

```
depictio ingest --template generic/manifest-tables/1 \
  --manifest https://data.example.org/run42/manifest.json
```

`--manifest` takes an `https://` URL or a local file, sets the template's `MANIFEST_URL` and replaces `DATA_DIR`.

```
curl -X POST "$API/depictio/api/v1/projects/from_manifest" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEPICTIO_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"manifest_url": "https://data.example.org/run42/manifest.json",
       "template_id": "generic/manifest-tables/1", "dry_run": true}'
```

Also `project_name` and `variables`. The call ingests before it returns, and reports `unmatched_manifest_types` and `pruned_optional_dcs`.

`POST /projects/ingest_manifest` with `project_id` and `manifest_url` maps the manifest's types onto the project's tags, switches each matched collection to manifest mode and ingests it. A collection that fails gets its former scan back. `dry_run` reports the mapping only.

The server fetches a manifest through the [gateway](#what-the-server-checks-before-fetching) and checks every entry URL first: if any is refused, nothing is ingested and the 400 lists `rejected_entries`. An `s3://` manifest is not read yet: serve it over `https://`.

## Refreshing the data

When the files behind a project change, refresh it in place: **Project settings**, then **Data refresh**.

- **Collections**: **All refreshable collections**, or one. Only a manifest, a URL or a bucket prefix can be refreshed; with none, the section says **Nothing to refresh**.
- **Refresh now** reads again what changed, new and changed files, and leaves the rest. **Read everything again** rebuilds every collection.
- The progress is followed for up to 30 minutes, with **Reload project** at the end. Closing the dialog does not stop it, and a notification says how it ended.

Owners, editors and administrators can refresh; on a public instance, administrators only. A local folder is refreshed with the CLI, [`depictio ingest … --update-config`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#refreshing-a-project). A project made from a run folder is checked against it again first: a required collection whose source is gone fails, an optional one is skipped, and neither is emptied.

| Status       | API value    | Meaning                                                                                                                 |
| ------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Planned**  | `planned`    | Dry run: would be refreshed                                                                                             |
| **Queued**   | `dispatched` | Handed to a worker                                                                                                      |
| **Running**  | `running`    | Being ingested                                                                                                          |
| **Ingested** | `ingested`   | Table rebuilt, a new [data version](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/#data-versions) |
| **Failed**   | `failed`     | **Details** says why                                                                                                    |
| **Skipped**  | `skipped`    | Optional and absent                                                                                                     |

From a script, `POST /depictio/api/v1/projects/refresh_manifest` takes `project_id`, and optionally `data_collection_tag`, `dry_run`, `full` (read everything again) and `async_run` (return a `run_id` to poll at `GET …/refresh_manifest/{run_id}`). An asynchronous refresh is recorded in the [ingestion history](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#ingestion-history), command `refresh_manifest`.

[**Run ingestion**](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#run-ingestion) and [`depictio watch`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#watch-command) read local folders only: on remote data, use **Data refresh**.

## Reading S3 buckets

An `s3://` location a user gives is matched against the configuration before any request, so naming a bucket never reveals whether it exists. The first matching rule wins:

| Rule | Location                                                                             | Read with                                                            |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | The bucket holding the instance's own data                                           | Refused                                                              |
| 2    | The bucket of the project's [storage settings](#project-storage-settings), with keys | The project's keys                                                   |
| 3    | Listed in `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_PUBLIC_S3_BUCKETS`                                        | No credentials, on Amazon S3                                         |
| 4    | Anything else, when the project has storage settings                                 | Those settings only                                                  |
| 5    | Listed in `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_CREDENTIALED_S3_BUCKETS`                                  | The server's AWS default chain (environment, IAM role, web identity) |
| 6    | Anything else                                                                        | Refused                                                              |

Both lists take comma-separated `bucket` or `bucket/prefix` entries ([environment reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#remote-data-sources)). Anyone on the instance can read what the credentialed list names. The instance's own S3 keys are never used for a user's location. The CLI reads from its own machine: a public bucket without keys, any other with the keys of its configuration or the machine's AWS credentials.

### Errors

| Code                | HTTP | Meaning                                                |
| ------------------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `s3_refused`        | 422  | No rule allows the read; nothing was sent              |
| `s3_access_denied`  | 422  | The bucket refused the credentials, or there were none |
| `s3_no_such_bucket` | 422  | No such bucket on that endpoint                        |
| `s3_wrong_region`   | 502  | The bucket is in another region                        |
| `s3_unreachable`    | 502  | The storage could not be reached                       |
| `s3_error`          | 502  | Any other S3 error                                     |

In the run folder flow, `s3_refused` and `s3_access_denied` open the [Private bucket](#private-bucket-at-creation) fields.

### Project storage settings

**Project settings**, then **Storage**, for owners and administrators. **Configure storage** asks for:

| Field                                    | Content                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Endpoint URL**                         | Such as `https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com`. Through the API, empty means Amazon S3 |
| **Bucket**                               | Required                                                                             |
| **Region**                               | `us-east-1` by default; **Test connection** detects and saves it                     |
| **Access key ID**, **Secret access key** | Both empty for a public bucket. The secret is stored encrypted and never shown again |

The saved settings show **Secret set** or **No secret**, with **Test connection**, **Edit** and **Remove**. They are read credentials only: tables are still written to the instance's storage. They are deleted with the project, never exported in a template, and kept encrypted in a [backup](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/backup/index.md). An endpoint on a private network must be on `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_ALLOWLIST`, and `http://` needs `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_ALLOW_HTTP`. API: `GET`, `PUT`, `DELETE /projects/{project_id}/storage` and `POST …/storage/test`; see [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#per-project-storage-credentials).

The CLI reads the same fields from `remote_storage_options` in its configuration:

```
remote_storage_options:
  endpoint_url: https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com
  bucket: my-bucket
  region: eu-west-1
  access_key_id: AKIA...        # leave both keys out for a public bucket
  secret_access_key: ...
```

## Google Cloud Storage (v1.21.0+)

GCS speaks S3 through its [XML API](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/interoperability): set `endpoint_url: https://storage.googleapis.com` in the project's storage settings or in `remote_storage_options`, with an HMAC key (Cloud Storage, **Settings**, **Interoperability**) for a private bucket. Then point a collection at `s3://<bucket>/<key>`.

- Reading only: GCS cannot be the instance's own storage.
- The folder browser asks for keys on a GCS bucket, since `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_PUBLIC_S3_BUCKETS` covers the AWS endpoint only.
- A public bucket was checked end to end; a private one with an HMAC key not yet.

## Sharing a project

A project can be frozen into a template bundle that someone else runs on their own instance, against their own data.

1. **Export**: **Project settings**, **Create a template**: a **Template ID** (`my-lab/rnaseq-qc/1`), a **Version**, a **Description (optional)** and a **Data root (optional)**. Or `depictio template export <project_id> --template-id my-lab/rnaseq-qc/1 -o ./templates`. The bundle holds `template.yaml` and `dashboards/*.yaml`, with the data root as `{DATA_ROOT}` and a manifest URL as `{MANIFEST_URL}`.

1. **Send** the folder by git, zip or chat.

1. **Run** it with each collection bound to the recipient's data:

   ```
   depictio ingest --template ./templates/my-lab/rnaseq-qc/1 \
     --bind samples=s3://their-bucket/run7/*.samples.csv \
     --bind metadata=/data/run7/metadata.tsv
   ```

A project read from an `s3://` folder

The export checks the bundle with a local test path as `{DATA_ROOT}`, which `s3_prefix` and `url` collections refuse: it stops with *Exported config does not round-trip through Project validation*. From the CLI, `--data-dir ""` exports without a data root.

To copy the project itself, data included, use **Export as a ZIP file** or **Send to another instance**: see [Project migration](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/migrate/index.md). The full export reference is on [Templates](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/templates/#export-a-project-as-a-template).

## What the server checks before fetching

Every `https://` URL a user gives goes through one gateway: a scheme allowlist, DNS resolution refusing private, loopback and reserved addresses, a check at every redirect, and a streamed download with a size cap and a timeout. `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_ALLOWLIST` pins the hosts, exclusively while set, and `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_DENYLIST` blocks some. A refused fetch answers `remote_url_rejected` (400), a failed one `remote_fetch_failed` (502). Details on [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#remote-data-sources).
