```
- tag: viz-secondary-structure
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: ss_calls
  viz_kind: secondary_structure
  config:
    viz_kind: secondary_structure
    entity_col: entity
    position_col: position
    state_col: ss_code
    source_col: ss_source
    reference_source: S4PRED
    p_helix_col: p_helix
    p_strand_col: p_strand
    p_coil_col: p_coil
```

### Predicted aligned error

v1.19.0+ `viz_kind: pae_matrix`

A model's PAE matrix with pLDDT strips. A low-error block on the diagonal is a confident domain. A brush picks the scored range.

**Input:** one PAE file per protein (a `pae` file collection, `pae_dc_tag`), plus a residue table, one row per residue.

| Column     | Config key     | Need                         | Type    | Example  |
| ---------- | -------------- | ---------------------------- | ------- | -------- |
| `position` | `position_col` | required                     | Numeric | `1`, `2` |
| `entity`   | `entity_col`   | optional, picks the PAE file | String  | `P04637` |
| `plddt`    | `value_col`    | optional, the pLDDT strips   | Numeric | `41.2`   |
| `chain`    | `chain_col`    | optional, chain boundaries   | String  | `A`      |

See [The data](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/proteins/#the-data).

**Compatible inputs:** proteinfold PAE TSV, AlphaFold DB or ColabFold JSON.

**Controls**

- Primary: Entity, Colours
- Cosmetic: pLDDT strips, brush (diagonal, rectangle)

YAML

```
- tag: viz-pae-matrix
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: residues
  viz_kind: pae_matrix
  config:
    viz_kind: pae_matrix
    pae_dc_tag: pae_files
    entity_col: entity
    position_col: position
    value_col: plddt
```

### Ramachandran

v1.19.0+ `viz_kind: ramachandran`

Backbone phi and psi of the model, computed in the browser from the 3D tile's file. The favoured regions are a guide, not MolProbity contours.

**Input:** the structure file of the [3D structure](#molecule-3d) tile, plus a residue table, one row per residue.

| Column         | Config key     | Need                                  | Type    | Example       |
| -------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------- |
| `position`     | `position_col` | required                              | Numeric | `175`, `858`  |
| `entity`       | `entity_col`   | optional                              | String  | `P04637`      |
| `chain`        | `chain_col`    | optional                              | String  | `A`           |
| `conservation` | `value_col`    | optional, point colour                | Numeric | `0.82`        |
| `domain`       | `category_col` | optional, point colour                | String  | `DNA-binding` |
| `uniprot`      | `uniprot_col`  | optional, `structure_source: resolve` | String  | `P04637`      |
| `gene`         | `gene_col`     | optional, `structure_source: resolve` | String  | `TP53`        |
| `sequence`     | `sequence_col` | optional, `structure_source: resolve` | String  | `MEEPQSDPSV`  |

**Compatible inputs:** The structure file the 3D tile reads.

**Controls**

- Primary: Protein, Colour by, Residue classes
- Cosmetic: Approximate favoured regions, marker size, follow selection

YAML

```
- tag: viz-ramachandran
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: residues
  viz_kind: ramachandran
  config:
    viz_kind: ramachandran
    structure_dc_tag: structures
    entity_col: entity
    position_col: position
    color_mode: plddt
```

# Architecture

Depictio is built on a modern microservices architecture that provides flexibility, scalability, and maintainability.

The figure draws the default: the browser reads indexed files (genome tracks, 3D structures) from S3 through presigned URLs. With `DEPICTIO_S3_BROWSER_ACCESS=proxy` (v1.22.0+) they go through the API instead (see [Data Flow](#data-flow)).

## Microservices Overview

Depictio's architecture consists of six main components organized by category:

### Core Services

| Component    | Technology             | Purpose                                                                   |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Backend**  | FastAPI                | RESTful API, authentication, business logic                               |
| **Frontend** | React + Vite + Mantine | Vite SPA served by nginx, which also proxies the API; no state of its own |

### Data Layer

| Component    | Technology                  | Purpose                         |
| ------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| **Database** | MongoDB                     | Metadata, users, configurations |
| **Storage**  | S3 (SeaweedFS when bundled) | Data files, Delta Lake tables   |

### Infrastructure

| Component        | Technology | Purpose                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Cache/Broker** | Redis      | DataFrame cache, Celery queue and results, live events                                             |
| **Worker**       | Celery     | Previews, code figures, screenshots, MultiQC; always on. A second worker for ingestion is optional |

______________________________________________________________________

### FastAPI Backend

The backend service is built with FastAPI, a modern, high-performance web framework:

- RESTful API endpoints for all platform functionality
- JWT-based authentication and authorization
- Asynchronous request handling for improved performance
- Pydantic models for data validation and serialization
- Beanie ODM for MongoDB integration

### MongoDB Database

MongoDB serves as the primary database, storing:

- User accounts and authentication information
- Project metadata and configurations
- Workflow definitions and run information
- Dashboard layouts, structure, and content
- Data collection metadata

### S3 Storage

S3-compatible object storage holds:

- Processed data ready for visualization (Delta Lake format)
- Genome-browser compatible data
- Large file assets

Docker Compose and the Helm chart bundle [SeaweedFS](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs) as the store since v1.12.0 (MinIO before). Any S3 endpoint can replace it: see [External S3](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/#external-s3).

### Redis Cache/Broker

Redis serves three purposes in Depictio, each on its own database:

- **Caching** (db 0): DataFrames read from Delta tables, and the per-address limit on sign-in attempts
- **Task Broker** (db 1 and 2): message broker and result backend for Celery background tasks
- **Live events** (db 3): the pub/sub channel of [real-time events](#real-time-events-v114)

Sessions are not kept in Redis: tokens live in MongoDB, and the browser keeps its own copy.

### Frontend — React viewer

The frontend is a Vite + Mantine **React SPA** (`depictio/viewer/`, shared `packages/depictio-react-core/`), graduating onto canonical URLs in **v1.0.0**. It provides:

- Interactive data visualization components
- Real-time data updates
- Draggable and customizable dashboard layouts
- Integration with the backend API

The legacy Plotly Dash frontend was removed in v0.13.12. See the [changelog](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/changelog/index.md) for the full migration history.

______________________________________________________________________

## React SPA Surfaces (v1.0.0+)

The React viewer (`depictio/viewer/`) is a single Vite SPA served by nginx with a fallback rewrite. It exposes three logical surfaces against the same FastAPI backend:

| Surface        | URL Pattern                          | Purpose                                            |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| **Management** | `/dashboards`, `/projects`, `/admin` | Dashboard listing, project management, admin panel |
| **Viewer**     | `/dashboard/{id}`                    | Read-only dashboard viewing                        |
| **Editor**     | `/dashboard-edit/{id}`               | Dashboard editing and component creation           |

During the v0.12–v0.13 series the same surfaces ran at `/*-beta` paths alongside the legacy Dash frontend. Dash was removed in v0.13.12; the `*-beta` suffix paths redirect to canonical in v1.0.0.

______________________________________________________________________

## Background Processing (v0.6.0+)

Depictio supports **background task processing** using Celery and Redis for computations that would otherwise block the UI.

### When Background Processing is Used

The worker always runs; there is nothing to turn on.

| Work                          | Runs on the worker                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Figure previews in the editor | By default (`DEPICTIO_CELERY_OFFLOAD_PREVIEW`)                                                                            |
| Dashboard renders             | When the source table is 50 MB or more, or always with `DEPICTIO_CELERY_OFFLOAD_RENDERING`                                |
| Code figures                  | Always, to keep user code off the API                                                                                     |
| Dashboard thumbnails          | Always                                                                                                                    |
| Offloaded ingestion           | On the separate [ingestion worker](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/#ingestion-worker) |

### Environment Variables

| Variable                            | Default | Description                                   |
| ----------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_CELERY_WORKERS`           | `4`     | Worker processes, set on the worker container |
| `DEPICTIO_CELERY_BROKER_HOST`       | `redis` | Redis broker hostname                         |
| `DEPICTIO_CELERY_BROKER_PORT`       | `6379`  | Redis broker port                             |
| `DEPICTIO_CELERY_BROKER_DB`         | `1`     | Redis database for Celery broker              |
| `DEPICTIO_CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND_DB` | `2`     | Redis database for Celery results             |

All of them, including the offload thresholds: [Celery Task Queue](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#celery-task-queue).

______________________________________________________________________

## Real-time Events (v1.1.4+)

Depictio can push **live dashboard updates over WebSocket** when the data behind a dashboard changes, so viewers refresh without polling. The subsystem is disabled by default (`DEPICTIO_EVENTS_ENABLED`) and opt-in per project.

Moving parts:

- **Event service + connection manager** (FastAPI): track WebSocket subscriptions per dashboard and broadcast `data_collection_updated` events.
- **Redis pub/sub**: fans events out across API workers and replicas, on a dedicated Redis DB (default `3`, separate from cache and Celery).
- **MongoDB change streams** (optional, requires a replica set): detect data-collection changes at the database layer.
- **WebSocket channel** `/depictio/api/v1/events/ws`: JWT-authenticated via a `token` query parameter and permission-checked at viewer level; the React viewer subscribes per dashboard and drives the live indicator.

Activation requires both the server flag and a `realtime` block in the project's `project.yaml`.

See the [Real-time events guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/realtime-events/index.md) for setup, and the [environment reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#real-time-events) for the full `DEPICTIO_EVENTS_*` list.

______________________________________________________________________

## Data Flow

The figure at the top of this page draws it:

1. **CLI** reads the run's files, writes the Delta tables to S3 itself, then registers them through the API (`/deltatables/upsert`), which records the metadata in MongoDB. *Add data* in the web UI does the same on the server.
1. **API** answers every figure, table and card: it reads the Delta tables from S3, with the frames cached in Redis.
1. **React viewer** only talks to the API, through its nginx proxy. It never reaches MongoDB, Redis or S3, except for indexed files (genome tracks, 3D structures), read from S3 through presigned URLs. With [`DEPICTIO_S3_BROWSER_ACCESS=proxy`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#s3-browser-access) (v1.22.0+) the API streams those too, for an S3 store browsers cannot reach.

______________________________________________________________________

## Related Documentation

- [Dashboards](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/index.md) - Dashboard modes, tabs, and layouts
- [Components](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/components/index.md) - Available component types
- [Data Model](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/data-model/index.md) - Domain objects and relationship model
- [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/index.md) - Security features and code restrictions
- [Real-time events](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/realtime-events/index.md) - Enabling live WebSocket dashboard refresh

# Comments and Annotations

Discuss a dashboard where the data is: comment threads on a component or a whole tab, and annotations drawn on top of charts, tables and maps.

## Overview

There are two things you can attach to a dashboard:

- **Comments**: a thread on one component, or on the whole tab. Threads take replies, can be resolved and reopened, and remember the filters and the selection that were active when they were written.
- **Annotations**: a shape drawn on a component, in the style of newsroom charts: a highlighted range, a reference line, a set of marked points or rows, or a note with an arrow. Every annotation is also a thread, so it has the same badge, the same drawer and the same discussion as a plain comment.

One section of the Palmer Penguins dashboard with annotations on four charts: x and y ranges, reference lines, arrow notes, marked points inside a shaded box or lasso region, and rings on box-plot outliers.

Stored outside the dashboard

Threads and annotations are kept in their own MongoDB collection, not in the dashboard document. Saving the dashboard or editing its layout never drops them, and after a YAML re-import they re-attach to their components (see [below](#when-the-data-or-the-component-changes)). They are not part of a dashboard's YAML export, but [backups](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/backup/index.md) include them. Deleting a dashboard, a tab or a project deletes its threads. Annotations are drawn by the viewer on top of the figure at render time: nothing is recomputed on the server, and the component's own definition is unchanged.

Comments and annotations live in the dashboard **viewer** (`/dashboard/{id}`), not in the editor.

______________________________________________________________________

## Who can see what

| Who                                               | Comments and annotations                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Project **owners** and **editors**                | Read and write every thread on the project's dashboards                                                                                                                                                     |
| Instance **admins**                               | Same as owners                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Project **viewers**                               | No threads, no badge, no drawer. They see only the annotations switched to **Visible to viewers**, as a shape and a label. With [viewers can comment](#viewers-can-comment) on, they read and write threads |
| Visitors of a **public** project, anonymous users | Same as viewers: published annotations only, never a discussion                                                                                                                                             |
| **Single-user mode**                              | The session is the instance admin, so everything is available                                                                                                                                               |

The discussion itself is never shown to viewers. Publishing an annotation exposes its shape, its colour and its label, nothing else.

Thread actions follow the author:

- an editor or owner can reply, resolve, reopen, edit an annotation and change its visibility;
- you can edit or delete **your own** comments; a project owner can also delete anyone's comment (it is replaced by *Comment deleted*);
- a whole thread can be deleted by its author, a project owner or an admin.

### Viewers can comment (v1.17.2+)

A showcase instance may want remarks from the people it shows a dashboard to, without giving them edit rights. `DEPICTIO_COMMENTS_VIEWERS_CAN_COMMENT=true` (default `false`) lets anyone with viewer access to a project read and write its threads:

- a viewer replies, edits or deletes their own comments, and deletes their own threads;
- resolving or reopening a thread, publishing or editing an annotation, annotate mode and agent proposals stay with editors and owners; a viewer never sees proposals or rejected threads;
- anonymous visitors and the temporary accounts of public mode never comment. Since v1.17.3 a guest is offered to [sign in](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/authentication-modes/#guest-sign-in) instead.

Commenters see each other's email addresses. On Kubernetes, the setting is the `backend.env` key of the same name.

______________________________________________________________________

## The comments drawer

There are two ways in, both visible only to editors and owners (and to viewers when [they may comment](#viewers-can-comment)):

- the **Comments** button in the dashboard header opens every thread of the current tab. Its badge counts open threads (or, when there are none, proposals awaiting review), and its tooltip also counts threads whose data changed;
- the **comments icon** in a component's action bar opens that component's threads. A number badge counts open threads, a pulsing violet dot flags agent proposals awaiting review, and the icon turns **orange** when one of the component's open threads no longer matches its data or its definition (see [When the data or the component changes](#when-the-data-or-the-component-changes)).

Left: the **Comments** tab on the whole tab, with a thread flagged *Data changed*. Right: the **Annotations** tab, grouped by component, each card carrying its numbered badge.

The drawer docks on the right without covering the dashboard, so clicking a thread can scroll the page to its component:

- **Scope line.** Under the title, either *Whole tab · N components with threads*, or *On* followed by the component's name. The pill's **x** goes back to the whole tab. In the whole-tab view, threads are grouped by component; clicking a group header narrows the drawer to that component.
- **Comments / Annotations.** Two tabs, each with its count. Plain comments and annotations are listed apart.
- **Show.** Status chips: **Open**, **Resolved** and **Proposed**. Open and Proposed are on by default.

### Writing a comment

The composer sits at the bottom of the **Comments** tab. It says what you are commenting on (*Commenting on the whole tab*, or a component's name), and lists what will be attached:

- the **active filters** (*N active filters will be attached*);
- the **current selection** on that component, when there is one (points, bars or rows selected on the dashboard).

Type the comment and press **Post** (or Ctrl+Enter). A comment holds up to 4,000 characters.

### Working with a thread

Each thread card shows its author, the time it was written, its status, and badges for what it captured (a selection, *N filters*) and for staleness. Below the discussion:

| Action                   | Effect                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Reply**                | Adds a comment to the thread (up to 500 per thread)                                        |
| **Resolve** / **Reopen** | Moves the thread between Open and Resolved                                                 |
| **Show on dashboard**    | Scrolls to the component, highlights it, and re-applies the thread's filters and selection |
| **Delete thread**        | Deletes the thread and all its replies, after a confirmation                               |

Show on dashboard restores the view, not the past

The filters and selection come back, but they are applied to today's data and to the component as it is now. If either changed since the thread was written, the thread says so (see below). If the component was removed, a notice says so instead of scrolling.

______________________________________________________________________

## Annotating a component

### Annotation shapes

| Tool                                            | Kind            | What it draws                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Range on x** / **Range on y**                 | Range highlight | A band across one axis, behind the data. Drag a box: only its x (or y) extent is kept          |
| **Vertical line** / **Horizontal line**         | Reference line  | A dashed line at one x or y value, in front of the data. Click to place it                     |
| **Mark points (lasso)** / **Mark points (box)** | Marked points   | Rings around the selected points or bars, optionally with the selected area shaded behind them |
| **Note**                                        | Note            | A numbered label with an arrow pointing at a data point. Click a point to attach it            |

Shapes are stored in **data coordinates**, so they keep their place when the figure is resized, zoomed or redrawn. Marked points are stored by the component's selection column when it has one, so they follow their rows across re-sorting and re-ingestion; charts without one (bars, histograms) store plain coordinates.

### Drawing an annotation

1. Hover the component and click **Annotate** () in its action bar. A tool palette appears in the top-left corner of the figure, with a one-line hint under it.
1. Pick a tool. Zoom and pan stay available from the Plotly modebar; while they are active no tool is highlighted, and clicking a tool again goes back to drawing.
1. Draw. The shape appears as a dashed preview with a live count, for example *18 points in range* or *40 points*.
1. Fill in the popover: a **Label** (required, up to 120 characters), a **Color**, for marked points **Highlight the selected area** and its **Area opacity**, an optional **Comment** to start the discussion, and **Visible to viewers**. Press **Save**.
1. Click (or press Esc) to leave annotate mode.

Drawing never touches the dashboard: annotate mode detaches the component's cross-filtering, so a lasso drawn for an annotation does not filter or clear anything.

Annotate mode on a scatter plot: the tool palette with **Mark points (lasso)** active, the lassoed points previewed on the chart, and the form for the new annotation.

Each annotation gets a number on its tab, shown as a badge (①, ②, ...) in the annotation's colour, on the chart and on its card in the drawer. Hovering a label on the chart shows what it covers, such as the range and the number of points inside it.

A y range, an arrow note, points marked inside a shaded box, and a threshold line.

A lasso region around one group of points, with a note and a reference line.

Rings on box-plot outliers, drawn where the points actually sit.

Two x ranges on an overlaid histogram.

### Editing an annotation

Click an annotation's label (or one of its rings) on the chart. A popover opens in place, titled after its kind, with:

- **Label** and **Color**;
- for a range highlight: **Opacity**;
- for a reference line: **Line style** (**Solid**, **Dashed**, **Dotted**) and **Line width**;
- for marked points: **Ring width**, and **Highlight the selected area** with its **Area opacity** when the points were drawn with a region.

Changes are previewed live on the chart; **Cancel** puts the saved version back. The popover also offers **Open discussion**, which jumps to the thread in the drawer, and **Delete annotation**. The same editor opens from **Edit annotation** on the thread's card in the drawer.

Clicking the label of a range highlight: its hover summary, and the inline editor with the label, the colour and the opacity.

### Showing an annotation to viewers

**Visible to viewers** is off by default: a new annotation is internal to the project's editors and owners. Switch it on, in the creation form or on the thread's card, and viewers of the dashboard see the shape and its label. They never see the discussion, and clicking a published annotation opens nothing for them. An agent's annotation cannot be published until a person accepts it.

______________________________________________________________________

## Where you can annotate

The **Annotate** action only appears on components that can take a shape. Comments work on every component, and on the tab itself.

| Component                   | Annotations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Figures**                 | Every cartesian Plotly figure: all four shapes. 3D, polar, pie and hierarchical charts (sunburst, treemap, icicle) and parallel coordinates are comment-only                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Advanced visualizations** | The single-panel cartesian kinds: volcano, MA, QQ, Manhattan, embedding (2D only), scatter, DA barplot, ANCOM-BC differentials, stacked bar, rarefaction, enrichment, dot plot, lollipop (one gene shown), PR benchmark, ROC / PR curve, confusion matrix, metric CI bars, profile, GSEA running score (single panel) and coverage track (single panel, not in the Locus view) |
| **MultiQC figures**         | Line and bar graphs and other plots drawn on one pair of axes. Marked points are stored as **sample names**, so marking a line graph rings whole sample lines. Multi-panel figures are comment-only                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **MultiQC General Stats**   | Row annotations in the table view, keyed on the sample name (not in the violin view)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Tables**                  | Tables with a row-id column (`row_selection_column` or `selection_column`): rows can be marked                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Maps**                    | Scatter and choropleth maps: **Mark points** (lasso or box, with an optional shaded longitude / latitude region) and **Note**. Ranges and lines have no meaning on a map. Density maps are comment-only                                                                                                                                                                        |

Multi-panel and non-cartesian advanced visualizations (complex heatmap, oncoplot, signal matrix, sashimi, UpSet, sunburst, Sankey, phylogeny) stay comment-only: a shape needs a single pair of axes.

A significance line, marked genes and notes on a volcano plot; a genome-wide line and a peak note on a Manhattan plot; a lasso cluster on a UMAP; marked loci on a QQ plot; an NES range and marked terms on an enrichment dot plot; a plateau range on rarefaction curves.

Sample lines marked as a whole, and a quality threshold line.

Annotated rows in the General Statistics table.

Marked rows, with their badges in the pinned annotation column.

A shaded longitude / latitude region, marked sites and a note on a scatter map.

### Marking table rows

In annotate mode a table shows a single **Mark rows** tool in its top-right corner. Click rows to select them, then press **Mark N selected rows**. Marked rows get the annotation's numbered badge in a narrow column pinned to the left of the grid.

### Components with several views

Some components show one of several plots: a MultiQC component switching dataset, between counts and percentages or to a log scale, and advanced visualizations whose tile offers several views on different axes (volcano / MA / QQ, marker dot plot / enrichment, PR / ROC). An annotation remembers the view it was drawn on and only appears on that view, so a line drawn on the volcano never lands on the MA plot's axes.

______________________________________________________________________

## When the data or the component changes

When a thread is written, Depictio records a fingerprint of the component's definition and of every data collection it reads. Each time threads are listed, both are compared with the dashboard as it is now, and the thread card shows:

| Badge                 | Meaning                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Data changed**      | A data collection the component reads was processed again since the thread was written. Any new aggregation counts, even a re-ingest of identical files |
| **Component changed** | The component's definition was edited. Moving or resizing the tile does not count                                                                       |
| **Component removed** | The component is no longer on the tab                                                                                                                   |
| **M of N found**      | Some of the points or rows an annotation marked are not in the chart's current data                                                                     |

Open threads with changed data or a changed component also turn the component's comments icon orange, so staleness is visible on the dashboard without opening the drawer.

After a dashboard is re-imported from YAML, components may come back with new identifiers. A thread whose component seems gone re-attaches itself to the component with the same title, when exactly one component on the tab has that title.

______________________________________________________________________

## Agent proposals

Threads and annotations can also be written by an agent, through the comments API. An agent always acts **on behalf of** the user whose credentials it uses, and its threads are held for review:

- an agent's thread starts as **Proposed**. Its annotation is drawn faded and dashed, and it appears under the **Proposed** chip;
- the card shows the agent's name, *Agent on behalf of* the person who launched it, and the **Evidence** the agent attached (structured claims backing its comment);
- **Accept** turns the proposal into an ordinary open thread. **Reject** asks for an optional reason, then hides the thread and keeps the decision;
- a proposal cannot be resolved, and its annotation cannot be made **Visible to viewers**, until it is accepted. If a person edits a proposed annotation, the card says **Edited by a human**.

Running the same agent again updates its earlier pending (or rejected) proposals instead of duplicating them; a re-proposed rejection goes back to review. One agent run can open at most 50 threads.

Comments are data, not instructions

The text of a comment is never treated as an instruction for an agent reading the dashboard.

______________________________________________________________________

## Known limits

- A range on a **categorical** axis stores category positions, so it moves if the order of the categories changes.
- Rings on box, violin and bar points are drawn as shapes: hover and click-to-edit go through the numbered label there.
- On charts with marginal plots, y ranges and horizontal lines also span the marginal panels.
- When the id column repeats a value, a mark resolved by id rings only the first matching row.
- Long labels placed in data coordinates can stretch the axis range, and labels near the edge of the plot can be clipped.
- On maps, labels are numbered `(1)`, `(2)`, ... rather than ①, ②.
- There are no mentions or notifications yet.

- [Interactive Selection Filtering](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/interactive-selection-filtering/index.md): the selections a comment can capture
- [Backup & Restore](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/backup/index.md): what a snapshot covers

# Component export and embedding (v1.17.0+)

A component of a dashboard can be served to another website, live, in one of two formats:

- **Plotly spec (JSON)**: `{data, layout, config, meta}`, drawn by the site's own plotly.js and styled like the rest of its page.
- **Embeddable page (HTML)**: one self-contained page running Depictio's own renderer, for an `<iframe>` or to keep as a file. It makes no network call once loaded.

Both read the dashboard as it is now, with its latest data: the link always returns the current state of the component.

| You want to                                        | Where                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Get the link, `curl` or snippet for one component  | The tile's **Export / embed** action                                                                                       |
| Know which components export in which format       | `GET …/export/dashboards/{id}/components`                                                                                  |
| Turn the feature on, or let a site frame the pages | [`DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_*`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#component-export) |

______________________________________________________________________

## Turning it on

The export API is **off by default**: serving embeds relaxes the framing protections on its path, and lets callers without a token read public projects. An administrator turns it on in the server's environment:

| Variable                                   | Default |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_ENABLED`           | `false` | Serve the export routes and show **Export / embed** on the tiles. Off, every route answers `404` with `code: embed_disabled`                                                                                                                                        |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`   | empty   | Sites allowed to frame an exported page, comma-separated (`https://lab.example.org`). They become the page's CSP `frame-ancestors` and may also fetch the JSON format from a browser. Empty: the pages open on their own but no site can frame them. `*` is refused |
| `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_CSP_UNSAFE_INLINE` | `false` | Allow inline scripts in the exported page instead of listing the hashes of its scripts. Only for a bundled script that cannot be hashed ahead of time                                                                                                               |

The Helm chart (`backend.env`), both compose files and `.env.example` carry the first two, and `depictio local up` passes them on from the shell that starts it:

```
DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_ENABLED=true depictio local up
```

The HTML format needs the embed bundle

The page is built from a prebuilt bundle, `depictio/viewer/dist-embed/embed.html`. The Docker images include it. The Python package does not yet, so on a server installed with `pip` or `uv tool` (`depictio local` included), `format=html` answers `503` with `code: bundle_unavailable` while the JSON format works. From a checkout, `cd depictio/viewer && pnpm run build:embed` builds it.

______________________________________________________________________

## From a tile

While the API is on, every tile of the viewer has an **Export / embed** action, among the actions shown when the pointer is over it.

The action opens a dialog that names the component and its type, then offers:

- **Mode**: *Plotly spec (JSON)* or *Embeddable page (HTML)*. A mode the component does not have is greyed out, and its tooltip says why. The dialog opens on JSON when the component has it.
- **Theme**: light or dark.
- **Include the current filters (N)**: the filters active on the dashboard, carried in the link. Without it, the export draws the component unfiltered.
- **Snippets**: the URL, a `curl` command, and a `plotly.js` snippet for JSON or an `<iframe>` for HTML, with **Open** and **Copy**. Past 2000 characters, the `curl` command switches to the `POST` form.

The dialog warns when a link will not work as is:

- **Private project**: the link answers `403` without a token. The snippets send `Authorization: Bearer $DEPICTIO_TOKEN`, to be replaced with a long-lived token from **Account settings → CLI agents**. Your own session token never goes into a snippet. An `<iframe>` cannot send a token, so embed a page from a public project.
- **No site may frame this page yet**: `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_EMBED_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is empty.

There is no **Export / embed** on filter controls, on genome browser tiles, or while a past [version](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/index.md) is shown, since the export always serves the current dashboard. A tile of a [section shown on every tab](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#persistent-sections) exports from the tab that owns it.

______________________________________________________________________

## What exports how

| Component                                | JSON                  | HTML                |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------- |
| Figure, map                              |                       |                     |
| MultiQC                                  |                       |                     |
| Advanced visualization                   | some kinds, see below | all but three kinds |
| Table, card, image, text, filter control |                       |                     |
| Genome browser                           |                       |                     |
| Highlight                                |                       |                     |

- **JSON** needs a figure the server can build in Python. For advanced visualizations that is the complex heatmap, UpSet plot and Sankey, and the volcano (with its MA and QQ views), embedding, Manhattan, stacked bar, differential abundance bar plot, sunburst, the dot plot's enrichment view and the four benchmarking kinds. The other kinds answer `501`, with the URL of their HTML page in `html_url`.
- **HTML** runs the viewer's renderer, so every component it draws in the browser renders the same way. Three advanced visualizations have no offline page: the genome view, the contact map and group comparison, which fetch or compute data as you zoom or select, and neither has a tile saved on a GenomeSpy view.
- The **genome browser** reads its track files by byte range from the API as you move around, so it has no offline page. A **highlight** draws another tab's component: export that one instead.

The manifest says the same for a given dashboard, per component, with the reason for any missing format. Read it rather than hardcoding the table.

______________________________________________________________________

## The API

All routes are under `/depictio/api/v1/export`:

| Route                                                       | Returns                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /dashboards/{dashboard_id}/components`                 | The manifest: every component with its `component_id`, type, `viz_kind`, title, `formats`, and `json_unavailable_reason` or `html_unavailable_reason` |
| `GET /dashboards/{dashboard_id}/components/{component_id}`  | The component in one format                                                                                                                           |
| `POST /dashboards/{dashboard_id}/components/{component_id}` | The same, with `filters`, `theme` and `controls` in a JSON body, for filters too long for a URL                                                       |

Parameters of the `GET`:

| Parameter         |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `format`          | `json` (default) or `html`                                                                                                                                               |
| `theme`           | `light` (default) or `dark`                                                                                                                                              |
| `filters`         | A URL-encoded JSON array of filters, see below                                                                                                                           |
| `controls`        | A URL-encoded JSON object of the component's own controls, such as `{"view": "ma"}` for a volcano saved on another view. Without it, the component draws as it was saved |
| `expect_revision` | The revision this caller was built against. If the component or its data has changed since, `409` instead of a different result                                          |

```
BASE=https://depictio.example.org/depictio/api/v1/export/dashboards/$DASH

# What this dashboard can export
curl -s "$BASE/components" | jq '.[] | {component_id, component_type, formats}'

# One figure as a Plotly spec, one table as a page
curl -s "$BASE/components/$FIGURE?format=json" | jq '.meta'
curl -s "$BASE/components/$TABLE?format=html" > table.html
```

```
<iframe src="https://depictio.example.org/depictio/api/v1/export/dashboards/DASH/components/CID?format=html"
        width="100%" height="420" style="border: 0" loading="lazy"></iframe>
```

### Filters

Each filter control of a dashboard is in the manifest with a `filter` entry: the column it filters, its type and the kind of control. With `?include_filter_options=true`, the entry also carries the values the control offers, distinct values or a min and max, so a host page can build its own control. This option reads every filtered column, which is why it is off by default.

```
{
  "component_id": "ce2962ed-…",
  "component_type": "interactive",
  "title": "Variety",
  "formats": ["html"],
  "filter": {
    "interactive_component_type": "MultiSelect",
    "column_name": "variety",
    "column_type": "object",
    "options": {"kind": "categorical", "values": ["Setosa", "Versicolor", "Virginica"]}
  }
}
```

A filter sent to the export is that entry with a `value`: a list of values for a select, `[min, max]` for a range.

```
curl -sG "$BASE/components/$FIGURE" --data-urlencode format=json \
  --data-urlencode 'filters=[{"column_name": "variety", "interactive_component_type": "MultiSelect", "value": ["Setosa"]}]'
```

`meta.filter_applied` in the JSON says whether filters were sent.

### Caching and pinning

Every response carries a weak `ETag` and an `X-Depictio-Revision` header, both readable from JavaScript on another site, and the JSON repeats the revision in `meta.revision`. The revision changes when the dashboard's content changes or when a collection the component reads is ingested again.

- Send `If-None-Match` with the `ETag` to get a `304` while nothing changed.
- Send `?expect_revision=` with a `meta.revision` to get a `409` (`code: revision_mismatch`) instead of a component that has moved on.

### Access

The export applies the dashboard's [permissions](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#permissions), in every [authentication mode](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/authentication-modes/index.md):

- a **public** project's components export without a token;
- a **private** project's need a bearer token of a user who can view it. Without one, the caller is always an anonymous non-admin, even on a single-user server, so only public projects are readable.

### Errors

| Status | When                                                                                           |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`  | `filters`, `controls` or `theme` is not valid                                                  |
| `403`  | A private project without a valid token                                                        |
| `404`  | The export API is off (`embed_disabled`), or no such dashboard or component                    |
| `409`  | `expect_revision` no longer matches (`revision_mismatch`)                                      |
| `422`  | The component has no such format (`unsupported_export`)                                        |
| `501`  | JSON for an advanced visualization drawn only in the browser. `html_url` points to its page    |
| `503`  | The HTML bundle is missing (`bundle_unavailable`), or a MultiQC figure is still being prepared |

______________________________________________________________________

## Limits

- **Live only.** The export serves the current dashboard and its latest data, and takes no version. The action is hidden while a past version is shown.
- **Saved controls.** An advanced visualization's thresholds, top-N or view are read from its saved settings, not from what a viewer has changed in their browser. Pass `controls` for another state.
- **Linked filters.** Without a token, a filter on one data collection does not reach components of another collection through a [cross-DC link](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/cross-dc-filtering/index.md). Authenticated exports follow the links.

______________________________________________________________________

## Behind your own reverse proxy

The exported page sets its own `Content-Security-Policy` and leaves out `X-Frame-Options`, so that the listed sites can frame it. A proxy that adds either header to every response defeats that: browsers enforce every CSP they receive, so a site-wide `frame-ancestors 'self'` blocks the embed. The nginx configuration of the Docker images has a separate `location` for `/depictio/api/v1/export/` for this reason. A proxy of your own needs the same exception.

### Building under active filters (v1.5.2+)

With filters applied, the builder previews the **filtered** data. An **Apply to preview** toggle switches back to the full dataset. Applies to every type except Text and MultiQC, which have no row filtering. See [Dashboard creation](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/guides/dashboard_creation/#previewing-with-active-filters-v152).

______________________________________________________________________

## Figure Components (v0.0.1+)

Figure components display data visualizations using Plotly charts. They support both **UI Mode** (drag-and-drop configuration) and **Code Mode** (Python code for custom plots).

### Supported Chart Types

**UI Mode** provides a curated selection of chart types through the visual interface:

| Category         | Chart Types                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Basic Charts** | Scatter, Bar, Line                                                                                  |
| **Statistical**  | Histogram, Box                                                                                      |
| **Matrix**       | ComplexHeatmap (via [plotly-complexheatmap](https://github.com/weber8thomas/plotly-complexheatmap)) |

Unlimited Charts with Code Mode

**Code Mode** supports the entire Plotly library, giving you access to all chart types including 3D plots, maps, financial charts, and more. See the [Plotly Python documentation](https://plotly.com/python/) for the complete reference.

### UI Mode

In UI Mode, configure charts through the visual interface:

1. Select a **Data Collection** as your data source
1. Choose the **Chart Type** (scatter, bar, histogram, etc.)
1. Map data columns to **X-axis**, **Y-axis**, and optional **Color** dimension
1. Customize appearance (title, axis labels, colors)

### Code Mode

Code Mode allows custom Python code for advanced visualizations:

```
import plotly.express as px

# df is your data collection as a pandas DataFrame
fig = px.scatter(
    df,
    x="coverage",
    y="quality_score",
    color="sample_type",
    title="Coverage vs Quality by Sample Type"
)

# Return the figure object
fig
```

Since **v1.14.0** a code figure that sets no colours of its own is drawn in the dashboard's [category colours](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#category-colors) when every trace name, *Other* aside, is a value of one coloured column; the map itself is `depictio_category_colors`. A template's `color_discrete_map=depictio_group_kwargs.get("color_discrete_map", {})` counts as setting none while no analysis group is active.

Security Note

Code Mode uses [RestrictedPython](https://restrictedpython.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) for security. Only approved libraries (pandas, plotly) are available. See [Security](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/index.md) for details.

### Configuration Options

| Option       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Default                 |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| Title        | Chart title displayed at top                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Auto-generated          |
| X-axis label | Label for horizontal axis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Column name             |
| Y-axis label | Label for vertical axis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Column name             |
| Color        | Column for color encoding                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | None                    |
| Hover data   | Additional columns shown on hover                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | None                    |
| `max_points` | Point cap for scatter-family figures before downsampling (v1.3.0+)                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Global default (10,000) |
| `font_scale` | Font-size multiplier for the whole figure layout font: axis labels, ticks and legend. Set from the tile's edit menu, 0.7× to 2×, with a full lite-YAML round trip (v1.8.0+)                                                                                                    | Unset (1×)              |
| Theme        | Plotly template for this figure. `mantine_light` / `mantine_dark` mean *follow the UI colour scheme*. Unset falls back to the dashboard default, then to [instance branding](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/branding/index.md) (v1.8.0+) | Unset                   |

### Figure style (v1.14.0+)

`figure_style: minimal` gives a figure the landing-page look: the title in the card header beside an icon badge with the subtitle inline, a transparent plot with faint dashed grid lines and no axis lines, the legend in one line under the plot, large unoutlined markers, tight margins and the toolbar only on hover. Bars end in a slight round, stacked segments are parted by a hairline, and grouped bars get a coloured underline naming each group instead of facet titles. Plots in this style are set in Inter unless the figure or the brand sets a font. Unset, a figure takes the `figure_style` of its [grid section](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#landing-tabs), else `default`. In the builder these keys are the **Card header & style** section.

| Option                     | Description                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `figure_style`             | `default` or `minimal`                                                                                                 |
| `subtitle`                 | A few dimmed words after the title (`minimal`)                                                                         |
| `icon_name` / `icon_color` | Iconify id and colour of the header badge (`minimal`). The colour defaults to the brand's primary                      |
| `hide_legend`              | Draw the figure without its legend, for a small tile                                                                   |
| `caption`                  | A line or two under the plot saying how to read it, in any style                                                       |
| `link`                     | `tab:<name>`: the tab this figure summarises, linked from the end of the header (`minimal`) or from the tile's actions |

An advanced visualization takes `figure_style`, `subtitle`, `icon_name`, `icon_color` and `link` for its card only: `minimal` draws the header and the frame, not the plot overlay, and `link` shows in that header alone. `hide_legend` is honoured by the [phylogeny summary](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#phylogenetic), and `caption` is not drawn. Its component-level `controls_placement` says where its controls dock; see [Controls and where they go](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#controls).

```
- tag: pcoa-overview
  component_type: figure
  visu_type: scatter
  figure_style: minimal
  title: Communities by city
  subtitle: PCoA, Bray-Curtis
  icon_name: mdi:scatter-plot
  caption: Each point is one sample; the closer two points, the more alike their plankton.
  link: "tab:Ordination & Clustering"
  # workflow_tag, data_collection_tag, dict_kwargs...
```

Clustered heatmaps moved

The ComplexHeatmap viz is now the [Hierarchical heatmap](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#hierarchical-heatmap) advanced visualization.

### Selection Filtering (Scatter Plots)

Scatter plots can act as interactive filters. Enable selection to let users lasso, box-select, or click points to filter other components.

| Option              | Description                                 |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `selection_enabled` | Enable selection filtering (`true`/`false`) |
| `selection_column`  | Column to extract from selected points      |

See [Interactive Selection Filtering](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/interactive-selection-filtering/index.md) for details.

## Table Components (v0.0.2+)

Table components display data in interactive tables with built-in filtering and sorting.

### Features

| Feature                    | Description                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Server-Side Pagination** | Efficiently handles large datasets by loading data in pages  |
| **Server-Side Scrolling**  | Virtual scrolling for smooth navigation through large tables |
| **Column Sorting**         | Click headers to sort ascending/descending                   |
| **Column Filtering**       | Filter by column values                                      |
| **Export** (v0.6.0+)       | Download data as CSV                                         |

### Configuration

| Option            | Description                                       | Default            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Data Collection   | Source data for the table                         | Required           |
| Visible Columns   | Allowlist of columns to display; omit to show all | All columns        |
| Page Size         | Rows per page (`10`, `25`, `50` or `100`)         | `100`              |
| Compact (v1.2.2+) | Tighter row and header heights                    | Off                |
| Style             | Column width, text alignment                      | Auto               |
| Title             | Header text above the table                       | Auto (from DC tag) |
| Description       | Subtitle text below the title                     | None               |
| Title Size        | Header level: `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, or `sm`           | `sm`               |
| Title Align       | Text alignment: `left`, `center`, or `right`      | `left`             |

### Row Selection Filtering

Tables can act as interactive filters. Enable row selection to let users click rows to filter other components.

| Option                  | Description                                     |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `row_selection_enabled` | Enable row selection filtering (`true`/`false`) |
| `row_selection_column`  | Column to extract from selected rows            |

See [Interactive Selection Filtering](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/interactive-selection-filtering/index.md) for details.

## Advanced Visualizations

Domain charts that know their column roles: a volcano binds a feature, an effect size and a significance, a genome view a chromosome and a position. Over forty kinds cover differential analysis, single cell, genome tracks, variants, microbiome, benchmarking and proteins. See [Advanced visualizations](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/index.md) for every kind with a screenshot, the data it reads, its controls and a YAML example.
