## The data

Every protein tile reads tables joined on two column names: `entity` (which protein) and `position` (the 1-based residue number in the structure's numbering). A tile shows one entity at a time: the one the filters name, else the reader's pick, else the first.

| Input               | Shape                                                                                                                                                              | Read by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Structure files** | `indexed_file` collection, `format: pdb` or `mmcif`, one file per entity, the sample id equal to the `entity` value. Predictors write pLDDT in the B-factor column | [3D structure](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#molecule-3d), [Ramachandran](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#ramachandran)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Residue table**   | `entity`, `position`, optionally `chain`, `residue`, `value`, `category`                                                                                           | [3D structure](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#molecule-3d), [Sequence track](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#sequence-track), [Secondary structure](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#secondary-structure), [Predicted aligned error](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#pae-matrix), [Ramachandran](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#ramachandran) |
| **Variants**        | `entity`, `position`, `ref_aa`, `alt_aa`, a consequence and a label                                                                                                | [3D structure](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#molecule-3d), [Sequence track](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#sequence-track)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Domains**         | `entity`, `start`, `end`, `label`, optionally `source`                                                                                                             | [Sequence track](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#sequence-track), [Domain architecture](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#domain-architecture)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Alignment**       | `msa_id` (the `entity` it aligns), `seq_id`, `rank` (0 is the query), `aligned_sequence`                                                                           | [Alignment](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#msa)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **PAE files**       | `indexed_file` collection, `format: pae`: proteinfold TSV, AlphaFold DB or ColabFold JSON                                                                          | [Predicted aligned error](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#pae-matrix)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

The helpers in `depictio/recipes/lib/` (`protein_structure`, `msa`, `hmm`, `secondary_structure`, `pae`) build these tables. See [Recipes](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/recipes/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## Linked by residue

- **A pick is a filter.** A click or brush emits a `residue_selection`: the entity, a `position` range and, on a complex, the chain. Every table with those columns narrows, and every protein tile shows the range. The last gesture wins.
- **A hover is not.** Pointing at a residue marks it in every protein tile, in the browser only.
- v1.19.1+ **Zoom can follow.** Turn on the sync icon of a tile, or a section's button, and the other residue tiles and the 3D model follow its zoom.
- A [lollipop](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#lollipop) joins with `selection_enabled: true`, a [profile](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/advanced-visualizations/#profile) with `residue_axis: true`. Cards and figures that do not draw the position column ignore the range.

## Where the structure comes from

`structure_source: file` reads the run's own files and makes no outbound call. The browser fetches them from S3 through presigned URLs, or through the API with [`DEPICTIO_S3_BROWSER_ACCESS=proxy`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#s3-browser-access) (v1.22.0+) when browsers cannot reach S3 (the tile otherwise fails with *Failed to fetch*). `structure_source: resolve` asks the server for a model by UniProt accession, by gene and taxon, or by sequence. The resolver is off until `DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_ENABLED=true`, and tries, first hit wins:

1. its cache in the instance bucket;
1. AlphaFold DB, by accession;
1. UniProt, gene and taxon to an accession, then AlphaFold DB;
1. ESMFold, for a sequence of at most 400 residues.

The tile credits the service it used. A `pae_matrix` has no resolver path. See [External structure services](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/security/#structure-resolver) for what leaves the server and the [environment reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#structure-resolver) for the settings.

## Numbering mismatch

A variant table and a model do not always number residues alike (a construct, an isoform, an off-by-one). A variant whose `ref_aa` disagrees with the model is listed under a *numbering mismatch* badge instead of being drawn on the wrong residue; one past the end of the model is counted under *outside the model*.

# Runs and run comparison (v1.21.0+)

A project made from a pipeline can hold several runs of it. The project's **Runs** tab says what each run produced and what each scan changed, and **Compare** opens a dashboard with what one run changed marked.

[![](../../images/guides/compare-runs/compare-runs.webp)](../../images/guides/compare-runs/compare-runs.mp4)

| Needs                                                    | For                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A project made from a pipeline run                       | The **Runs** tab                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Owner or editor role                                     | Attaching a run, refreshing data                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `DEPICTIO_DASHBOARD_VERSIONS_CHANGES_SINCE_ENABLED=true` | **Compare**, the dot on new runs, the marked new rows, the dashboard history in **Activity**. See [*"What's new"*](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/whats-new/#turn-it-on) |

## Attach a run

On the project page, **Add data** on the folder of another run of the same pipeline reads **Add run**: Depictio recognises it as a run. See [Remote data and manifests](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/index.md).

**Duplicate samples.** If the run's MultiQC reports name samples the project already holds, the dialog lists them and holds the run back until you resolve them.

Every Delta row carries the run that wrote it, in `depictio_run_id`: that is how Depictio tells runs apart.

## The Runs tab

One row per run, new runs marked with a dot. Unfold a run to see its folder, its files and its scans. A run's files are read only once you unfold it. Two workflows of a project that share a run tag keep their files and scans apart (v1.22.0+).

### Produced

The **Produced** block of a run lists its ingestions, the Delta commits it wrote and its MultiQC reports. Each Delta commit has **View rows**, which opens that collection's Data table with the run's rows on top (see [New rows in the Data table](#new-rows-in-the-data-table)).

### Scans and file statuses

Pick a scan under **Scans**. Each file then says what that scan did to it:

| Status        | Meaning                                            |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| **New**       | This scan brought the file                         |
| **Changed**   | This scan found the file changed and read it again |
| **Failed**    | This scan could not read the file                  |
| **Unchanged** | Brought by an earlier scan, not changed since      |

A changed file shows its size and date before and after. A MultiQC report also lists the samples and modules it gained or lost. **Only what this scan changed** hides the rest.

## Compare a dashboard with a run

**Compare** on a run opens a dashboard with what that run changed marked. With one dashboard, its tooltip names it; with several, a menu lists them under **What this ingestion changed in**.

The dashboard opens read-only at `?before_run=<run id>`. Its header key reads **This ingestion**, and each changed tile's **Before | Now** draws the data just before the run beside the data now. This view never moves your own *"What's new"* mark.

**Layout before <run>** opens each dashboard's definition as it last was before the run (a `?version=` preview). It shows the layout and components, not the data: an ingestion records no dashboard version, so the preview's data is whatever that version pinned.

MultiQC rows have no run column: MultiQC figures compare on new samples instead. See [MultiQC: compare runs](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/multiqc/#compare-runs).

## New rows in the Data table

**View rows** in **Produced**, or **Open in project** in the [*"What's new"* panel](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/whats-new/#panel), opens the collection's Data table read-only at `?table=<collection>&new_runs=<runs>`. The new rows come first and are marked, the rows you had seen follow, faded. **Hide what you had seen** drops them, **Back to full table** returns to the plain table.

## Data refresh

**Project settings → Data refresh** reads again a collection the server can reach: one from a manifest, a URL or a bucket prefix. Pick a collection, or leave the field empty to refresh them all, then **Refresh now**. Data ingested from a local folder is refreshed with the CLI ([`depictio ingest`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/depictio-cli/usage/#ingest-command)).

By default a refresh reads only what changed:

- the new and changed files are read, the files that are gone are dropped;
- a collection whose files and configuration match its last successful refresh is skipped;
- a MultiQC report whose source did not change is kept, and a rewritten one records what it gained or lost.

**Read everything again** reads every file and rebuilds every collection, changed or not: after an upgrade, or to repair a collection. When the refresh ends, **Reload project** shows the result.

Manifest and URL collections are read again on every refresh: their hash names the source, not its content. A refresh that rewrites identical rows writes a commit, but *"What's new"* does not count it.

[![](../../images/guides/data-updates/refresh-new-rows.webp)](../../images/guides/data-updates/refresh-new-rows.mp4)

## The Activity tab

The project's **Activity** tab has two views:

| View                 | Shows                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Latest ingestion** | The report of the last ingestion                                                                                                                |
| **History**          | Ingestions, dashboard versions and comments, newest first. An ingestion opens onto its steps. The list refreshes every 3 seconds while one runs |

Where the server can read the project's files, **Run ingestion** beside the view switch starts an ingestion on the server and switches to **History**.

**Activity** replaces the **Ingestion report** and **Timeline** tabs. Old links (`?tab=ingestion`, `?tab=timeline`, `#ingestion`, `#ingestion-history`) still open it. With *"What's new"* off, **History** is the list of ingestion runs it was before.

## Limits

- A run ingested again in place changes rows under the same run tag. **Before | Now** shows it, Split does not.
- Run times use the server's local clock.

- [Dashboard and data versions](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/#data-versions)

# Security Features

Depictio implements comprehensive security measures to protect your data and ensure safe operation in production environments.

______________________________________________________________________

## Authentication

### JWT-Based Authentication

Depictio uses JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for secure authentication:

| Feature                | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Token Security**     | Public/private key encryption (RS256)                                                                                         |
| **Algorithm Pinning**  | Algorithm pinned server-side (RS256/RS512); `alg=none` and algorithm-confusion attacks are rejected before any MongoDB access |
| **Claim Validation**   | Signature and `exp` claim are both verified on every request; expired tokens are rejected immediately                         |
| **Session Management** | Access token 1 hour, refresh token 7 days; a CLI token lasts 1 year                                                           |
| **Storage**            | The browser keeps the pair in local storage; the server keeps every live token in MongoDB, so deleting one revokes it         |
| **Token Refresh**      | Automatic refresh before expiration                                                                                           |

### Authentication Flow

### Registration Hardening

The `/register` endpoint strips the `is_admin` field from any incoming payload, so self-promotion to admin at registration is not possible. Admin privileges are granted exclusively via the `/auth/turn_sysadmin` endpoint, which enforces two guards: at least one admin must remain in the system at all times (last-admin guard), and a user cannot demote themselves (no-self-demote guard).

### Session Configuration

Token lifetimes are fixed. The signing algorithm is `DEPICTIO_AUTH_KEYS_ALGORITHM`, `RS256` by default: see the [environment reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

Depictio implements a hierarchical permission system for fine-grained access control.

### User Roles

| Role       | Description        | Typical Use                 |
| ---------- | ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| **Admin**  | Full system access | System administrators       |
| **User**   | Standard access    | Project members             |
| **Viewer** | Read-only access   | Collaborators, stakeholders |

### Permission Levels

Permissions are applied at multiple levels:

### Project Permissions

| Permission              | Admin | Editor | Viewer |
| ----------------------- | ----- | ------ | ------ |
| View dashboards         | Yes   | Yes    | Yes    |
| Create dashboards       | Yes   | Yes    | No     |
| Edit dashboards         | Yes   | Yes    | No     |
| Delete dashboards       | Yes   | No     | No     |
| Manage project settings | Yes   | No     | No     |
| Manage project members  | Yes   | No     | No     |

### Group-Based Access (v1.18.0+)

A project can be shared with [groups](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/groups/index.md) as owner, editor or viewer, beside its individual users. A user's role is the **highest** of their own role and their groups' roles, so a direct viewer whose group owns the project is an owner.

Since v1.18.0 every access check (projects, dashboards, workflows, files, tables, MultiQC, advanced visualizations, events, runs, the catalog and the screenshot service) goes through one module, `depictio/api/v1/permissions.py`, where these hand-rolled checks had drifted apart:

- an anonymous visitor matches public projects only;
- editors now pass every viewer-level read;
- renaming a data collection or editing its properties needs **editor**, and deleting one needs **owner**, where a direct viewer could write and an editor could not;
- `PUT /projects/update` checks the stored project and no longer writes `permissions`: sharing goes through the Permissions page or `POST /projects/update_project_permissions`.

A refusal is the same 404 as a missing resource. `GET /groups/list` returns names only, never membership.

______________________________________________________________________

## Code Execution Security (Code Mode)

When using Code Mode for custom visualizations, Depictio implements strict security measures.

### RestrictedPython Security

Depictio uses [RestrictedPython](https://restrictedpython.readthedocs.io/) (Zope Foundation) for secure code execution:

| Feature                        | Description                                     |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| **Battle-Tested**              | Used in production by Zope/Plone for 20+ years  |
| **Compile-Time Restrictions**  | Unsafe operations blocked during compilation    |
| **Safe Execution Environment** | Pre-approved globals and built-ins only         |
| **No System Access**           | File system, network, and OS operations blocked |

### Security Architecture

### Allowed Operations

```
# Available libraries in Code Mode
import plotly.express as px      # Visualization library
import plotly.graph_objects as go # Advanced plotting
import pandas as pd              # Data manipulation
df                               # Your dataset (read-only copy)

# Safe built-in functions
len(), range(), str(), int(), float(), sum(), min(), max()
list(), dict(), tuple(), set(), sorted(), reversed()
```

### Blocked Operations

RestrictedPython prevents these operations at compile-time:

| Category                | Blocked Operations                                        |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| **File Operations**     | `open()`, file I/O, filesystem access                     |
| **Network Access**      | `requests`, `urllib`, socket operations                   |
| **System Calls**        | `os.*`, `sys.*`, `subprocess`, shell commands             |
| **Dangerous Built-ins** | `exec()`, `eval()`, `__import__()`, `compile()`           |
| **Attribute Access**    | Private attributes (underscore methods) on unsafe objects |

### Locking figure code (v1.21.0+)

A code figure runs Python on a server worker. On an instance open to people you do not know, such as a workshop, set `DEPICTIO_VIEWER_CODE_FIGURES_LOCKED=true`. The server then refuses new figure code from anyone but an administrator, and the figure builder shows "Writing figure code is turned off on this server." Code already on a dashboard or shipped with a template or the catalogue keeps rendering, and saving, moving or duplicating dashboards still works. UI mode stays available for new figures.

### Past versions in a render (v1.15.0+)

A render request can draw a component as a past [dashboard version](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/index.md) defined it. The request names that version with `definition_version`, and the server reads the component from its own record of the version. A request cannot send a component definition, so the code of a code-mode figure always comes from a saved dashboard.

- A request that carries `component_overrides` is refused with 400.
- A version that no longer exists, or belongs to another dashboard, is refused with 400.
- A component that read another data collection in that version is refused with 409.

______________________________________________________________________

## Data Protection

### Encryption

| Data State     | Protection                                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **In Transit** | TLS 1.2+ for all HTTP communication              |
| **At Rest**    | MongoDB encryption, MinIO server-side encryption |
| **Tokens**     | RS256 asymmetric encryption                      |

### Data Isolation

- **Project boundaries**: Data strictly isolated between projects
- **User isolation**: Users can only access authorized projects
- **Delta Lake**: Versioned data with access controls
- **File-delete IDOR fix**: File-deletion permission is checked against `current_user.is_admin` (the requesting user's flag), not the file-owner's flag. This closes an IDOR where a non-admin could delete files owned by an admin account.

### Input Validation

All user input is validated:

- **Pydantic models** for API request validation
- **Sanitization** of user-provided text
- **Type checking** at API boundaries
- **Size limits** on uploads and queries

______________________________________________________________________

## Remote Data Sources (v1.16.0+)

The `url`, `s3_prefix` and `manifest` scan modes, and creating a project from a run folder, make the server read locations a user supplies, which is a textbook server-side request forgery surface. Every `https://` fetch, whether creating a data collection from a URL, ingesting a manifest, or a refresh task on the Celery worker, goes through one gateway module; every `s3://` read is decided by one [access module](#s3-locations); a folder on the server's disk is read only on a [`depictio local`](#folders-on-the-servers-disk) server, or by a **Run ingestion** inside the folders an administrator allowed. Nothing in server context reads a user-supplied location directly. See [Remote data and manifests](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/index.md) for the feature itself.

### What the gateway enforces

| Check                | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Scheme allowlist** | `https://` and `s3://`. Plain `http://` only with `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_ALLOW_HTTP=true`                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Address check**    | The host is resolved and private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast and unspecified addresses are rejected, including the cloud metadata endpoint                                                                                                                       |
| **Redirects**        | Every `Location` is re-validated against the same policy before it is followed; hops are capped by `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_MAX_REDIRECTS`                                                                                                                                              |
| **Bounded download** | Streamed, with a size cap (`DEPICTIO_REMOTE_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES`) and a per-operation timeout (`DEPICTIO_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_S`); a download that exceeds the cap is aborted and the partial file removed                                                                             |
| **Host lists**       | Exact host names, compared without case. `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_DENYLIST` always rejects. `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_ALLOWLIST` is exclusive while set, and a listed host bypasses the private-range check. An `s3://` location skips both: the [S3 rules](#s3-locations) apply instead |
| **Sanitised errors** | Transport and HTTP errors are logged with their cause and surfaced to the client without internal details                                                                                                                                                                       |

The policy is read from the environment on every call, so the API and the worker apply the same one as long as both are given the same `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_*` settings. The CLI, which fetches the user's own loopback and intranet hosts, reads directly but keeps the redirect and size caps.

Residual risk: DNS rebinding

The address is checked when the host is resolved, and a hostile resolver could answer differently between that check and the connection. The gateway does not pin the resolved address. Hardened deployments should run **allowlist-only**: set `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_URL_ALLOWLIST` to the hosts you trust, which turns the address check into a host check.

### S3 locations

Which bucket the server reads, and with which credentials, is decided from the configuration before any request goes out, so a bucket name typed by a user never becomes an existence or region oracle.

- The bucket that holds the instance's own data is refused as a source: it holds every project's data.
- The instance's own S3 keys are never used for a user-supplied location.
- A bucket is read without credentials when listed in `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_PUBLIC_S3_BUCKETS`, or with project storage settings that hold no key, and with the server's ambient credentials only when listed in `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_CREDENTIALED_S3_BUCKETS`. Anyone on the instance can read what the second list names. Both lists are empty by default.
- Any other bucket needs the project's storage settings, and is read with them alone. Settings typed in while creating a project from a run folder are the only credentials that request uses.
- Errors name the bucket and the prefix, never an endpoint of the instance, a key or a request id.

The full order is under [Reading S3 buckets](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/remote-data/#reading-s3-buckets). The CLI reads from the user's own machine and skips the instance-bucket refusal and the credentialed list.

### Folders on the server's disk

A server reads a local path stored on a project in two cases only: [**Run ingestion**](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#run-ingestion) (v1.15.0+), which reads inside `DEPICTIO_INGESTION_ALLOWED_DATA_ROOTS` alone, see [Starting an ingestion from the browser](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/#browser-trigger), and a `depictio local` server, which is the user's own computer. Otherwise, data ingested from a local folder is refreshed by the CLI that ingested it. On a `depictio local` server:

- Local folders are off unless `DEPICTIO_LOCAL_DATA_ROOTS` is set, and only in single-user mode (`DEPICTIO_AUTH_SINGLE_USER_MODE`). `depictio local up` sets both, with the home folder and the folders given with `--data-root-allow`. A server with roots but not in single-user mode logs a warning and keeps them off.
- Every local read (listing, inspecting, creating, refreshing) needs a request addressed to a loopback host (`localhost` or a loopback address), which also defends against DNS rebinding, from an administrator.
- Paths are resolved to their real path and confined to the roots. Hidden folders and the folders Depictio keeps for itself (`~/.depictio`, the local home, the keys and CLI configuration folders, the backups) are refused even below a root.
- A run folder over 100,000 files is refused. For a project made from a run folder, every template variable given as a path and every location a data collection scans must be inside it; one pointing elsewhere is refused.

Since **v1.18.0** a phylogeny tree's stored location follows the same rules. An `s3://` Newick goes through the [S3 location](#s3-locations) checks (never the instance bucket with the instance's keys), a local one is read only below the bundled projects or a `depictio local` folder, and an error no longer names the paths it tried.

### Per-project storage credentials

A project owner or an administrator can attach S3-compatible credentials so remote and manifest collections can read a private bucket.

- Credentials live in their own collection, never on the project document, so they cannot leak through project responses or exports. Template bundles never include them. An instance [backup](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/administration/backup/#what-is-covered) does, with the secret still encrypted: keep backup files as safe as the keys volume.
- The secret is **encrypted at rest** with a symmetric key stored next to the JWT key pair, in `DEPICTIO_AUTH_KEYS_DIR`. The API encrypts on write and the Celery worker decrypts inside refresh tasks, so backend and worker must mount the same keys volume; a worker with a keys directory of its own would mint a second key and find every stored secret unreadable.
- The secret is **write-only** in the API: responses only carry `has_secret`. An update that omits the secret keeps the stored one only while the access key, the endpoint and the bucket are unchanged, so a stored secret is never sent to another endpoint.
- Only project owners and administrators read or change the settings.
- The endpoint URL passes the same host gating as remote data URLs. The instance's own object storage is always allowed. Any other endpoint on a private network needs to be allowlisted, while an allowlist is set every endpoint must be on it, and `http://` needs `DEPICTIO_REMOTE_ALLOW_HTTP`. An empty endpoint, possible through the API only, means Amazon S3 and is not gated.
- The stored endpoint is checked again at every read, so tightening the host lists also stops settings saved before: their reads answer 409 until an owner updates them. A secret the instance cannot decrypt answers 500.
- These are read credentials only. Delta tables are still written with the instance's own storage configuration, and refresh workers re-read the credentials from the database rather than receiving them through the task broker.

### External structure services (v1.19.0+)

The [protein tiles](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/proteins/#structure-resolver) can fetch a model the run did not publish. The resolver is **off by default** (`DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_ENABLED`), because once on, exactly the accession, the gene and taxon, or the protein sequence leaves the server, to EBI's AlphaFold DB, UniProt or Meta's ESM Atlas. For an unpublished sequence that is a disclosure.

- Only the three configured hosts are contacted, redirects included and each re-checked.
- A model is capped in size (`MAX_BYTES`), each call and each request in time, and a body with no `ATOM` record is refused.
- Anonymous visitors of a public instance get a 403, so only signed-in users trigger calls.
- Models are cached in the instance bucket; failures are not.
- The tile names the service it called, with the endpoint under *Technical details*, and credits the model.

______________________________________________________________________

## Content Security Policy

Deployed instances send a Content-Security-Policy header. The development server sends none, so a policy violation only ever shows up on a deployment.

Most of the policy is `'self'`. Three allowances are not obvious, and are the ones to carry across if you replace the policy at a reverse proxy or ingress:

| Directive     | Allowance                          | Needed for                                                |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `script-src`  | `'unsafe-eval' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` | Plotly's WebGL renderer and the in-browser Python runtime |
| `connect-src` | `ws: wss:`                         | The real-time events WebSocket                            |
| `connect-src` | the basemap origins below          | Map tiles                                                 |

### Basemap origins

Maps load their style, glyphs, sprite and vector tiles over `fetch`, so `connect-src` governs them; allowing images is not enough. A map missing these renders blank.

```
https://basemaps.cartocdn.com
https://*.basemaps.cartocdn.com
https://tile.openstreetmap.org
```

The apex domain is listed separately because a `*.` wildcard does not match it.

The policy lives in two files

The API middleware (`depictio/api/main.py`) and the viewer's nginx template (`docker-images/nginx.conf.template`) each send their own copy, and the two must agree.

## Security Best Practices

### Genome browser track access (v1.20.0+)

The [genome browser](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/index.md) runs inside the viewer, not in an iframe, and the browser never talks to S3 or to a track host itself. Every track byte goes through the API's Range-capable track proxy:

- **Signed, expiring URLs.** The API hands the browser signed proxy URLs, valid for `DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_URL_TTL_S` seconds (6 hours by default). The proxy re-checks that the caller can read the data collection's project.
- **Ids, not URLs.** A request names a track of the collection's manifest, never a location, so a viewer cannot make the server fetch an address of their choosing.
- **Remote tracks need an allow-list.** A track read in place is refused unless its `https://` host is in `DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_HTTPS_HOSTS` or its `s3://` bucket is in `DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_S3_BUCKETS` (comma-separated lists). A listed S3 bucket is read with the server's credentials, so anyone who can open a collection pointing at it can read it: list only buckets that hold nothing private. In depictio's own data bucket, only the collection's `genomic_tracks/<dc_id>/` folder is served; a remote folder pointing elsewhere in it is refused.
- **Remote S3 credentials.** Without `DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_S3_ACCESS_KEY` and `DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_S3_SECRET_KEY`, remote buckets are read anonymously.
- **Direct access is opt-in.** A collection with `direct_access: true` has the browser fetch its `https://` tracks itself, which bypasses the proxy and needs the host to allow it with CORS.

The full variable list is in the [environment reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#genome-browser).

### OpenID Connect sign-in

[OpenID Connect single sign-on](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/sso/index.md) uses the authorization code flow with PKCE (`S256`). A callback is accepted only if it answers a login this instance started, and only once: the `state` is stored server-side in MongoDB and consumed atomically. The `nonce` binds the `id_token` to the login, and the token is verified against the provider's JWKS (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, with 60 seconds of clock-skew leeway). The email is trusted only when the provider asserts it is verified. The redirect URI comes from the configuration, never from the request, and redirects stay on this site. The browser is handed a single-use ticket in the URL fragment, so no token travels in a query string. Accounts created by single sign-on get a random password hash instead of an invalid placeholder.

### OAuth Callback Security

The OAuth callback validates that the redirect URL is same-origin before calling `window.location.assign`. This closes an open-redirect vulnerability where a crafted authorization response could send the user (and any attached tokens) to an attacker-controlled domain.

Since **v1.5.2** the CSRF `state` is stored in MongoDB (`oauth_states`), used once and expired by a TTL index. It was previously held in per-process memory, so sign-in only worked when the callback happened to reach the worker that issued the state.

`DEPICTIO_DEV_MODE` no longer skips state validation

The flag used to bypass this check entirely, leaving the callback without CSRF protection on any deployment that set it. It now only affects hot-reload and verbose logging.

### Deployment Recommendations

1. **Use HTTPS**: Always deploy behind TLS termination
1. **Secure MongoDB**: Enable authentication, use TLS
1. **Secure MinIO**: Enable access keys, use TLS
1. **Network Isolation**: Use private networks for internal services
1. **Regular Updates**: Keep dependencies updated

### Secret Management

| Secret                  | Recommendation                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| JWT Keys                | Generate unique keys per environment                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Database Credentials    | Use strong passwords, rotate regularly                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| API Keys                | Use environment variables, not config files                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| MinIO Credentials       | Separate credentials per environment; root password is a `SecretStr` with a ≥16-character validator and no default — the server refuses to start if the value is absent or matches a known-default string                   |
| Project storage secrets | Encrypted at rest with `secrets_key.bin` in `DEPICTIO_AUTH_KEYS_DIR`; back the keys volume up with the JWT key pair and mount it on the worker too, see [Per-project storage credentials](#per-project-storage-credentials) |

### Environment Configuration

```
# Example secure configuration
JWT_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH=/secrets/jwt_private.pem
JWT_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH=/secrets/jwt_public.pem
MONGODB_URI=mongodb://user:pass@mongo:27017/depictio?authSource=admin
MINIO_ACCESS_KEY=<generated-access-key>
MINIO_SECRET_KEY=<generated-secret-key>

# CORS — list allowed origins explicitly (comma-separated); wildcard with credentials is rejected
DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://your-domain.example.com

# Bootstrap admin (replaces initial_users.yaml)
DEPICTIO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<strong-password>
```

**CORS**: `allow_origins=["*"]` has been removed. Origins are configured via `DEPICTIO_FASTAPI_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (comma-separated list). A wildcard combined with `allow_credentials=True` is explicitly rejected by the framework and will raise a startup error.

**Admin bootstrap**: `initial_users.yaml` is replaced by env-driven bootstrap via `DEPICTIO_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. This avoids shipping a default credentials file and ensures the admin password is injected as a secret at deploy time.

### Kubernetes Security

When deploying on Kubernetes:

- Use **Secrets** for sensitive configuration
- Enable **Network Policies** to restrict pod communication
- Use **ServiceAccounts** with minimal permissions
- Enable **Pod Security Standards**
