```
      y: petal.length
      color: variety

  # Card: Metric with aggregation
  - tag: sepal-length-average
    component_type: card
    workflow_tag: python/iris_workflow
    data_collection_tag: iris_table
    section: Overview
    aggregation: average
    column_name: sepal.length
    icon_name: mdi:leaf
    icon_color: "#8BC34A"

  # Interactive: MultiSelect filter
  - tag: variety-filter
    component_type: interactive
    workflow_tag: python/iris_workflow
    data_collection_tag: iris_table
    section: Sample
    interactive_component_type: MultiSelect
    column_name: variety
    custom_color: "#858585"

  # Interactive: RangeSlider filter
  - tag: sepal-length-filter
    component_type: interactive
    workflow_tag: python/iris_workflow
    data_collection_tag: iris_table
    section: Sample
    interactive_component_type: RangeSlider
    column_name: sepal.length

  # Table: Data display
  - tag: data-table
    component_type: table
    workflow_tag: python/iris_workflow
    data_collection_tag: iris_table

  # Image: Gallery component
  - tag: sample-gallery
    component_type: image
    workflow_tag: python/image_workflow
    data_collection_tag: sample_images
    image_column: image_path
    thumbnail_size: 150
    columns: 3
    max_images: 9

  # MultiQC: Quality control report
  - tag: fastqc-quality
    component_type: multiqc
    workflow_tag: python/nf_workflow
    data_collection_tag: multiqc_report
    selected_module: fastqc
    selected_plot: per_base_sequence_quality

  # Figure: Clustered heatmap
  - tag: gene-expression-heatmap
    component_type: figure
    workflow_tag: python/bio_workflow
    data_collection_tag: expression_matrix
    visu_type: heatmap
    dict_kwargs:
      index_column: gene_name
      row_annotations: [gene_type]
      cluster_rows: true
      normalize: zscore

  # Map: Scatter map with selection
  - tag: sampling-map
    component_type: map
    workflow_tag: python/my_workflow
    data_collection_tag: sample_metadata
    lat_column: latitude
    lon_column: longitude
    color_column: biome
    hover_columns: [sample_id, site_name]
    map_style: carto-positron
    selection_enabled: true
    selection_column: sample_id
```

## Component Types Reference

| Type          | Description                                    | Required Fields                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `figure`      | Plotly charts (scatter, box, heatmap, etc.)    | `visu_type` (ui mode) or `code_content` (code mode)                                             |
| `card`        | Metric cards with aggregations                 | `aggregation`, `column_name`                                                                    |
| `interactive` | Filters (RangeSlider, MultiSelect, etc.)       | `interactive_component_type`, `column_name`                                                     |
| `table`       | Data tables                                    | *(none required — title auto-generated from DC tag)*                                            |
| `text`        | Headings and prose tiles                       | *(none required — `title` is the heading, `body` the prose)*                                    |
| `image`       | Image galleries from S3/MinIO                  | `image_column`                                                                                  |
| `multiqc`     | MultiQC quality control report viewer          | `selected_module`, `selected_plot`                                                              |
| `map`         | Geospatial maps (scatter, density, choropleth) | `lat_column`, `lon_column` (scatter/density) or `locations_column`, GeoJSON source (choropleth) |

### Figure Component

Two rendering modes are supported:

**UI Mode** (default) — select a chart type and pass Plotly Express parameters:

```
- tag: scatter-plot
  component_type: figure
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  visu_type: scatter       # see valid values below
  dict_kwargs:
    x: column_x
    y: column_y
    color: category_column
    title: Chart Title
```

**Valid `visu_type` values (UI mode):** `scatter`, `line`, `bar`, `box`, `violin` (v1.13.0+), `histogram`, `ecdf`, `strip`, `area`, `funnel`, `density_heatmap`, `density_contour` (v1.15.0+), `heatmap`

**Code Mode** — write arbitrary Python/Plotly code for full flexibility:

```
- tag: custom-plot
  component_type: figure
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  mode: code
  code_content: |
    import plotly.express as px
    fig = px.scatter_matrix(df, dimensions=["sepal.length", "sepal.width", "petal.length"])
```

**ComplexHeatmap** — clustered heatmap with annotations (via [plotly-complexheatmap](https://github.com/weber8thomas/plotly-complexheatmap)):

```
- tag: gene-expression-heatmap
  component_type: figure
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: expression_dc
  visu_type: heatmap
  dict_kwargs:
    index_column: gene_name
    value_columns: [sample_A, sample_B, sample_C]
    row_annotations: [gene_type, pathway]
    cluster_rows: true
    cluster_cols: true
    normalize: zscore
    colorscale: RdBu_r
    split_rows_by: gene_type
    cluster_method: ward
    cluster_metric: euclidean
```

Heatmap `dict_kwargs` parameters:

| Parameter                       | Type   | Description                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `index_column`                  | string | Column for row labels                                 |
| `value_columns`                 | list   | Numeric columns for the matrix (omit for all numeric) |
| `row_annotations`               | list   | Columns shown as colored side bars                    |
| `cluster_rows` / `cluster_cols` | bool   | Enable hierarchical clustering                        |
| `normalize`                     | string | `zscore`, `minmax`, or `none`                         |
| `colorscale`                    | string | Plotly colorscale (e.g. `RdBu_r`, `Viridis`)          |
| `split_rows_by`                 | string | Split heatmap rows by annotation column               |
| `cluster_method`                | string | `ward`, `average`, `complete`, `single`               |
| `cluster_metric`                | string | `euclidean`, `correlation`, `cosine`                  |

Code mode and visu_type

`visu_type` is not validated when `mode: code`. Any Plotly chart can be built in code mode. `code_content` must be non-empty when `mode: code`.

**Selection filtering** — enable lasso/box selection to filter linked components:

```
- tag: scatter-with-selection
  component_type: figure
  visu_type: scatter
  selection_enabled: true
  selection_column: sample_id   # required when selection_enabled=true
  # ...
```

### Card Component

**Single-metric card:**

```
- tag: metric-card
  component_type: card
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  aggregation: average
  column_name: numeric_column
  column_type: float64     # optional — enables offline aggregation validation
  icon_name: mdi:chart-line
  icon_color: "#2196F3"
```

**Multi-metric summary card** — secondary aggregations displayed below the hero value:

```
- tag: petal-length-summary
  component_type: card
  workflow_tag: python/iris_workflow
  data_collection_tag: iris_table
  aggregation: average           # hero metric (large display)
  aggregations:                  # secondary metrics (compact rows)
    - median
    - std_dev
    - min
    - max
  secondary_layout: grid         # optional — how the block below the hero is drawn
  column_name: petal.length
  column_type: float64
  icon_name: mdi:leaf
  icon_color: "#43A047"
  title: "Petal Length"
```

`aggregations` is read by the four list-driven layouts (`vertical`, the default; `compact`; `grid`; `box_plot`). The other twelve `secondary_layout` values compute their own block and ignore it — see the field table below.

**Number format** — `format` sets how the value and its secondary print:

| `format`     | Prints                                                                     |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `percent`    | A 0 to 1 share as a percentage: `41%`, `4.7%` under 10%, `0.032%` under 1% |
| `si`         | A large value with a suffix: `214k`, `3.7M`, `1.2G`                        |
| `integer`    | A whole number with thousands separators                                   |
| `decimals:N` | N decimals (0 to 6), kept as written so a row of values lines up           |

`format` and `decimals` are exclusive, and `percent` is refused on a `count` or `nunique` card. Unset, a value keeps fewer decimals as it grows (`3,641`, `12.35`, `0.123`, `0.00032`). The same names apply to [text live values](#text-live-values).

```
- tag: mapped-share
  component_type: card
  workflow_tag: python/samples_workflow
  data_collection_tag: samples
  aggregation: median
  column_name: mapped_fraction
  column_type: float64
  format: percent
```

**Conditional aggregation** — pre-filter data before computing metrics:

```
- tag: high-coverage-count
  component_type: card
  workflow_tag: python/samples_workflow
  data_collection_tag: samples
  aggregation: count
  column_name: sample_id
  column_type: object
  filter_expr: "(col('coverage') >= 30) & (col('quality_score') > 80)"
  icon_name: mdi:filter-check-outline
  icon_color: "#F4511E"
  title: "High-Quality Samples"
```

`filter_expr` accepts a Polars expression string. See [Filter Expressions](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/filter-expressions/index.md) for the full reference.

**Aggregation × column_type compatibility:**

| column_type | Valid aggregations                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `int64`     | `count`, `nunique`, `sum`, `average`, `median`, `min`, `max`, `range`, `variance`, `std_dev`, `percentile`, `q1`, `q3`, `box_plot_stats`, `skewness`, `kurtosis` |
| `float64`   | `count`, `nunique`, `sum`, `average`, `median`, `min`, `max`, `range`, `variance`, `std_dev`, `percentile`, `q1`, `q3`, `box_plot_stats`, `skewness`, `kurtosis` |
| `bool`      | `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max`                                                                                                                                     |
| `datetime`  | `count`, `min`, `max`                                                                                                                                            |
| `timedelta` | `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max`                                                                                                                                     |
| `category`  | `count`, `mode`                                                                                                                                                  |
| `object`    | `count`, `mode`, `nunique`                                                                                                                                       |

column_type is optional

If you omit `column_type`, validation against the compatibility table is skipped offline. When a server is configured (`--server`, or the default server), the column type is inferred from the server schema and used for validation automatically.

**Secondary layout fields** — `secondary_layout` picks how the block under the hero value is drawn, and each layout reads one companion field. The full list of layouts and what they render is in [Components](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/components/#secondary-layout-modes).

| Field                             | Type      | Default    | Read by                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `secondary_layout`                | str       | `vertical` | *(picks the layout)* — one of the 16 modes                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `aggregations`                    | list[str] | `null`     | `vertical`, `compact`, `grid`, `box_plot`                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `breakdown_col`                   | str       | `null`     | `top_n`, `concentration`, `composition`, `donut`                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `top_n_count`                     | int (1–5) | `3`        | `top_n`, `concentration`, `composition`, `donut`                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `coverage_max`                    | float     | `null`     | `coverage`, `gauge`                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `threshold_value` (v1.4.0+)       | float     | `null`     | `threshold` — the QC cut-off; without it the strip is not drawn                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `threshold_direction` (v1.4.0+)   | `min`     | `max`      | `min`                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `threshold_warn` (v1.4.0+)        | float     | `null`     | `threshold` — must lie on the failing side of `threshold_value` (below it for `min`, above it for `max`), and needs `threshold_value`. Since v1.13.0 a warn value on the passing side fails validation instead of being dropped |
| `follow_region_filter` (v1.13.0+) | bool      | `false`    | Any layout — let a genome region brushed on the dashboard narrow the card. See [Which components follow a region](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/interactive-selection-filtering/#region-scope)       |
| `attrition_cols` (v1.4.0+)        | list[str] | `[]`       | `attrition` — ordered stage columns after the card's own, never re-sorted by value                                                                                                                                              |
| `trend_col` (v1.4.0+)             | str       | `null`     | `trend` — the ordered column the sparkline buckets along                                                                                                                                                                        |

```
# Pass/warn/fail against a QC cut-off
- tag: mean-coverage
  component_type: card
  workflow_tag: python/samples_workflow
  data_collection_tag: samples
  aggregation: average
  column_name: coverage
  column_type: float64
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 30
  threshold_warn: 20
  threshold_direction: min
  title: "Mean Coverage"
```

### Interactive Component

```
# MultiSelect — for categorical/text columns
- tag: category-filter
  component_type: interactive
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  interactive_component_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: category

# RangeSlider — for numeric columns
- tag: numeric-filter
  component_type: interactive
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  interactive_component_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: value
  column_type: float64     # optional — enables offline type compatibility check

# DateRangePicker — for datetime columns
- tag: date-filter
  component_type: interactive
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  interactive_component_type: DateRangePicker
  column_name: sample_date
```

**Scoped interactive component** — pre-filter data to restrict available options:

```
# Only show varieties present in rows where petal.length > 4
- tag: long-petal-variety-filter
  component_type: interactive
  workflow_tag: python/iris_workflow
  data_collection_tag: iris_table
  interactive_component_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: variety
  column_type: object
  filter_expr: "col('petal.length') > 4"
  title: "Varieties (petal > 4 cm)"
```

`filter_expr` scopes the component's options/range to the filtered subset. See [Filter Expressions](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/filter-expressions/index.md).

#### Initial values and slider options (v1.13.0+)

| Field                         | Type                                 | Applies to                                                                                          | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default_value`               | value or list                        | `Select`, `MultiSelect` (list allowed), `SegmentedControl`, `Slider` (number), `Checkbox`, `Switch` | The value the filter starts with, and returns to on **Reset all**                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `default_range`               | `[low, high]`                        | `RangeSlider` (numbers), `DateRangePicker` (ISO dates)                                              | The range the filter starts with                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `slider_mode`                 | `gte`, `gt`, `lte`, `lt`, `eq`, `ne` | `Slider`                                                                                            | How the column is compared with the slider's value. `gte` (keep rows at or above it) by default                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `show_histogram`              | bool                                 | `RangeSlider`                                                                                       | Draw the column's distribution above the slider track, on the same scale, so a threshold is placed against the data. Off by default                                                                                                                                             |
| `show_mark_labels` (v1.17.0+) | bool                                 | `Slider`, `RangeSlider`                                                                             | `false` keeps the tick marks but drops their values. Unset, every tick is labelled                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `always_selected` (v1.19.0+)  | bool                                 | `Select`                                                                                            | The filter always holds exactly one value: empty (first load, **Reset all**) or holding a value its list no longer offers, it takes the first enabled option. It cannot be cleared. For pickers that feed tiles showing one unit at a time, such as one structure or one family |
| `default_by` (v1.19.0+)       | numeric column                       | `Select` with `always_selected`                                                                     | Start on the option ranking first on this column, e.g. the family with the most members, instead of the first in the list. The list stays alphabetical, and a pinned data version skips the ranking                                                                             |
| `default_order` (v1.19.0+)    | `desc`, `asc`                        | with `default_by`                                                                                   | `desc` (default) starts on the largest value, `asc` on the smallest                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `banner_facts` (v1.19.1+)     | list                                 | `Select` with `always_selected`                                                                     | Figures shown in the tab's [scope banner](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#scope-banner)                                                                                                                                                    |

A default on the wrong control fails validation: `default_value` on a `RangeSlider`, a list on a `Slider`, or a `default_range` whose low end is above its high end.

```
- tag: min-depth
  component_type: interactive
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  interactive_component_type: Slider
  column_name: depth
  default_value: 10        # rows with depth >= 10 at first load
- tag: qvalue-range
  component_type: interactive
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  interactive_component_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: qvalue
  default_range: [0, 0.05]
  show_histogram: true
- tag: family-picker
  component_type: interactive
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: families
  interactive_component_type: Select
  column_name: family
  always_selected: true
  default_by: n_members    # opens on the largest family
```

A `Slider` is a threshold since v1.13.0

A single-value `Slider` used to keep only the rows equal to its value. It now keeps the rows at or above it. Set `slider_mode: eq` on a slider that should keep the exact match.

**Interactive type × column_type compatibility:**

| column_type | Valid interactive_component_type            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `int64`     | `Slider`, `RangeSlider`                     |
| `float64`   | `Slider`, `RangeSlider`                     |
| `datetime`  | `DateRangePicker`                           |
| `category`  | `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `SegmentedControl` |
| `object`    | `Select`, `MultiSelect`, `SegmentedControl` |
| `bool`      | *(not yet supported)*                       |
| `timedelta` | *(not supported)*                           |

### Table Component

```
- tag: data-table
  component_type: table
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: table_dc
  page_size: 25            # rows per page (default: 100)
  columns: [col1, col2]   # optional: the visible columns, in this order (v1.19.0+; omit to show all)
  compact: false          # optional: tighter row and header heights (default: false)
  title: "Sample Data"    # optional: auto-generated from DC tag if omitted
  description: "Complete measurements across all samples"  # optional subtitle
  title_size: h3          # h1, h2, h3, or sm (default: sm)
  title_align: left       # left (default), center, or right
```

**Title / description** fields are rendered as a header above the AG Grid table. When `title` is omitted, it is auto-generated from `data_collection_tag`.

### Text Component

Headings and prose used to document and organise a dashboard. Text tiles bind to no data source, so `workflow_tag` and `data_collection_tag` are unused.

```
- tag: section-overview
  component_type: text
  title: Within-Sample Diversity
  order: 2                    # heading level H1–H6 (default: 1)
  alignment: left             # horizontal: left (default), center, right
  vertical_alignment: center  # vertical: top, center (default), bottom
  body: |
    Shannon, observed features and Faith's PD measure within-sample
    richness and evenness.
```

| Field                | Type      | Default  | Description                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | --------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `order`              | int (1–6) | `1`      | Heading level, H1 through H6                                                                                                                                        |
| `alignment`          | `left`    | `center` | `right`                                                                                                                                                             |
| `vertical_alignment` | `top`     | `center` | `bottom`                                                                                                                                                            |
| `body`               | str       | `""`     | Optional paragraph below the heading. Block markdown since v1.14.0, see [Components](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/components/#markdown) |
| `values`             | map       | `null`   | Live values the title and body print, see [Live values](#text-live-values)                                                                                          |
| `surface` (v1.14.0+) | `none`    | `card`   | `tinted`                                                                                                                                                            |
| `accent` (v1.14.0+)  | str       | null     | `null`                                                                                                                                                              |

`vertical_alignment` defaults to `center` (v1.4.0+)

Set `vertical_alignment: top` for the pre-v1.4.0 rendering. See [Components](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/components/#text-components) for why the default changed.

#### Live values

A text tile can print values computed from the data. Declare each one under `values`, then cite it as `{{name}}` in the title or the body. `{{param:KEY}}` prints a pipeline parameter of the run, read from the project's [run provenance](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#run-provenance-card), and needs no declaration.

```
- tag: findings
  component_type: text
  values:
    top: {dc: taxonomy_rel_abundance, column: Phylum, aggregation: top, weight: rel_abundance}
    top_share: {dc: taxonomy_rel_abundance, column: Phylum, aggregation: top_share, weight: rel_abundance, format: percent}
    shannon: {dc: alpha_diversity, column: shannon, aggregation: median, format: "decimals:2"}
  body: |
    - **{{top_share}}** of the reads are {{top}}, the most abundant phylum
    - **{{shannon}}** median Shannon diversity
    - Classified against {{param:dada_ref_taxonomy}}
```

| Field         | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dc`          | yes      | `data_collection_tag` the value is computed on                                                                                                                                     |
| `column`      | yes      | Column to aggregate                                                                                                                                                                |
| `aggregation` | yes      | A card aggregation except `box_plot_stats` (`count`, `nunique`, `sum`, `average`, `median`, `min`, `max`, `mode`, …), or `top` / `top_share`                                       |
| `weight`      | no       | `top` and `top_share` only: the column summed per category. Without it, categories are ranked by row count                                                                         |
| `filter_expr` | no       | A [filter expression](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/filter-expressions/index.md) applied before aggregating, as on a card                               |
| `format`      | no       | `percent` (a 0 to 1 fraction, printed as a percentage), `integer`, `si` (`1.2k`, `3.4M`) or `decimals:N`, N from 0 to 6. Unset, a number prints as a card prints it and text as is |

`top` is the category with the largest summed `weight`, and `top_share` its share of the total, as a fraction. Both are for text only: a card refuses them.

How live values behave

- **They follow the filters**, as cards do: the tab's filters, and the filter bar of the section the tile sits in. They are computed with the cards, in the same request.
- **A value that cannot be computed prints a dash** (–). While a value loads, the tile shows a dimmed ellipsis.
- **Names** are lower-case letters, digits and `_`, start with a letter and have at most 12 characters. There is no space inside the braces. Validation fails on a placeholder that names no declared value, and on a value the tile never prints.
- **`{{legend:column}}`** (v1.20.4+) as the value of a list item prints the colour key of a column the dashboard colours with [`category_colors`](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#category-colors), a dot and the value per line. A column without pinned colours prints a dash.
- **Placeholders fill** prose, bold text, link labels, headings, tables and the title. Code spans stay literal.
- **At import**, a list item that cites a value whose data collection is missing or empty in the project is removed, so each item should make sense on its own. A line that is not a list item stays and prints the dash. A tile left with nothing to say is removed.

### Image Component

```
- tag: image-gallery
  component_type: image
  workflow_tag: python/workflow_name
  data_collection_tag: images_dc
  image_column: image_path   # required: column with image paths
  thumbnail_size: 150        # pixels (default: 150)
  columns: 4                 # grid columns (default: 4)
  max_images: 20             # max images shown (default: 20)
```

`s3_base_folder` is optional

If omitted, the image base folder is resolved automatically from the data collection's S3 configuration at runtime.

### MultiQC Component

Embeds a specific plot from a MultiQC quality control report. Both `selected_module` and `selected_plot` are required — they uniquely identify which plot to render.

```
- tag: fastqc-quality
  component_type: multiqc
  workflow_tag: python/nf_workflow
  data_collection_tag: multiqc_report
  selected_module: fastqc
  selected_plot: per_base_sequence_quality
```

Both fields are required

Omitting either `selected_module` or `selected_plot` will fail validation. YAML-defined components must be explicit about which plot to display.

### Map Component

Supports three map types: `scatter_map` (default), `density_map`, and `choropleth_map`.

**Scatter map** — point markers at lat/lon coordinates:

```
- tag: sampling-map
  component_type: map
  workflow_tag: python/my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: sample_metadata
  lat_column: latitude
  lon_column: longitude
  color_column: biome
  size_column: read_count
  hover_columns: [sample_id, site_name]
  map_style: carto-positron
  selection_enabled: true
  selection_column: sample_id
```

**Choropleth map** — colored regions from GeoJSON:

```
- tag: country-choropleth
  component_type: map
  workflow_tag: python/my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: sample_metadata
  map_type: choropleth_map
  locations_column: country_name
  featureidkey: properties.NAME
  color_column: sample_id
  choropleth_aggregation: count
  color_continuous_scale: Viridis
  opacity: 0.6
  # GeoJSON source — pick one:
  geojson_url: "https://example.com/countries.geojson"   # URL
  # geojson_dc_tag: europe_geojson                        # DC tag
```

**Valid `map_type` values:** `scatter_map`, `density_map`, `choropleth_map`

**Valid `map_style` values:** `open-street-map`, `carto-positron`, `carto-darkmatter`

Choropleth requirements

Choropleth maps require `locations_column`, `color_column`, and a GeoJSON source (`geojson_url`, `geojson_dc_tag`, or `geojson_data`). Selection filtering is not supported on choropleth maps.

**Placement** (v1.4.0+) — a map can stay in the grid or be lifted into a dashboard-wide panel that follows the viewer across every tab. See [Components](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/components/#dashboard-wide-map-panel) for what each state looks like.

```
# two extra keys on any map component
placement: floating            # grid (default) or floating
floating_initial_state: docked # compact (default), expanded, docked, hidden
```

| Field                    | Values                                    | Default   | Description                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `placement`              | `grid`, `floating`                        | `grid`    | `floating` claims no grid cell; the map belongs to the whole tab family |
| `floating_initial_state` | `compact`, `expanded`, `docked`, `hidden` | `compact` | The state the panel opens in. Ignored when `placement: grid`            |

State is remembered per viewer

`floating_initial_state` only sets where the panel starts. Once a viewer moves, resizes or folds it, their own choice is remembered for that dashboard family.

## Validation

The CLI validates YAML files in two passes:

| Pass                     | Runs                                                                                                                         | Checks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **1. Schema and domain** | Always; no server needed. A failure stops here.                                                                              | YAML syntax; required fields (`title`, each component's own); `visu_type` is a known chart type; `mode: code` has a `code_content`; `selection_enabled` has a `selection_column`; `aggregation` and `interactive_component_type` suit `column_type`, when it is given; MultiQC has both `selected_module` and `selected_plot`; an image has an `image_column` |
| **2. Server schema**     | With a server; `--offline` skips it. Without `--server`, the default server is tried and what it finds is shown as warnings. | `workflow_tag` and `data_collection_tag` resolve to a collection of the project; `column_name` is one of its columns; when `column_type` is not given, it is read from the collection and `aggregation` or `interactive_component_type` is checked against it                                                                                                 |

Error output is a clean per-component table — each invalid field gets its own row:

```
                     Validation Errors
┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓
┃ Component              ┃ Field           ┃ Message        ┃
┡━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩
│ image-missing-column   │ image_column    │ Field required │
│ multiqc-missing-module │ selected_module │ Field required │
│ multiqc-missing-plot   │ selected_plot   │ Field required │
└────────────────────────┴─────────────────┴────────────────┘
```

## Best Practices

### File Organization

```
project/
├── project.yaml              # Project configuration
├── dashboards/
│   ├── overview.yaml         # Main overview dashboard
│   ├── qc_metrics.yaml       # QC-specific dashboard
│   └── samples.yaml          # Sample analysis dashboard
└── README.md
```

### Component Naming

A component's `tag` is its identity. Since v1.15.0 a component without an `index` gets an id derived from its tag, so importing the same YAML again gives the same ids and each component keeps its [history](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/#component-history). On a child tab the id also depends on the tab's title, so two tabs can reuse a tag. Within one tab, tags must be unique: a YAML that repeats one is refused with *Component tags must be unique within a tab*. A component without a tag gets a new id at each import.

Use descriptive tags that indicate purpose:

```
# Good: Descriptive tags
- tag: box-variety-sepal-length   # Chart type + data
- tag: sepal-length-average       # Metric + aggregation
- tag: variety-filter             # Column + purpose

# Avoid: Generic tags
- tag: figure-1
- tag: card-2
```

### Incremental Validation Workflow

```
# Step 1: check schema and domain constraints (no server needed)
depictio dashboard validate my.yaml --offline

# Step 2: full validation including column names
depictio dashboard validate my.yaml --server ~/.depictio/admin_config.yaml

# Step 3: dry import (schema check only, no write)
depictio dashboard import my.yaml --dry-run

# Step 4: actual import
depictio dashboard import my.yaml --server ~/.depictio/admin_config.yaml

# Step 5: roundtrip check (export back and diff)
depictio dashboard export <id> --server ~/.depictio/admin_config.yaml -o out.yaml
diff my.yaml out.yaml
```

### Version Control

- **Do version control** dashboard YAML files
- **Use meaningful commit messages** describing dashboard changes
- **Review diffs** before merging dashboard changes
- **Tag releases** when deploying to production

# Genome browser (v1.20.0+)

[![](../../images/guides/genome-browser/table_to_browser.webp)](../../images/guides/genome-browser/table_to_browser.mp4)

A row picked in a table: its record card and the genome browser follow (nf-core/riboseq dashboard template).

The `jbrowse` component shows a run's coverage, peaks, variants and alignments in an embedded [JBrowse 2](https://jbrowse.org) view. Dashboard filters pick the tracks and move the browser to a picked row; a click on a feature filters the dashboard back. Nothing else has to run: the track bytes come through the API, in `depictio local up`, Docker Compose and Kubernetes alike.

## GenomeSpy and JBrowse together

nf-core/chipseq, Locus tab: the lanes above are a `genome_view` tile (GenomeSpy), one dot per call on chr14:37.0-39.5 Mb, with the browser's window as a band. The `jbrowse` component below is open on that band.

The lanes show every library's calls along the chromosome; the browser shows the tracks of one region. Each drives the other:

- **Lanes to browser**: brush a region on the lanes and the browser opens on it. The browser does not filter on the region, so every track stays open ([Navigator](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/navigator/index.md)).
- **Browser to lanes**: the browser's window is drawn as a band on every lane.
- **Browser to dashboard**: a click on a feature filters the dashboard on its track's sample, and the lanes keep that sample's calls ([Browser to dashboard](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/browser-to-dashboard/index.md)).
- **Dashboard to browser**: filters pick the tracks, and a picked row moves the browser ([Table to browser](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/table-to-browser/index.md)).

Both can share one colour ramp, so a time course reads the same on the lanes and on the tracks ([Time course](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/time-course/index.md)).

## Examples

Each example opens its own page: the clip, what it shows, and the few lines of YAML behind it.

- **[Table to browser](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/table-to-browser/index.md)**

  A row picked in a table frames the browser on it.

- **[Browser to dashboard](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/browser-to-dashboard/index.md)**

  A click on a feature filters the dashboard on its sample.

- **[Navigator](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/navigator/index.md)**

  Brush a region on GenomeSpy lanes; the browser opens on it.

- **[Time course](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/time-course/index.md)**

  One colour ramp from the earliest library to the latest.

- **[Ranked calls](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/ranked-calls/index.md)**

  A numbered track of the best calls, picked and zoomed.

- **[Sashimi](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/sashimi/index.md)**

  Splice junctions as arcs over RNA coverage.

- **[Breakpoints](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/breakpoints/index.md)**

  Both sides of a call, the breakpoint view and the circular view.

- **[UCSC tracks](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/ucsc-tracks/index.md)**

  Tracks of the UCSC catalogue next to the run's own.

- **[Variant colours](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/variant-colours/index.md)**

  Variants coloured by a category of the dashboard.

- **[Raw JBrowse configuration](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/raw-jbrowse/index.md)**

  Any JBrowse setting or track, merged last.

______________________________________________________________________

## How it works

**Two inputs.** The collection's rows say which tracks open; the files reach the browser through the API.

______________________________________________________________________

## Quick start

A tracks manifest, one row per file, declared as a `genomic_tracks` collection of the project, and a `jbrowse` component on the dashboard:

```
track_id    sample  format  uri
S1.cov      S1      bigwig  coverage/S1.bigWig
S1.reads    S1      bam     bam/S1.sorted.bam
S2.cov      S2      bigwig  coverage/S2.bigWig
```

```
- data_collection_tag: tracks
  config:
    type: genomic_tracks
    metatype: Metadata
    scan: {mode: single, scan_parameters: {filename: tracks.tsv}}
    dc_specific_properties:
      format: TSV
      polars_kwargs: {separator: "\t"}
      sample_column: sample
      assembly: hg38
```

```
- component_type: jbrowse
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: tracks
  title: Genome browser
```

The manifest is found like any table: by the collection's `scan`, in the workflow's data location, next to the run's results. Its relative paths are read from the manifest's own folder (`tracks_base_path` sets another one). In the nf-core dashboard templates, a recipe writes the manifest from the files the run published, so there is no file to write.

______________________________________________________________________

## The `genomic_tracks` collection

| Key                                                                                 | Default               | Meaning                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `uri_column`                                                                        | `uri`                 | A relative path, or an `s3://` or `https://` URI                       |
| `sample_column`                                                                     |                       | The column tracks are filtered and selected on                         |
| `format_column`                                                                     | `format`              | The format, else inferred from the extension                           |
| `index_column`                                                                      | `index_uri`           | The index, else the `.tbi`, `.csi`, `.bai` or `.crai` next to the file |
| `track_id_column`, `name_column`, `color_column`, `category_column`, `order_column` |                       | Track id, label, colour, folder, opening order                         |
| `assembly`                                                                          | `hg38`                | A [built-in assembly](#assemblies) or a custom one                     |
| `tracks_base_path`                                                                  | the manifest's folder | Where relative paths are uploaded from                                 |
| `remote_base_uri`                                                                   |                       | Where relative paths are read in place instead                         |
| `direct_access`                                                                     | `false`               | Let the browser fetch `https://` tracks itself                         |
| `display_defaults`, `presets`                                                       |                       | JBrowse configuration per format, and named fragments for `preset`     |

**Formats:** `bigwig`, `bedgraph`, `bed`, `bigbed`, `narrowpeak`, `broadpeak`, `vcf`, `bam`, `cram`, `gff3`, `gtf`, `hic`, `fasta`. Tabix formats need a `.tbi` or `.csi` index.

### Internal and external tracks

| Track                      | Manifest `uri`                                  | Collection key                       | Read by                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Internal                   | relative path                                   |                                      | the API, from depictio's storage, after an upload at ingestion |
| External, in place         | relative path, or absolute `s3://` / `https://` | `remote_base_uri` for relative paths | the API, from an allow-listed host or bucket                   |
| External, from the browser | `https://`                                      | `direct_access: true`                | the browser (the host must send CORS headers)                  |

Nothing to set: at ingestion each file is uploaded with its index under the collection's `genomic_tracks/<dc_id>/` folder, and removed with the collection or the project.

```
dc_specific_properties:
  remote_base_uri: s3://my-results/run-42/   # or https://data.example.org/run-42/
```

The server reads only what the administrator allows:

```
DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_S3_BUCKETS=my-results
DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_HTTPS_HOSTS=data.example.org
# a private bucket, or one outside AWS
DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_S3_ENDPOINT_URL=https://s3.example.org
DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_S3_ACCESS_KEY=...
DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_REMOTE_S3_SECRET_KEY=...
```

The nf-core templates take the run's results folder as a variable: `depictio run --var TRACKS_URI=s3://<bucket>/<run>/results/`.

```
dc_specific_properties:
  remote_base_uri: https://data.example.org/run-42/
  direct_access: true
```

The host must answer cross-origin range requests, and the instance's Content Security Policy must allow it (by default only depictio itself and UCSC's download server).

### Assemblies

| Assembly   | Organism    | Aliases                     | Gene track  |
| ---------- | ----------- | --------------------------- | ----------- |
| `hg38`     | Human       | `GRCh38`                    | GENCODE     |
| `hg19`     | Human       | `GRCh37`                    | GENCODE     |
| `hs1`      | Human T2T   | `T2T-CHM13v2.0`, `CHM13`    | NCBI RefSeq |
| `mm10`     | Mouse       | `GRCm38`                    | GENCODE     |
| `mm39`     | Mouse       | `GRCm39`                    | NCBI RefSeq |
| `danRer11` | Zebrafish   | `GRCz11`                    | NCBI RefSeq |
| `dm6`      | Fly         | `BDGP6`                     | NCBI RefSeq |
| `ce11`     | Worm        | `WBcel235`                  | NCBI RefSeq |
| `sacCer3`  | Yeast       | `R64`, `R64-1-1`            | NCBI RefSeq |
| `TAIR10`   | Arabidopsis | `araTha1`                   | NCBI RefSeq |
| `wuhCor1`  | SARS-CoV-2  | `MN908947.3`, `NC_045512.2` | NCBI genes  |

These are presets: the sequence, chromosome sizes, chromosome aliases and gene track of each are already wired to UCSC's files, and gene search works on them. The list covers the genomes of the nf-core test datasets; it is not a limit. Any other genome is a custom assembly of three URLs, and UCSC's [GenArk](https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/hubs/) hubs publish them for thousands of assemblies:

```
assembly:
  name: MN908947.3
  aliases: [NC_045512.2]
  twobit_uri: https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/wuhCor1/bigZips/wuhCor1.2bit
  chrom_sizes_uri: https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/wuhCor1/bigZips/wuhCor1.chrom.sizes
  refname_aliases_uri: https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/wuhCor1/bigZips/wuhCor1.chromAlias.txt
```

A custom assembly has no gene search; type a locus instead.

______________________________________________________________________

## The `jbrowse` component

| Key                                                       | What it does                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `track_mode`, `max_tracks`, `initial_tracks`              | Open the filtered tracks (or `all`), and how many                   |
| `initial_categories`, `default_tracks`                    | Open on these track categories, or always show these tracks         |
| `location`                                                | The opening locus, or a gene name                                   |
| `locus_from`                                              | Follow the filtered rows of another collection                      |
| `selection_enabled`, `selection_column`, `selection_mode` | Filter the dashboard from the browser                               |
| `color_by`, `color_scale`, `variant_color_by`             | Colour tracks by a column, along a ramp, or variants by a category  |
| `ucsc_tracks`, `show_annotation`                          | UCSC Genome Browser tracks, the assembly's gene track               |
| `show_junctions`, `read_pairs_display`                    | Sashimi arcs; DNA reads as pileup, arcs or cloud                    |
| `views`                                                   | `breakpoint` and `circular` views                                   |
| `display`, `preset`, `config_overrides`                   | Display defaults, a configuration preset, raw JBrowse configuration |
| `fetch_size_limit_mb`, `force_load`                       | The per-track download limit, lifted or not                         |
| `placement`                                               | `grid`, or `floating` to keep the browser on screen across tabs     |

The component builder has a *Genome browser* type with the same settings.

______________________________________________________________________

## Versions and security

- A [version](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/versioning/index.md) preview or a dataset pin reads the manifest at its pinned commit. The track files are not versioned.
- The browser never receives a storage URL or credentials: tracks come through signed proxy URLs (6 hours), the proxy re-checks read access, and clients name tracks by id, never by URL.
- External files are read only from allow-listed hosts and buckets; `http://` is refused and redirects are not followed.
- `DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_ENABLED=false` turns the browser off. Every `DEPICTIO_JBROWSE_*` variable is in the [environment reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/index.md).

## Limits

- Track data is parsed on the page's main thread: fine for tens of open tracks. A view carries at most 500.
- Large unindexed BED and bedGraph files are refused: `bgzip` and `tabix` them.
- No browser in the nf-core/methylseq template (unindexed bedGraphs) or nf-core/hic (a `.hic` map needs a Hi-C display).

# Breakpoints

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/fusion_chord.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/fusion_chord.mp4)

With a `mate`, the browser shows both sides of a call side by side. The breakpoint view joins them by their split reads and discordant pairs, and the circular view draws every structural variant of the tracks as a chord. In the clip, a chord tile picks the fusions and both breakpoints follow.

```
# on the jbrowse component
read_pairs_display: arcs         # discordant pairs as arcs
views: [breakpoint, circular]
circular_categories: [Structural variants]   # manifest categories the circle draws
locus_from:
  data_collection_tag: fusions
  chrom_column: chrom_a
  start_column: pos_a
  mate: {chrom_column: chrom_b, start_column: pos_b}
```

Used in the [nf-core/rnafusion dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/rnafusion/index.md) and [nf-core/oncoanalyser dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/oncoanalyser/index.md).

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# Browser to dashboard

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/browser_to_dashboard.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/browser_to_dashboard.mp4)

Click a feature in the browser: the dashboard filters on the sample of its track, and the navigator above keeps that sample's calls. With `selection_mode: visible_tracks`, the set of open tracks is the selection instead.

```
# on the jbrowse component
selection_enabled: true
selection_column: sample           # default: the collection's sample_column
```

Used in the [nf-core/viralrecon dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/viralrecon/index.md).

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# Navigator

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/chipseq_peaks.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/chipseq_peaks.mp4)

A `genome_view` tile on the same tab draws the calls of every sample along the whole chromosome, with the browser's window as a band. Zoom on the calls, brush one: the browser opens on it. The browser does not filter on the region, so every track stays open.

```
# a tile on the same tab as the browser
- component_type: advanced_viz
  viz_kind: genome_view
  data_collection_tag: peaks
  config:
    chr_col: chr
    pos_col: start
    end_col: end
    score_col: score
    mark: bar
    open_on_view_window: true      # whole chromosome, the browser's window as a band
    interaction_mode: select       # a drag brushes a region
```

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/atacseq_peaks.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/atacseq_peaks.mp4)

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/cutandrun_peaks.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/cutandrun_peaks.mp4)

Used in the [nf-core/chipseq dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/chipseq/index.md), [nf-core/atacseq dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/atacseq/index.md) and [nf-core/cutandrun dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/cutandrun/index.md).

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# Ranked calls

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/ranked_rows.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/ranked_rows.mp4)

`rank_track` adds a track of the best calls, numbered in `sort_by` order and coloured by a category. Pick one, zoom on it, click it: the panel shows its fields, inheritance and each family member's genotype, and the reads sit under it.

```
# on the jbrowse component
locus_from:
  data_collection_tag: ranked_variants
  chrom_column: chrom
  start_column: pos
  sort_by: rank_score
  label_column: call_label
  rank_track: 20                   # the 20 best calls, numbered
  rank_color_by: model_class
```

The ranked-variant counter and **Prev**/**Next** also work for visitors of a public dashboard.

Used in the nf-core/raredisease dashboard template.

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# Raw JBrowse configuration

`config_overrides` passes JBrowse configuration as it is: per-format displays, per-track settings, extra tracks. An extra track is fetched by the browser itself, so its host must send CORS headers and be allowed by the instance's Content Security Policy.

```
# on the jbrowse component
config_overrides:
  formats:
    bam: {displays: [{type: LinearAlignmentsDisplay, height: 80}]}
  extra_tracks:
    - type: FeatureTrack
      trackId: regions
      name: Regions of interest
      adapter:
        type: BedTabixAdapter
        bedGzLocation: {uri: "https://data.example.org/regions.bed.gz"}
        index: {location: {uri: "https://data.example.org/regions.bed.gz.tbi"}}
```

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# Sashimi

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/sashimi_junctions.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/sashimi_junctions.mp4)

Splice junctions are drawn as arcs over the coverage of RNA alignments. Pick a locus in the landscape and the reads follow; the browser zooms with the other genome tiles.

```
# on the jbrowse component
show_junctions: true
color_by: sample
ucsc_tracks: [mane]
follow_window: true
```

Used in the [nf-core/rnafusion dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/rnafusion/index.md).

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# Table to browser

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/table_to_browser.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/table_to_browser.mp4)

Pick a row in a table: the browser moves to its locus and its record card follows. With no row picked, the browser opens on the best row of the collection (`sort_by`). The toolbar steps through the rows, lists them in a picker, and shows where they fall along the genome. A contig spelled `21` in the table and `chr21` in the assembly (or the reverse) is matched.

```
# on the jbrowse component
locus_from:
  data_collection_tag: orfs        # a table on the same dashboard
  chrom_column: chrom
  start_column: start
  end_column: end
  sort_by: score                   # opens on the best row
# on the table: one picked row at a time
row_selection_mode: single
```

Used in the [nf-core/riboseq dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/riboseq/index.md).

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# Time course

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/genomespy_jbrowse.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/genomespy_jbrowse.mp4)

The tracks and the navigator lanes share one sequential ramp, so a time course reads down the browser, each library on its own scale. Zoomed out, a track shows the mean of each window.

```
# on the jbrowse component
color_scale:
  column: time_point               # a manifest column
  order_by: time_order
  scheme: viridis
display:
  autoscale: localsd
  summary: avg
```

Used in the nf-core/nascent dashboard template.

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# UCSC tracks

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/ucsc_and_tracks.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/ucsc_and_tracks.mp4)

Any bigWig, bigBed or VCF track of the UCSC Genome Browser catalogue for the assembly opens next to the collection's tracks. The builder searches the catalogue by name; each track keeps its own menu, and force load lifts the download limit.

```
# on the jbrowse component
ucsc_tracks: [clinvarMain, dbSnp155Common]
fetch_size_limit_mb: 5
```

[![](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/ucsc_builder.webp)](../../../images/guides/genome-browser/ucsc_builder.mp4)

Used in the [nf-core/viralrecon dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/viralrecon/index.md).

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)

# Variant colours

Variant features take the dashboard's category colours, read from a VCF INFO field (an effect, an impact, a caller), so the browser and the other tiles agree. `variant_label_by` names them by part of an INFO field instead of the VCF ID.

```
# on the jbrowse component
variant_color_by:
  column: coding_effect            # colours from the dashboard's category_colors
  info_field: IMPACT               # the VCF INFO field holding the category
```

Used in the [nf-core/oncoanalyser dashboard template](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/pipeline-templates/nf-core/oncoanalyser/index.md).

[All examples](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/genome-browser/#examples)
# API

# API

The viewer and the CLI both work through Depictio's REST API, under `/depictio/api/v1`. Log in with `POST /auth/login`, then send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

- **API reference**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Every endpoint, generated from the OpenAPI specification.

  [API reference](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/api/reference/index.md)

- **FastAPI docs**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Swagger UI and ReDoc, served live by your own server.

  [FastAPI docs](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/api/fastapi_docs/index.md)

- **Jobs**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Poll the work the server finishes in the background.

  [Jobs](#jobs)

Serving one component to another website? See [Component export](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/component-export/#the-api).

## Jobs (v1.15.0+)

Some requests start work that outlives an HTTP request. They answer with a `job_id`, and the client polls the job until it ends. Paths are under `/depictio/api/v1`. The routes exist only when `DEPICTIO_JOBS_ENABLED` is true; otherwise `/jobs` answers 404. See [Jobs](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/env-reference/#jobs).

| Method and path              | What it does                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /jobs/{job_id}`         | One job: `status`, `step`, `detail`, `progress`, `result` or `error`, timestamps, and `poll_after_seconds`, the suggested wait before the next poll |
| `GET /jobs`                  | Your jobs, newest first. Filters `kind`, `status` and `project_id`; `limit` (1–200, default 50) and `skip`. Admins see everyone's                   |
| `POST /jobs/{job_id}/cancel` | Cancels a job that has not ended, and asks the worker to stop its task                                                                              |

A job is `pending`, `running`, `success`, `failed` or `cancelled`. A job that belongs to someone else answers 404, as a missing one does; admins can read any job. There is no route to create a job: the endpoint that owns the work creates it, and names its `kind`.

| Kind                | Created by                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deltatable.upsert` | `POST /deltatables/upsert` with `async_mode: true`, when [offloading](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/installation/docker/#async-upsert) is on. Without it the response has no `job_id` and the work is done |
| `project.ingest`    | `POST /projects/ingestion/trigger/{project_id}`, the [**Run ingestion**](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/dashboards/#run-ingestion) button                                                          |

The project page uses these routes for its ingestion tab:

| Method and path                                       | What it does                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /projects/ingestion-runs/{project_id}`           | The project's ingestion runs, newest first, with `limit` and `skip`. Paths and host details are removed for viewers who cannot edit the project |
| `GET /projects/ingestion/trigger-status/{project_id}` | Whether **Run ingestion** is offered (`enabled`), usable by the caller (`available`), and the `reason` when it is not                           |
| `POST /projects/ingestion/trigger/{project_id}`       | Starts an ingestion; `overwrite` as a query parameter. Returns `job_id`, `run_id` and `already_running`                                         |

`GET /utils/capabilities` lists `jobs`, `deltatables.async_upsert` and `ingestion.browser_trigger` in its `features` when each is turned on, so a client can check before relying on them.

# API Documentation Integration

This page explains how to integrate the Depictio API documentation with MkDocs using the OpenAPI specification.

## Automated OpenAPI Specification Export

Depictio includes a script to automatically export the OpenAPI specification from a running API instance. This ensures that your documentation always reflects the latest API changes.

### Using the Script

The script is located at `update_openapi.py` in the documentation root directory. To use it:

1. Make sure your Depictio API is running (typically at <http://localhost:8058>)
1. Run the script:

```
# From the depictio-docs directory
python update_openapi.py
```

This will fetch the OpenAPI specification and save it to `docs/api/openapi.json`.

### Script Options

The script supports several command-line options:

```
python update_openapi.py --help
```

- `--api-url`: Base URL of the API (default: <http://localhost:8058>)
- `--output`: Path where the OpenAPI JSON file should be saved (default: docs/api/openapi.json)
- `--indent`: JSON indentation level (default: 2)

### Integration with Documentation Build

You can integrate this script into your documentation build process by adding it to your build scripts or CI/CD pipeline. For example:

```
# Start the API server
docker-compose up -d depictio-backend

# Wait for the API to be ready
sleep 10

# Fetch the OpenAPI specification
python update_openapi.py

# Build the documentation
mkdocs build
```

## Displaying API Documentation in MkDocs

Once you have the OpenAPI specification, you can display it in your MkDocs site using the `swagger-ui-tag` plugin.

### Basic Usage

To display the API documentation on a page, add the following to your Markdown:

```
<swagger-ui url="../../api/openapi.json"/>
```

The path should be relative to the current Markdown file.

### Customization Options

You can customize the Swagger UI display with additional options:

```
<swagger-ui
  url="../../api/openapi.json"
  expand="all"
  theme="dark"
/>
```

Available options include:

- `expand`: Controls the default expansion setting for operations and tags. Values are "list" (default), "full", "none", or "all".
- `theme`: The theme to use. Values are "light" (default) or "dark".
- `try-it-out-enabled`: Whether to show the "Try it out" section. Values are "true" or "false".

## Example: Full API Documentation Page

Here's an example of a complete API documentation page:

```
# API Reference

This page provides interactive documentation for the Depictio API.

## Authentication

To use the API, you need to authenticate using JWT tokens. See the [Authentication](#/components/securitySchemes/bearerAuth) section for details.

## Endpoints

<swagger-ui url="../../api/openapi.json"/>
```

## Fallback for Static Documentation

If you want to provide API documentation even when the OpenAPI specification hasn't been generated (e.g., for GitHub Pages), you can include a simplified static version:

```
<swagger-ui url="../../api/openapi.json" fallback="true"/>
```

With the `fallback` option, if the OpenAPI specification file is not found, a message will be displayed instead of an error.

## Troubleshooting

### OpenAPI Specification Not Found

If you see an error about the OpenAPI specification not being found:

1. Make sure you've run the `update_openapi.py` script
1. Check that the path in the `url` attribute is correct relative to the current Markdown file
1. Verify that the file exists in the expected location

### Swagger UI Not Displaying

If the Swagger UI component is not displaying:

1. Make sure the `swagger-ui-tag` plugin is installed and enabled in your `mkdocs.yml`
1. Check for JavaScript errors in your browser's developer console
1. Try using a different browser

# Templates

# Depictio Templates

Templates are pre-packaged project configurations that set up a complete bioinformatics analysis project, dashboards included, with a single command.

```
depictio ingest /data/my_ampliseq_run \
  --template nf-core/ampliseq/latest
```

______________________________________________________________________

## Available templates

All Certified Reviewed Experimental Draft

No template matches that search.

______________________________________________________________________

## Status levels

Draft

Generated and not yet reviewed. Expect it to need fixes before it is usable.

Experimental

Shared as-is. Feedback and PRs welcome.

Reviewed

Tested, CI passes, reviewed by the Depictio team or community.

Certified

Validated by the **pipeline lead developer**. Highest trust level.

______________________________________________________________________

## How templates work

A template bundles:

- **[Project configuration](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/templates/#template-yaml-structure)**: workflows, data collections and cross-DC links, with [`{VAR_NAME}` placeholders](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/templates/#template-variables)
- **[Recipes](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/recipes/index.md)**: Python transforms that turn raw pipeline outputs into dashboard-ready tables
- **[Dashboard YAML](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/features/yaml-sync/index.md)**: imported on the first run, with the template variables substituted
- **[Cross-DC links](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/templates/#cross-dc-links)**: interactive filtering across data collections
- **[Recipe seeds](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/usage/projects/templates/#recipe-seeds)**: each recipe's output committed as a `.tsv`, so the bundled project can be explored, and re-ingested, without the pipeline run behind it (v1.6.0+)

______________________________________________________________________

## Pipeline version and template version

A template carries two version numbers. They move independently.

- **Pipeline version**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  The pipeline release the template reads, last in its id: `nf-core/rnaseq/3.26.0`.

  *Choose it* with `--template`, or the **Pipeline version** picker on a template's page.

- **Template version**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  The revision of the template itself, such as `2.0.0` to `2.1.0`, for one pipeline release.

  *Find it* beside the picker, in the ingest log, and in the project and dashboard settings.

When the template version moves, what you need to do depends on which number changed:

Major `2.1.0 → 3.0.0`

**The data collections changed.** A collection, a column or a template variable was added, removed or renamed.

Ingest the run again.

Minor `2.0.0 → 2.1.0`

**The dashboards changed.** Figures, tabs or recipes moved; every collection keeps its columns.

Import the dashboards again.

Patch `2.1.0 → 2.1.1`

**Only text changed.** Titles, captions and descriptions.

Nothing to do; import again to get the new wording.

Depictio records the template version a project was ingested with, and the one each dashboard was imported from. The viewer warns when a newer one is available.

______________________________________________________________________

## Contributing a template

Want to add a template for another pipeline? The contributing guide covers the directory layout, recipe requirements, and review process.

[Read the contributing guide](https://depictio.github.io/depictio-docs/latest/developer/contributing-templates/index.md)
